## D422 — THE COUNTERSPELL FAMILY: `This spell can't be countered.` on a spell face, the countered-this-way destination (`If that spell is countered this way, exile it / put it into its owner's hand / on top of its owner's library instead`), and the `{X}` price (`Counter target spell unless its controller pays {X}`) — the face carries the uncounterable line and the counter funnel reads it beside the script property; `counterTo` rides the counter clause and the executor moves the countered card there; a price of `{X}` is the spell's announced X, substituted as the prompt is raised (2026-09-13)

**9,596 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 9,568
(+28: 28 spells whole with no script — Remand, Dissipate, Memory Lapse, Lapse of Certainty, Syncopate,
Logic Knot, Clash of Wills, Force of Negation, No More Lies, Deny Existence, Void Shatter, Liquify,
Faerie Trickery, Spell Shrivel, Excise, Eject, Horribly Awry, Abrupt Decay, Supreme Verdict, Dovin's
Veto, Void Rend, Last Word, Volcanic Fallout, Inescapable Blaze, Long Goodbye, Heated Debate, Tears
of Valakut, Assert Authority).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` **6,133** (no rows — the generator rows no spell);
the REFUSED ledger 1,521 → **1,532** (11 added by reason; THREE `X payment price` rows named STALE by
the guard and deleted). Fixtures 6,798 → **6,803** (6,642 by name + 154 tokens: the five proof spells).
`scriptableToday` 1,620 → **1,630**; the select pool 0 → 11 → 0; the ladder `[1630, 1729, 3091, 4745,
6082]`. Bot reach 9,492 → **9,520** from 291 commanders. An engine seam on Opus 5 by the user's choice
— the stack-interaction slice the spec's §4.8 names, bounded to what the counter already does.

### The measurement chose it — the spell sentences the vocabulary refuses, by shape

The spell leftover (4,319 cards whose leftover is their lines alone; 2,004 with exactly ONE unread
sentence) was measured sentence by sentence: `Until end of turn, target <X> ...` 50 (quoted-ability
grants, mostly — the reorder alone flips 5), `This spell costs {M} less to cast` 29, `As an
additional cost` 20, `Destroy target <X>` 19, `Search your library for up to` 17, `Counter target
spell unless its controller pays` 16, `Prevent all combat damage` 16, `If that spell is countered
this way` 15, `This spell can't be countered` 12 (30 sentences over the lines-only spells), `If this
spell was kicked, that / it / instead` 13 + 10 + 8, `Create a token that's a copy` 14 (Fable's). The
three counter shapes share one seam — the counter effect the engine already runs — and the ledger
held three `X payment price (the parser refuses one: D369)` rows waiting on exactly the third.

### The seam — the face, the destination, the price

- **The face** (`oracle.ts` `OracleFace.cantBeCountered`, `oracleParse.ts`): `This spell can't be
  countered.` printed on an instant or sorcery face (a trailing reminder — Slice from the Shadows'
  note about ward — is the same line); a permanent's line stays its script's
  (`CardScript.cantBeCountered`, D336). `effectParse` drops the line (no clause of the spell, like
  Devoid); `engineComplete` claims it off the flag; the classifier's structural list keeps only the
  OTHER wordings (`can't be countered by spells or abilities`) and reads the plain line as the
  engine's own. The counter funnel (`triggers.ts` `withoutCountersOfTheUncounterable`, now with the
  oracle) and the executor's counter case read the face beside the script property: the counter is
  dropped, the move with it, and a line says so.
- **The destination** (`oracle.ts` `EffectSpec.counterTo` — REQUIRED, null elsewhere; `effectParse.ts`
  `matchCounteredThisWay`): the two-sentence span `<counter sentence>. If that spell is countered
  this way, exile it | put it into its owner's hand | put it on top of / on the bottom of its owner's
  library instead of (putting it) into its owner's / that player's graveyard.` — the first sentence is
  asked of the rules on its own (a plain counter, or a counter-unless-pays whose unpaid branch is the
  counter) and the destination rides the counter clause; a first sentence that is not a counter
  refuses the span. `effects.ts` moves the countered card there (a library placement top or bottom,
  the hand, exile); flashback's exile stands only where the clause names the graveyard.
- **The price** (`effectParse.ts` `readPrice`, `effects.ts` `payOptional`): `{X}` is the spell's
  announced X (`obj.xValue`, CR 601.2b), substituted into the prompt's cost as it is raised — an X
  nobody announced is 0; the D369 refusal pin moved (`payMana.test.ts`).
- `src/engine/counterFamily.test.ts` (4): the parser's three shapes and two refusals; Counterspell
  aimed at Abrupt Decay resolves, counters nothing, says so, and the Decay resolves and kills; Remand
  puts the countered Bears in its owner's hand and draws, Dissipate exiles, Memory Lapse puts it on
  top of its owner's library; Syncopate for X=2 asks the caster for `{2}` — declined, the spell is
  countered into exile with nothing spent; paid, it resolves with the two Forests tapped — the
  replay hash on each.
- **Tier 3** (`tier3.ts`): the Ward note read past a reminder — `(This includes by the ward
  ability.)` names ward without granting it, and two cards the engine now runs completely carried a
  note to pay a cost they never print.
- **Fuzz**: Remand and Dissipate are staples (a counter each, aimed by the driver at whatever is on
  the stack) beside Abrupt Decay, feeding `countersRedirected` (a countered card moved off the stack
  to a hand or a library — exile is flashback's too and is not counted; a floor) and
  `uncounterableSaid` (the funnel's line, no floor — a counter aimed at the Decay is the driver's coin
  flip): **1,619 redirected / 0 uncounterable over the gate's 500 seeds** (210 / 0 at 60).

### The wave — 28 whole, no rows

The selector offered 11 once the family read, every one a spell whose OTHER line the vocabulary does
not read (the generator rows no spell): a colour qualifier on the target (Fry), a three-type sweep
(Obliterate), the amass mechanic (Commence the Endgame), a target's controller as a referent
(Inevitable Defeat), a conditional draw on the destroyed card (Raze to the Ground), a hand reveal
that exiles (Thought Distortion), `artifact or land` (Wreak Havoc), the spell's X in a pump (Slice
from the Shadows), and the CONDITIONAL uncounterables the face does not carry — Banefire's `if X is
5 or more` and Exquisite Firecraft's Spell mastery — beside Martyr of Frost's reveal cost; 11
ledgered by reason. The 28 whole are the spells whose counter shape was the whole of what they
lacked.

### Traps

- **THE INGEST AND THE PARSER MUST AGREE ON THE LINE**: `parseEffects` scrubs a reminder before it
  drops the line, the ingest's regex read the raw text — with the strict regex Slice from the
  Shadows would have been COMPLETE by the parser and COUNTERABLE by the engine (D90's exact
  failure); the ingest admits the trailing parenthetical.
- **`selfRef` RUNS BEFORE THE DROP**: the card's own `This spell` is `~` by the time the line filter
  sees it — the filter reads `(?:This spell|~) can't be countered.`
- **A REMINDER IS NOT A KEYWORD**: the Ward note fired on `(This includes by the ward ability.)`.
- **THE ROW MAKER ROWS NO SPELL**: a spell in the pool is a ledger row by construction — the wave's
  yield is the vocabulary's alone, measured by the leftover diff (28 seam, 0 rowed).

## D423 — THE KICKED INSTEAD: `If this spell was kicked, <clause> instead.` REPLACES the clause before it — `it deals 4 damage instead` (the spell's own damage at the previous target), `that creature gets +5/+5 until end of turn instead` (a referent clause about the previous object), `create four of those tokens instead` (the previous token at a new count); the executor skips the base on a kicked spell and the instead clause on a plain one; the fuzz driver's kick is a coin flip (2026-09-13)

**9,605 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 9,596
(+9: 9 spells whole with no script — Burst Lightning, Roil Eruption, Shivan Fire, Might of Murasa,
Gift of Growth, Colossal Growth, Explosive Growth, Saproling Migration, Conqueror's Pledge).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` **6,133** (no rows — the select pool was 0); the REFUSED ledger **1,532** (unchanged;
the guard named nothing stale). Fixtures 6,803 → **6,807** (6,646 by name + 154 tokens: the four proof
spells). `scriptableToday` **1,630**; the ladder `[1630, 1729, 3091, 4745, 6080]`. Bot reach 9,520 →
**9,529** from 291 commanders. An engine seam on Opus 5 by the user's choice — the kicker's `instead`
half, bounded to the clause shapes the referent rewrite (D392) already reads.

### The measurement chose it — the kicked sentences over the one-unread spells

D422's spell-sentence probe (2,004 spells with exactly ONE unread sentence) put the kicked forms third:
`If this spell was kicked, that / it / instead ...` 13 + 10 + 8 = 31 sentences over some forty shapes.
Read shape by shape: the `instead` forms whose clause is ABOUT the clause before them — `it deals N
damage instead` 3, `that creature gets ±N/±N until end of turn instead` 3 + 4, `create N of those tokens
instead` 3 — are D392's referent rewrite one gate over (the clause is the previous clause's target,
token or phrase, with a new number); the rest carry a target of their own (`instead destroy target
creature` — Bloodchief's Thirst, Waste Management, Blood Beckoning), a referent the vocabulary has no
phrase for (`that player discards three cards instead` — Bog Down, Hypnotic Cloud), a scoped referent
(`those creatures get -2/-2 instead` — Marsh Casualties, Dauntless Unity), a sweep with a qualifier
(Canopy Surge, Breath of Darigaaz), a library search (Primal Growth, Grow from the Ashes), a copy
token (Rite of Replication — Fable's), or a non-instead kicked clause beside an unread first line
(Vines of Vastwood, Savage Offensive). D403 read `If this spell was kicked, <X>.` as X gated on the
kick and pinned the `instead` form as a REFUSAL; the same pin moves.

### The seam — a clause that replaces the one before it

- **The spec** (`oracle.ts` `EffectSpec.kickedInstead` — REQUIRED, `false` elsewhere; always beside
  `ifKicked: true`): the instead clause is a second `EffectSpec` right after the base, carrying the
  base's target index and its own numbers.
- **The parser** (`effectParse.ts` `kickedInsteadRewrite`, in `clausesOf` after the referent
  rewrite): `If this spell was kicked, (instead) <clause> (instead).` is read against the clause
  before it — `create N of those tokens` re-keys the previous `createToken` at N (`TOKEN_WORDS`; a
  previous that is itself kicked refuses), `it deals N damage` re-asks the rules with the previous
  clause's phrase (`~ deals N damage to <phrase>.` — the whole sentence machinery, not a number
  swap), and anything else goes through `referentRewrite` and is refused when it lands a target of
  its own, a payment, or a count. The previous clause's phrase is carried onto the instead clause
  the way a referent's is.
- **The executor** (`effects.ts`, the steps builder): a base whose NEXT clause is `kickedInstead` is
  skipped on a kicked spell with a line — `Burst Lightning was kicked — “Burst Lightning deals 2
  damage to any target.” is replaced.`; on a plain cast the instead clause falls under D403's
  `ifKicked` gate (`was not kicked — … does nothing`). Nothing else moves: the target was aimed once
  at cast, the kick is the object's `kicked` count.
- `src/engine/kickedInstead.test.ts` (3): Burst Lightning at Air Elemental — 2 damage on a plain
  cast with the `was not kicked` line, lethal 4 kicked with the `is replaced` line; Might of Murasa
  +3/+3 plain and +5/+5 kicked, then Gift of Growth kicked on the same Bears (the untap is NOT
  replaced, the +4/+4 stacks to power 11); Saproling Migration two tokens plain, four kicked — the
  replay hash on each. `kicker.test.ts`' D403 pin moved (the instead form is `auto` now,
  `[['damage', 2, false], ['damage', 4, true]]`).
- **Fuzz**: Burst Lightning, Saproling Migration and Gift of Growth are staples feeding
  `kickedReplaced` (the `is replaced` line; reported) and `kickedInsteadSkipped` (the unkicked
  instead's `does nothing` line; the floor): **6 replaced / 106 skipped over the gate's
  500 seeds** (16 skipped at 60). The driver's kick is a COIN FLIP now
  (`chosen.kicker && p.below(2) === 0`): the offer carried `kicker` whenever the face had one and the
  driver always sent `kicked: 1`, so a kicker spell was cast only when the kick was affordable —
  D403's "the next pick may cast it plain" was never true (its counters read 1 / 1 at 60). A
  fuzz-driver change shapes every seed; the gate's other floors held.

### The wave — 9 whole, no rows

The selector offered nothing (the pool 0 — the nine spells' other sentences were already the
vocabulary's, and no permanent waits on a kicked instead); the yield is the leftover diff's alone
(9 seam, 0 rowed, 0 regressed).

### Traps

- **THE PREVIOUS CLAUSE IS THE ANCHOR, NOT THE SENTENCE**: `it deals 4 damage instead` names no
  target — the base's phrase is re-asked with the new number, so a base the rules refused leaves the
  instead clause refused too (both halves read, or neither: D90).
- **A COUNTED TOKEN IS NOT RE-KEYED**: `create N of those tokens` refuses a previous `createToken`
  that is itself kicked; the count is the sentence's word, never a count expression.
- **THE DRIVER ALWAYS KICKED**: a rate canary on a kicked branch reads the DRIVER's coin, not the
  pool — the unkicked branch is the abundant one and carries the floor.
- **A PROOF TARGET MUST SURVIVE THE PLAIN HALF**: a 5/2 died to the unkicked 2 damage and the kicked
  proof had no target — the suite aims at a 4/4.

## D424 — THE CLASSIFIER READS AS THE ROW MAKER READS: the optional trigger (`you may <payload>` on a trigger is the row maker's optional def since D313), the row kinds the vocabulary does not read (the drain, the opponents' life loss, a counter on this permanent or on each creature, the loot, the draw-and-lose, the monarch, the self bounce / sacrifice / untap, the graveyard returns, the regenerations, the mills, the artifact tokens), the attached static's keyword list (the anthem's — fear, infect, wither, flanking, intimidate, a landwalk, a protection), the named self head (`When Ryusei dies, it deals …`) and the activation restriction the engine enforces (`Activate only as a sorcery.`) — mirrored by hand in `primitives.ts`; 49 ledger rows the row maker had outgrown drained; the generator's hand baseline measured after the fire's own put (2026-09-13)

**9,753 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 9,605
(+148: 148 rows — Bontu's Monument, Celestial Ancient, Verduran Enchantress, Mesa Enchantress, Grim
Haruspex, Harvester of Souls, Soul of the Harvest, Garruk's Packleader, Wirewood Savage, Corpse
Traders, Eternal Dragon, Kuldotha Phoenix, Phyresis, Spirit Mantle's kin, the five lucky charms and the
five Talismans, Wooden Sphere's cycle, the three Bringers, Path of Discovery, Seraph of the Masses,
Barricade Breaker, Bloodthirst's Furyborn Hellkite and their kin).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,133 →
**6,281**; the REFUSED ledger 1,529 → **1,664** by the tally (49 stale rows drained, 184 added by
reason — D423's 1,532 was a hand count three over the tally). Fixtures 6,807 → **6,963** (6,800 by
name + 156 tokens). `scriptableToday` 1,630 → 1,914 once the classifier read → **1,766** once the
148 landed; the select pool 0 → 283 → 332 → 0; the ladder `[1766, 1769, 3160, 4779, 6130]` (the
`optional` step is 3 now — the bucket holds what waits on the yes/no AND a head). The bot deck is Emmara, Soul of the
Accord's (GW, reaching 4,098 from 274 two-colour commanders — the five-colour pick cast nothing, below).
A mechanical wave on Opus 5 by the model rule.

### The measurement chose it — the row maker run over every one-piece leftover permanent

The one-piece leftover after D423 was 11,158 cards, 11,158 of them on a LINE; the trigger bodies split
by shape were a long tail (`you may pay {M}. If you do` 57 + 41, `this creature deals N damage to`
48, `put a +N/+N counter on each` 41, `it gets +N/+N until end of` 34, `you may draw a card` 32, `you
may search` 32 … forty shapes under twenty). The seams-between-the-readers method settled it: the
ROW MAKER itself was run over every one-piece leftover permanent (8,590 — `pool424.json` wide, the
lines probe, the vocabulary probe, `make-rows124.cjs -dwide`) and it ROWED 140 the classifier had
never offered — 91 refused by the classifier (`optional` 28, `unclassified` 31, `layer6` 7,
`effect:counter` 6, `effect:sacrifice` 5, `chooseFromZone` 5, `duration` 7), 49 in the ledger under a
reason the row maker had outgrown (`a trigger head outside the row library` 18 — the lucky charms'
`Whenever a player casts a blue spell`, a filtered head the reader takes since D374; `a payload
outside both readers (Pay {1}. If you do, you gain 1 life.)` 9 — the payment sentence the vocabulary
reads whole since D400). Its refusal histogram over the other 8,450 is the map for the decisions after
this one: `trigger payload not a pump` 2,823, `a line that is neither an activated ability nor a
library trigger` 1,559, `effect not a row kind` 1,446, `trigger head not in the library` 699, a
filtered head's adjective 234, `cost` 197, a condition outside the closed vocabulary 178, an
intervening if outside the closed reader 162.

### The mirrors — `rowMakerReads` and three lists, in `primitives.ts`

- **`rowMakerReads(text, cardName)`**, asked of a permanent's line before the `optional` bucket can
  file it: the line `selfRef`'d, its payload peeled (a trigger's after the head, an activated
  ability's after the colon), then (3) an `Activate only …` sentence whose every clause is in the
  closed set the row maker's own limit reader takes (`as a sorcery`, `as an instant`, `once each
  turn`, `during your turn(, before attackers are declared)`, `during your upkeep`, the hand-size
  and graveyard-count forms, `if you control N <predicate>`, the turn record's `TURN_COND`) is stood
  out, or the line stays where it was; (1) a trigger payload's LEADING `you may` (never `you may
  pay`, never a verb price — the vocabulary's own sentence) is stood out; (2) the payload as the
  self subject reads it is asked of `ROW_PAYLOADS` — a mirror of `parseEffect`'s kinds in the row
  maker that the vocabulary does not read — and, when (1) or (3) uncovered it, of `expressible`.
  Under ANY trigger head: the row maker refuses a head outside its library BY NAME, as it always
  has (54 of the 184 ledgered this wave).
- **`ONESHOT_KW = STATIC_KW`** — the one-shot pumps' fourteen keywords become the row maker's `KW`
  (every Tier-2 keyword the engine enforces with no number); **`AURA_KWS = STATIC_KWS`** — the
  attached static's grant list is the anthem's (the keywords, a landwalk, a protection quality; the
  row maker's `grantBody` reads one list for both) — `Enchanted creature has infect` (Phyresis),
  `has mountainwalk` (Burrowing), `has protection from black and from red` (Mask of Law and Grace)
  are rows.
- **`SELF_SUBJECT_HEAD`** admits `~` beside the `this <type>` forms: a NAMED head (`When Ryusei dies,
  it deals 5 damage to each creature without flying.`) is the same subject once `selfRef` has spelled
  the name.
- The three example pins moved (`you may draw a card` under a dies head, `you may return target
  creature card from your graveyard to your hand`, `you may put a quest counter on this enchantment` —
  `scriptable`, the row maker's since D313/D303), `optional` 77 → 0 in the sole-need table.
- **The drain**: the 49 ledger rows the wide run named (`drain-stale424.cjs`, by plain string — a
  regex in a heredoc halves its backslashes, invariant 14) deleted so the selector offers them; 41
  landed, 8 re-ledgered by the port's own reasons.

### The generator — the hand baseline after the fire's put

Six draw suites under FILTERED heads failed by one (Garruk's Packleader, Grim Haruspex, Harvester of
Souls, Soul of the Harvest, Wirewood Savage, Paleoloth): the harness's `put` finds a named card in
the LIBRARY first and in the HAND second, and the opening seven had dealt the head's fixture (Blade
of the Sixth Pride) to the hand — the put took it out, the draw put one back, `hand0 + 1` read
`hand0`. `castsFromHand` had been guessing this per head (`artifactEnters`, `constellation`,
`selfOrAnotherCreatureEnters`, `creatureYouControlDies` carried a `- 1` for exactly this reason, right
under the seed and wrong under another deck). The arm re-measures the hand right after a fire whose
FIRST statement puts a fixture for p1 (`remeasureHand`, `hasLeadingPut` — the trigger has not
resolved yet), `hand0` is `let` on those suites, and the four put-based heads are out of
`castsFromHand` (21 suites this wave carry the re-measure; the six pass). The attached static's
suite asserts the landwalk and the protection it grants (`lw` / `prot` on the host, the anthem's
asserts one subject over — the helpers were emitted and never read, and tsc named nine suites).

### The wave — 148 rows, 8 unported, 184 ledgered

332 offered (283 the mirrors admitted + the 49 drained); 156 rows, 8 refused by their suites and
unported by name — an untap under the any-creature-enters head beside a sacrifice-cost ping whose
game ends before the fire (Blasting Station), a scry under the cycle-or-discard head whose cycling
draw moves the library count (Curator of Mysteries), an opponent-cast head with a timing rider the
arm cannot stage (Eyes of the Wisent), a payment beside an another-target line (Gravity Negator),
and a protection quality the derive does not read — `from multicolored` (Guildscorn Ward), `from
creatures` (Holy Mantle, Spirit Mantle, Unquestioned Authority); 148 landed (attachedStatic 16,
vocab 61 + 18 optional, draw 4 + 15 optional, drain 7, token 8 optional, massCounter 3, selfCounter
3 + 5 optional, gainLife 5, loseLifeOpponents 4, sacrificeSelf 4, loot 4, untapSelf 4 optional, the
graveyard returns 3, drawLose 2, damageTarget 2, tapTarget 2, threshold 2, anthem 2, damageOpponents,
mill, pumpTarget, self, bounceSelf, drawN); 184 ledgered by reason.

### The bot deck — at most two colours

The close-out's battery failed twice on `the bots cast spells unaided — 0 cast lines`: the regenerated
deck (Go-Shintai of Life's Origin, five colours, chosen for reaching 9,677 cards) swapped two cards and
the solo game's FIXED seed drew seventeen turns in which three bots cast nothing. Reproduced against
the real database (four bots, the runner, five seeds): the five-colour deck cast one to nine spells a
game between four seats — cheap spells of every colour over basics split five ways — and the two swapped
cards changed nothing (the old list cast the same). `buildBotDeck` picks the commander among those
with AT MOST TWO COLOURS now (reach still decides among them): Emmara, Soul of the Accord (GW) reaching
4,098 cards; the same seeds cast seven to eleven a game, every seat casting in four of five, and the
battery reads 6 cast lines. The gate was rerun on the final tree.

### Traps

- **THE CLASSIFIER IS A HAND MIRROR, AND IT DRIFTS**: every reader the row maker gained since D313
  (the optional trigger), D371 (the row kinds, the `KW` list) and D374 (the filtered heads) was
  invisible to the classifier until the row maker itself was run over the leftover. The wide run is
  the measurement that finds the drift; run it before choosing.
- **A STALE LEDGER ROW IS INVISIBLE TO THE GUARD** until a SEAM completes the card: a row the row
  maker has merely outgrown stays; the wide run names those too.
- **A REGEX IN A HEREDOC HALVES ITS BACKSLASHES** (invariant 14, again): `drain-stale424.cjs`'s first
  draft died on `\[`; the second finds each row as a plain string.
- **THE HARNESS PUT MAY TAKE FROM THE HAND**: a hand-count assert measured before a fixture's put is
  wrong whenever the opening seven dealt the fixture; measure after the put, never guess per head.
- **A FIVE-COLOUR BOT DECK CASTS NOTHING**: the widest reach picked five colours the moment the pool held a
  five-colour commander, and the battery's fixed seed found the game with no casts; the commander is at most
  two colours now, and the deck is measured by casts, not by reach.
- **A GRANT LIST THE DERIVE DOES NOT READ**: `protection from multicolored` / `from creatures`
  pass the row maker's `PROT` and land no protection; the suite's new assert caught all four.

passed / 11 skipped · 500-seed gate, 6 shards, 969.2 s wall · build clean · probe
124/124 · battery 140/140.**

## D425 — THE SACRIFICED SELF, THE `you` SCOPE AND THE OPPONENT-OR-PLANESWALKER NOUN: `Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target.` (the `It` is the object the cost put in the graveyard — CR 608.2h), `~ deals N damage to you.` (a player scope on the controller alone) and `target opponent or planeswalker` (the target parser's kinds since D293) — three wordings the executor already had the machinery for that the sentence reader refused (2026-09-13)

spells whole with no script: Inferno Jet, Aftershock, Bedeck // Bedazzle, Jeskai Charm).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,281 → **6,342** (63 rows in, two D187 spell defs OUT — Burning Fields and Kiss of Death read whole now, and a spell def exists only where the vocabulary cannot: their suppression pins named them and `retire-425b.cjs` retired them); the REFUSED ledger 1,664 → **1,683** (two spell rows the guard
named STALE — Inferno Jet, Aftershock — deleted; 21 added by reason). Fixtures 6,963 → **7,026** (6,863

### The measurement chose it — the wide run's refusal histogram, read by shape

D424's wide run left the map (`make-rows-wide.log`): `effect not a row kind` 1,446 activated effects,
of which `It deals N damage to <target>` 48 — every one under a cost that SACRIFICES the permanent
(Mogg Fanatic's `Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target.`), the row maker's activated
branch spelling `This creature` as `~` but never `It`; `trigger payload not a pump` 2,823, of which `~
deals N damage to you.` 8 (+ 7 as `it`, 17 one-piece cards and 61 carrying the sentence — Serendib
Efreet, City of Brass, Lord of the Pit); `~ deals N damage to target opponent or planeswalker.` 3 + 4
activated (31 cards carry the noun, 20 with nothing else unread). Three readers one word short of a
mechanism the engine had: `damageTo` derives the source where it lies (a fixed number from the
graveyard is the printed number), `scopeMembers` walks player scopes, `targetParse` reads `opponent or
planeswalker` as player + planeswalker with the opponent controller.

### The seam

- **`effectParse.ts`**: `you` in `SCOPE` and `readScope` (`{ kind: 'player', controller: 'you' }`) — a
  verb that refuses player scopes (destroy, exile, bounce) refuses it as it refuses `each player`;
  `opponent or planeswalker` in `NOUNS` above `opponent`. **`effects.ts`** `scopeMembers`: the `you`
  player scope is the controller alone.
- **`primitives.ts`** `selfSubject`: under an activated cost that sacrifices the permanent itself
  (`SELF_SACRIFICE_COST`), a leading `it deals` is `~ deals`. **The row maker** (`make-rows125.cjs`,
  the activated branch): the same rewrite when the parsed cost `sacrificesSelf`; **`gen125-vocab.cjs`**:
  the `damageEach` assert charges the controller's own life for the `you` scope.
- `src/engine/scopedBoard.test.ts` (+1): Ashes to Ashes exiles two of the opponent's creatures and its
  second sentence costs the CASTER 5 and the opponent nothing; the replay hash.
  `src/data/twoPassEffects.test.ts` (+4): the parse pins (the scope, the noun, Char's compound `and 2
  damage to you` stays unread, `Destroy you.` stays unread).

### The wave — 63 rows, 6 unported, 21 ledgered

84 offered; 69 rows, 6 refused by their suites and unported by name — `Sacrifice this creature: It
deals damage equal to ITS POWER to target creature` (Cinder Shade, Flame Elemental, Ghitu Fire-Eater,
Heartfire Immolator, Minotaur Illusionist, Skarrgan Skybreaker): the sacrificed source's power is last
known information the executor reads as 0 from the graveyard — D421's dead-source gap, one shape over,
and the fixed-number form lands while the power form waits; 63 landed (damageTarget 39, vocab 33, draw
3, returnSelfToHand, self); 15 refused by reason (a combat-role clause the suite has no fixture for 6, a
payment branch the suite cannot assert — `damageEach` under `unless you pay` 3: Force of Nature, Hasran
Ogress, Minion of Tevesh Szat; a filtered head's adjective 2).

### Traps

- **THE SACRIFICED SELF IS `It`**: the vocabulary and the row maker spell `This creature` as `~`
  everywhere and `it` only under a self head; an activated line whose cost eats the permanent names the
  effect's subject `It`, and 49 lines waited on one rewrite.
- **A FIXED NUMBER FROM THE GRAVEYARD IS RIGHT, A POWER IS NOT**: `damageTo` derives the sacrificed
  card where it lies — the printed number, the printed keywords — so `It deals 1 damage` is CR 608.2h's
  answer, and `damage equal to its power` is not (the counters and pumps died with it): six suites
  refused the power form and the classifier keeps reading it (the port ledgers it by name).
- **A SCOPE WORD IS A SCOPE EVERYWHERE**: `you` in `SCOPE` reaches every scoped verb; the player-refusing
  verbs refuse it the way they refuse `each player`, and the pin says so.
- **A FAILED GATE KEEPS RUNNING**: `verify.cjs --full` runs every gate to the end after a red one (the six
  fuzz shards start after a failed unit suite), so a rerun launched on `gates FAILED` overlaps the first
  run's shards and its own unit suite times out for the load (`net.test.ts`, the tournament) — wait for
  the first verify PROCESS to exit before launching again; the first run's only red was the two D187
  suppression pins the noun outgrew (Burning Fields, Kiss of Death — retired), the second's the overlap,
  the third clean.

Y. when each half reads whole on its own — `Target opponent loses 2 life and you gain 2 life.`, `You gain 2 life and draw a card.`, `Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature and untap it.`, `Draw a card, then discard a card.`; the caster's own discard (`Discard a card.`) as the each-player queue over the `you` scope; nineteen D187 spell defs the vocabulary outgrew retired (2026-09-13)

### The measurement chose it — the leftover's unread sentences that split into two the vocabulary reads

D424's wide run had left a long tail of trigger bodies (forty shapes under sixty). The sentence-level probe
(`and-probe425.txt` in d425/) asked a different question of every unread sentence over every leftover line
— a trigger's body, an activated effect, a spell's sentence: does it split at an ` and ` into two sentences
the vocabulary reads whole? 40,821 unread sentences, 235 split so, **188 cards with nothing else unread**; the
shapes: `Target opponent loses N life and you gain N life` 33, `You gain N life and draw a card` 31, `You
draw a card and you lose N life` 25, `Target player loses N life and you gain N life` 21, `~ deals N damage
to <target> and you gain N life` 11, `Put a +1/+1 counter on <X> and draw a card` 11 — the drains, the
cantrips, the helices: every one two rules the vocabulary already had, one word apart.

### The seam — `conjunctionSplit` in `clausesOf`

- **`effectParse.ts`** `conjunctionSplit(sentence, previous)`, tried in `clausesOf` only after no rule read
  the whole sentence, the referent rewrite and the kicked instead: at each ` and ` (then each `, then `) from
  the left, the left part with a period and the right part capitalised must EACH read as one clause — a rule
  each, or the right a referent of the left (`Tap target creature and it doesn't untap during its
  controller's next untap step.` — the freeze aims where the tap did) or of the clause before; a half that
  is a payment or a delay refuses; a right half led by `you may` / `if` / `when` / `unless` refuses. Each
  half keeps its own text and phrase; `parseEffects` numbers the targets clause by clause, so `Destroy
  target permanent and return target nonlegendary creature card …` (Ragnarok) takes 0 and 1 in printed order.
  A half that reads as nothing (`Destroy target creature and target land.` — `Target land.`) leaves the
  sentence unread, as before; an asking left half (`Sacrifice a creature and draw a card.`) still lands
  `assisted` by D195's rule — the split changes nothing about what a clause may be.
- **The caster's own discard**: `Discard a card.` / `You discard two cards.` — the each-player queue (D390)
  over the `you` scope (D425), one player, the ask last as ever: the loot's second half (`Draw a card, then
  discard a card.`), Careful Study, Faithless Looting, Emmessi Tome.
- **The generator** (`gen126-vocab.cjs`): the queued-discard assert asks p1 and refuses p2 for the `you` scope
  (`queueAsksP1` / `queueAsksP2`).
- `src/data/twoPassEffects.test.ts` (+7): the drain, the gain-and-draw, the counter-and-draw, the loot, the
  tap-and-freeze referent, two targets across the halves, the noun half refused, the asking left half
  assisted. `src/engine/scopedBoard.test.ts` (+3): Lightning Helix kills the Cyclops and gains three, Ambition's
  Cost draws three and loses three, Certain Death destroys the Bears then its controller loses two and the
  caster gains two — the replay hash. `counterEffects.test.ts`: Burst of Strength's pin REVERSED (D117 — the
  sentence the closed vocabulary refused for eleven decisions is exactly what the conjunction reads: the
  counter on the target and the untap of the same target).

### The wave — 82 rows, 1 unported, 53 ledgered; 45 spells whole; 19 defs retired

135 offered (127 the seam admitted + the 8 stale rows drained); 84 rows, the generator refusing two by
name (Nihilistic Glee — a hand-size condition beside a hand fixture; Cyclopean Snare — a tap cost beside a
vocabulary self bounce the suite reads after the return); 82 landed (vocab 87 abilities, token 3, scry 2,
attachedStatic, mass); 53 refused by reason (a filtered head's adjective 11, a payload outside both readers
11, a head outside the library 9, a queued discard the scaffold hand may not hold 4, a static line 4). The
suppression pins over the 551 shipped spell defs were run against the new reader before the gate: 18 went
red (`It deals N damage to <target> and you gain N life` — Lightning Helix, Warleader's Helix, Void Helix,
Douse in Gloom, Essence Drain, Essence Extraction, Agonizing Syphon, Defibrillating Current, Vicious Hunger,
Vampiric Feast, Vampiric Touch, Taste of Blood, Last Caress, Last Kiss; `You draw N cards and you lose N life`
— Ambition's Cost, Ancient Craving; Certain Death; Confront the Unknown) and were retired; Sovereign's Bite's
kin keep their reversed pins (D383 — a redundant def outranks the vocabulary and is a retirement of its own).

### The stale life — a bug the conjunction exposed

Two suites the gate named registered ONE script and cast a spell whose def was not there (Student of
Ojutai's Succumb to Temptation, Rewards of Diversity's Lightning Helix): the spells had run as NOTHING —
the vocabulary could not read them — and the suites had pinned that silence. With the conjunction they
run, and Rewards' self-aimed Helix read **43**: three damage and then three life in ONE batch, and
`state` is the snapshot before the batch (D295), so the gain's `LifeChanged` carried `to: 43` from the
life before the damage and the reducer WROTE it — the damage was lost. Latent since M6.3: any resolution
with two life events for one player (a self-aimed helix, a drain at yourself, a two-sentence burn and
gain) did this. `reducer.ts` applies the DELTA now (every emitter's `to` is life ± delta, so a lone event
lands where it always did); `effects.ts` keeps a per-resolution LIFE LEDGER (`lifeChanged`, `dealt` —
the damage this batch dealt to players included) so the log's `to` is right as well.
`scopedBoard.test.ts` (+1): Lightning Helix at yourself — the life unchanged, the one `LifeChanged` in the
log reading `[3, 40]`, the replay hash. Student of Ojutai's pin rewritten (Succumb's −2 meets Student's
+2 at 40), Rewards of Diversity's passes as written (the self-burn nets nothing, now truly).

### Traps

- **A SUPPRESSION PIN IS A GATE'S RED, NOT A BATTERY'S**: run the 551 `the suppression predicate holds` suites
  against a widened reader BEFORE the gate (four batches — the command line is too long for one) and retire
  what they name; D425 found two in its gate, D426 eighteen before it.
- **A HALF THAT READS AS NOTHING REFUSES THE WHOLE**: the split is the closed vocabulary twice, not a wider
  vocabulary — `Target land.` reads as nothing, so `Destroy target creature and target land.` stays unread.
- **A SUITE THAT PINS A SPELL'S SILENCE**: two suites registered one script and cast a second card the
  vocabulary could not read, pinning the nothing it did; a wider reader makes the card run and the pin is
  rewritten, not adapted (D117) - and one of them found the stale life.
- **THE STALE LIFE**: two life events for one player in one batch overwrote each other for as long as the
  reducer wrote `to`; apply the delta, and keep a ledger for the log.
- **THE `you` SCOPE CHANGES WHO THE SUITE ASKS**: the queued-discard assert read `p2 discarded` for every
  player scope; four `Discard a card.` rows failed until the assert asked p1 alone.

## D427 — THE SHIELD'S SOURCE AND RECIPIENT SCOPES: `Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt this turn by attacking creatures.`, `... by creatures with power 4 or less.`, `... by creatures target opponent controls.`, `... by target creature this turn.`, `Prevent all damage that would be dealt to creatures this turn.`, `... to you and creatures you control this turn.`, `... to and dealt by that creature this turn.` — the prevention shield (D382) takes a SOURCE filter and a recipient SET; the funnel reads both off the derived board (2026-09-14)

**9,975 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 9,947
(+28: 28 spells whole with no script — Harmless Assault, Vine Snare, Fog of War, Hunter's Ambush,
Galadhrim Ambush, Tanglesap, Hindervines, Forfend, Blinding Fog, Divine Light, Safe Passage, Eerie
Interference, Endure, Thwart the Enemy, Ethereal Haze, Fend Off, Warning, Restrain, Azorius Ploy, Snag,
Terrifying Presence, Repel the Abominable, Djeru's Resolve, Leap of Faith, Lithomancer's Focus, Foxfire,
Energy Arc, Fleeting Flight).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` **6,406** (no rows — the pool's fifteen permanents were
every one a shield the suite cannot prove); the REFUSED ledger 1,728 → **1,743** (15 added by reason).
Fixtures 7,107 → **7,114** (6,951 by name + 156 tokens: the seven proof spells). `scriptableToday` 1,828 →
**1,843**; the select pool 0 → 15 → 0; the ladder `[1843, 1848, 3248, 4844, 6170]`. Bot reach 4,133 →
**4,159** from 281. An engine seam on Opus 5 by the user's choice — the prevention slice of the spec's §4.6,
bounded to what the funnel already spends.

### The measurement chose it — the spell sentences after the conjunction

The spell-sentence probe rerun after D426 (`spellsent-probe427.txt`, 1,954 one-unread spells): `Prevent
all combat damage that would` 16 + `Prevent all damage that would be` 13 — 36 spells whose one unread
sentence was a shield with a SOURCE (`by attacking creatures`, `by creatures with power N or less`, `by
nongreen creatures`, `by target creature`, `by creatures target opponent controls`, `by creatures other
than target creature`) or a recipient SET (`to creatures`, `to creatures you control`, `to you and
creatures you control`, `to and dealt by that creature`) over a shield that named a recipient and never a
source (D382: `any` / `players` / `you` / one aim). The other families measured smaller still: the cost
reductions with a count or a condition 34 (a target-dependent half), the additional costs 20 (random
discards, either/or prices), the `Until end of turn, ...` heads 105 (quoted-ability grants, mostly).

### The seam — one shield, two scopes

- **`state.ts`** `PreventionShield.source?` (`ShieldSource`: one card, or a `creatures` / `sources` filter — a
  controller resolved to players when the shield is built, `attacking`, `unblocked`, `powerAtMost`,
  `notColor`, `colorless`, `notSubtype`, `withoutKeyword`, `noPlusCounter`, one card `except`ed) and two
  recipient kinds (`creatures` with a controller, `playerAndTheirs` with `creatures` / `permanents`);
  optional, so every earlier shield replays byte for byte.
- **`effectParse.ts`** `SHIELD_SRC` / `SHIELD_RECIP` (closed lists), `readShieldSource` /
  `readShieldRecipient`, four sentence rules (`dealt this turn by <SRC>` / `dealt by <SRC> this turn`,
  `dealt to <RECIP> this turn( by <SRC>)`, `<SRC> would deal this turn`, `to and dealt by <TARGET>`), a
  target as the source (`{ kind: 'target' }`), a target player whose creatures (`targetPlayer`), one target
  excepted; `REFERENT_SHIELD` admits `to it` / `to and dealt by that creature` mid-sentence to the referent
  rewrite. A form outside the lists — a colour of your choice, two colours, `except combat damage by
  enchanted creatures` — refuses the sentence (D90); a target recipient beside a target source refuses too.
- **`effects.ts`** (the `prevent` case): the source and the recipient the spec names, the aim taken by the
  one that needs it (`you` → the caster, `your opponents` → `notPlayer`, `target opponent` → that player).
- **`prevention.ts`** `sourceAdmits` / `covers(shield, entry, isCombat, board)`: the derived source (a
  creature? its controller, the attack and the block off `state.combat`, the power, the colours, the
  subtypes, the keywords, the +1/+1 counter) and the derived recipient (a creature? whose?) — the same cache
  the statics use.
- `src/engine/prevention.test.ts` (+6): Harmless Assault (the attackers deal nothing, a Bolt lands), Vine
  Snare (the 2/2 is stopped, the 5/2 is not), Hunter's Ambush (the red Cyclops is stopped, the green Bears
  is not), Fend Off (the targeted Bears deals nothing, the Cyclops five), Forfend (a Bolt at a creature is
  stopped, at a player lands), Safe Passage (you and yours covered, the opponent not) — the replay hash.
  `src/data/twoPassEffects.test.ts` (+4): the filters, the target forms, the recipient sets and the referent,
  the refusals.
- **Fuzz**: Harmless Assault and Forfend are staples (no target, cast wherever held), feeding
  `scopedShields` (the floor) and `scopedPrevented` (reported — the driver rarely attacks): **88
  scoped / 14 stopped over the gate's 500 seeds** (14 scoped at 60).

### The wave — 28 whole, no rows

The selector offered 15 permanents (Kor Haven, Maze of Ith, Songstitcher, Lady Evangela, Cephalid
Illusionist ...) — every one a COMBAT shield the row's suite cannot prove without an attack it does not
declare (`it must attack`, D398's refusal; the combat-only both-ways form joins it — the suite's ping is not
combat damage and the shield lets it through, rightly); 15 ledgered by reason, 0 rows. The 551 suppression
pins were run before the gate (D426's rule): none red.

### Traps

- **A COMBAT-ONLY SHIELD IS PROVEN ONLY BY AN ATTACK**: the generator's ping is not combat damage; a
  combat-only shield with a source or a set — or the both-ways form — is refused by name like the Fog
  shape, or its suite asserts a prevention that rightly did not happen (two rows failed before the refusal
  was written).
- **THE CONTROLLER IS RESOLVED WHEN THE SHIELD IS BUILT**: `you` and `your opponents` are the caster and
  everyone else at build time (`{ player }` / `{ notPlayer }`), never read off the shield later — a shield is
  state and must say who it means.
- **A REFERENT MID-SENTENCE NEEDS ITS OWN ADMISSION**: the referent rewrite reads a sentence that STARTS with
  the referent or with a verb that takes it; `to it this turn` inside a shield sentence needed
  `REFERENT_SHIELD` to be tried at all.

## D428 — THE TRIGGERING PLAYER: `Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, that player discards a card.`, `At the beginning of each player's upkeep, that player loses 1 life.`, `Whenever a player casts a spell, that player discards a card.`, `Whenever a creature dies, that creature's controller loses 1 life.` — a trigger head whose event names ONE player carries that player onto the stack, and the payload's `that player` is its `target player` clause aimed there without asking (2026-09-14)

**9,994 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 9,975
(+19: 19 rows under the library heads — Abyssal Specter, Blazing Specter, Copper Tablet, Dingus Staff,
Furnace Scamp, Headhunter, Necrogen Mists, Odylic Wraith, Oppression, Order of Yawgmoth, Orzhov Racketeers,
Riptide Pilferer, Silent Specter, Soul Bleed, Spellshock, Wei Night Raiders, Chilling Apparition, Lightning
Skelemental, Specter's Shroud).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,406 → **6,425**; the REFUSED ledger 1,743 → **1,747**
(4 added by reason: three referent discards AT RANDOM — the vocabulary refuses randomness under a def, the
standing rule — and Stab Wound's attached pump that kills the 2/2 Bears). Fixtures 7,114 → **7,133** (6,970 by
name + 156 tokens). `scriptableToday` 1,843 → **1,846**; the select pool 0 → 23 → 0; the ladder `[1846, 1852,
3254, 4850, 6176]`. Bot reach 4,159 → **4,162** from 281. An engine seam on Opus 5 by the user's choice — the
smallest cut through the family the wide run and the spell probe both named (`this creature deals N damage to
that player` 32 in D424's map; `that player` as the left half's player in D426's residue).

### The measurement chose it — the referent under a library head

The one-piece leftover permanents whose payload names `that player` (or `its controller`, `that creature's
controller`, `that spell's controller`) under a head the library already fires: **300** (`probe-player428`),
by head `combatDamagePlayer` 75, `eachUpkeep` 49, `eachOpponentUpkeep` 14, `dealsDamagePlayer` 13,
`aPlayerCastsSpell` 11, `enchantedControllerUpkeep` 8, `combatDamageCreature` 7, `opponentCastsSpell` 5,
`aCreatureDies` 4, `dealsDamageOpponent` 4, `anyCreatureEnters` 3 (the `etb` 49 and `upkeep` 14 name a player
INSIDE the payload — `target player reveals ... that player ...` — and are D392's referent, not this one). The
bodies: `that player discards a card` 11 (+4 at random), `~ deals N damage to that player`, `that player loses
N life`, `that player mills N`, `that player sacrifices a creature`, `that player gets a poison counter`, and a
long tail the vocabulary does not read yet (`that player reveals the top card`, `that player exiles cards from
the top`, `that player chooses target player who ...`). The classifier's offer once the mirror read the
rewrite: 23 permanents; the row maker rowed 19.

### The seam — one field, read once at the bus

- **`api.ts`** `TriggerDef.playerOf?(ctx, self, ev, item) → PlayerId | null`: the player the head names,
  read off the EVENT (the damaged player, the active player, the caster, the dying or entering creature's
  controller, the damaged creature's controller) — never off the board later. A `null` answer fires nothing:
  the head named nobody. **`state.ts`** `PendingTrigger.player?` and `StackObject.player?` (optional, so
  every earlier trigger replays byte for byte); **`triggers.ts`** asks it at both fan-out sites (the printed
  defs and the granted ones), per item under `perItem`; **`loop.ts`** carries it onto the stack object.
- **The generator** (`playerHeads128.cjs`): the eighteen heads whose event names one player, each with its
  `playerOf` (mirroring the head's matcher — a damage head reads BOTH damage events, since its `Any` twin fires
  on noncombat damage), the referent words it admits (`that player` under the player heads, the creature's
  controller under the dies / enters / damage-to-creature heads, the spell's controller under the cast heads),
  a `perItem` for the heads whose batched event names a player per item (a wrath kills creatures of several
  players — one firing each, CR 603.2c), and the player the suite's fire makes it. The row maker rewrites the
  referent to `target player` and reads the payload by the VOCABULARY ALONE (a row kind would ask for the
  player); the def asks no target (`targets` absent) and its `resolve` aims the one pick at `obj.player`
  through `ctx.vocabulary` — `withStillLegalPicks` keeps a player who has not lost (CR 800.4a), which is
  exactly the referent's rule. The suite's fixture for the clause is the player the head's fire names (p2 under
  the damage and opponent heads, p1 under the caster's own cast, the end step, the entering Bears); a payload
  that ASKS (a discard) stops the fire at the prompt as D398's asking payloads do; p2's life under a
  combat-to-player head is read net of the fire's own combat damage (`p2LifeAdjOf`).
- **The classifier** (`primitives.ts` `ROW_PLAYER_HEADS` / `ROW_PLAYER_REF`): the same heads and referent
  words, the same rewrite before `expressible` — a referent word the head does not name refuses the line.
- `src/engine/triggeringPlayer.test.ts` (+4): the damaged player named and the payload aimed there with no
  `chooseTargets` prompt; a head that names nobody fires nothing; a per-item head names each item its own
  player; the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Copper Tablet ({2}, every seat — pings the player whose upkeep it is) and Oppression (whoever
  casts a spell discards) are staples feeding `playerReferents` (the floor: stack objects carrying the
  triggering player): **91 at 60 seeds; 964 over the gate's 500**.

### The wave — 19 rows

The selector offered 23 permanents; the row maker rowed 19 (the eleven discards, the damage and life-loss
pings, the mills, the poison counter) and refused 4 by reason. Every suite passed on the first port but one
`tsc` unused-parameter slip in the per-item fan-out (fixed in the head table); the engine regression (127
files, 14,149 tests) green; no vocabulary widening, so the 551 suppression pins were not due (D426's rule).

### Traps

- **A DAMAGE HEAD IS TWO DEFS**: `dealsDamagePlayer` / `dealsDamageOpponent` emit a combat def and an `Any`
  twin on `DamageDealt` (D371), and the row's `playerOf` is copied onto both — a `playerOf` that read only
  `CombatDamageDealt` silenced the twin (the first generation did; the head table reads both events now).
- **THE FIRE'S OWN COMBAT DAMAGE IS IN THE BASELINE'S WAY**: `p2life0` is read before the attack, so a
  referent life loss under a combat head asserts `p2life0 - power - N` (double strike twice, infect none);
  no earlier row ever asserted p2's life under a combat head, which is why nothing carried the adjustment.
- **THE REFERENT PAYLOAD IS THE VOCABULARY'S ALONE**: `parseEffect` reads `~ deals N damage to target player`
  as the `damageTarget` ROW KIND, whose emitter asks `ChooseTargets`; a referent row must take the
  vocabulary reading of the rewritten sentence and nothing else, or the suite waits for a prompt the def never
  raises.

## D429 — THE WIDE RUN IS THE OFFER: the row maker run over the WHOLE leftover (16,764 permanents) rowed 112 cards the classifier never offered — its D424 mirror's drift since (the statics `can't be blocked` / `can't block` / `attacks each combat if able` / the untap-step skip / `can't be countered`, the modal lines, the filtered and intervening-if heads, the fights, the P/T counts) plus the subjectless `Gain N life.` — and the wave landed 99 of them (2026-09-14)

**10,094 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 9,994
(+100: 99 rows — Wurm's Tooth, Ajani's Mantra, Dragon's Claw and the five-colour lifegain cycles, the
Loyal lieutenant cycle, Kambal, Consul of Allocation, Yawgmoth's Edict, Aether Sting, Bereavement, Gimli,
Counter of Kills, Ryusei, the Falling Star, Dragonlord Ojutai, Nettle Sentinel, River Sneak, Teysa,
Orzhov Scion, the Spellbombs, Cankerbloom, Aether Channeler, Sunken City and their kin — and Dragonlord
Ojutai's second face name by the leftover diff).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,425 → **6,524**; the REFUSED
ledger 1,747 → **1,773** (13 added by reason from the port, 32 the classifier's new static mirror offered
on cards whose other line the row maker refuses, 19 STALE entries the guard named removed — cards refused
by reason in earlier decisions that the row maker reads now). Fixtures 7,133 → **7,232** (7,067 by name +
158 tokens: two token pins). `scriptableToday` 1,846 → **1,864**; the select pool 0 → 32 → 0; the ladder
`[1864, 1870, 3252, 4850, 6177]`. Bot reach 4,162 → **4,212** from 297. A mechanical wave on Opus 5 — no
engine seam; a change to the PRODUCTION SYSTEM (the plan's own phrase): the classifier's offer is no longer
the only way a card reaches the row maker.

### The measurement chose it — the map after the triggering player

The wide row-maker run over the one-piece leftover (8,342 permanents, `make-rows-wide.log`) and, for the
first time, over the MULTI-piece leftover (8,422, `make-rows-wide2.log`): the refusal histogram is flat
everywhere — `trigger payload not a pump` 2,559 + 1,579 over hundreds of shapes (the largest `Put a +N/+N
counter on ...` 94 + 48, `Search your library for a ...` 21 + 38, `You may pay {N}. If ...` 47, `Look at the
top ...` 58, the search forms, the copy tokens), the static lines 1,559 + 2,949 (`As this <permanent>
enters, choose a <creature type | color>` 121 — the chosen characteristic, the largest single family left;
`X gets +N/+N for each` 60; `X's power is equal to` 59; `Enchant player` 42; `You may look at the top card of
your library any time` 36; `As an additional cost` 44; `X costs {N} less` 46; the keyword mechanics Cumulative
upkeep 30, Soulbond 24, Exploit 23, Ascend 22, Cascade 22, Backup 23), `effect not a row kind` 1,360 + 598
(`Add one mana of any color` 41 — a sacrifice-cost mana ability, Phyrexian Altar; the activated searches 41 —
the fetch lands), the heads outside the library 699 + 560. And, sitting in the histogram's ROWS line: 23 +
64 cards the row maker rowed that the classifier never offered — the D424 mirror's drift since D425–D428
(the row maker gained heads, filters and referents the mirror did not). The referent residue D428 left
measured 180 over ~100 shapes (max 4); the triggering-OBJECT referent 385 by a loose count, ~60 real.

### The change — the offer, the mirror, the two harvester gaps

- **The wide run is the offer.** `poolWIDEALL.json` (every leftover permanent) → `linesWIDEALL.json` →
  `vocab-ok-wide.json` (3,503 readings) → `make-rows129.cjs` → 112 rows → `pool429.json` = their names, and
  the standard pipeline from there. The classifier's `select.cjs` pool stays the MEASUREMENT of what the
  mirror offers (32 after the mirror widening — every one ledgered by the wide run's reason).
- **The classifier's static mirror** (`primitives.ts` `ROW_STATICS` / `rowMakerStatic`): the row maker's exact
  static sentences — `~ can't be blocked.`, `~ can't block.`, `~ attacks each combat if able.`, `~ doesn't
  untap during your untap step.`, `~ can't be blocked by creatures with power N or less / greater` (the
  fixture bounds), `Enchanted creature doesn't untap during its controller's untap step.`, `~ can't be
  countered.` — asked after `rowMakerReads`; and `Gain N life.` in `ROW_PAYLOADS`.
- **The subjectless life gain** (`make-rows129.cjs`): `Gain N life.` is `gainLife` beside `You gain N life.`
  — the payload an optional trigger leaves once `you may` is peeled (Wurm's Tooth, Grazing Gladehart, the
  Claws, Feathers, Eyes and Horns: 24).
- **The harvester asks what the row maker asks** (`collect-payloads.cjs`, D398's rule twice over): the `you
  may` peel (Living Totem's counter read in the wide run only because another card printed the bare
  sentence), the modal bullets (both spellings), the activation restriction peeled off an activated payload
  (Vedalken Certarch).
- **The lines dump skips the TOKEN printing that shares a card's name** (`zz-lines`, `commanderLegality`):
  an Offspring's or an eternalized copy is a record whose text lacks the keyword line — the first dump read it
  for Intrepid Rabbit, Starscape Cleric, Coruscation Mage and Sinuous Striker, the row maker rowed a card
  that was not there, and the shipped-script DISCLAIM check named all four (a def claiming `LINES[0]` — the
  Offspring line — for a trigger printed on line 1).
- The teeth check's unshipped example: Ajani's Mantra SHIPPED this wave (the subjectless gain under its
  optional landfall trigger), so Gravity Sphere holds the post (the Yotian Dissident → Humility turnover).

### The wave — 99 rows

112 rowed; 9 failed their first port on generator shapes the multi-line combinations reached first (an
enrage fight's damage baseline, a rampage fire that ends the game, a modal enters-or-attacks counter read
twice, a dead source's power, an Aura's untap-skip the suite could not find on the enchanted creature, a
fight suite naming `onBoard` the module never imports, a cant-attack-unless walk past its own declare step)
and 4 were the token-printing rows; all 13 ledgered by reason. Engine regression 127 files / 14,347 green;
leftover diff 100 newly complete, 0 regressed. No vocabulary widening: the 551 suppression pins were not due.
Gate run 1 red on the two Ajani's Mantra sites above (the unit suite's tier3 example, the fuzz registry's
duplicate); the 60-seed canary green after the fix; run 2 green.

### Traps

- **A TOKEN PRINTING SHARES ITS CARD'S NAME**: the first ndjson record by name can be the Offspring or
  eternalized token, whose text lacks the keyword line; a lines dump must filter `commanderLegality`, and the
  disclaim check is what catches a row made on the wrong text.
- **THE HARVESTER MUST ASK WHAT THE ROW MAKER ASKS**, again: every peel the row maker performs before its
  lookup (`you may`, the restriction, the bullet marker) is a key the harvester must produce, or the row maker
  says `not a pump` about a sentence the vocabulary reads perfectly.
- **A SHIPPED EXAMPLE CANNOT BE THE UNSHIPPED ONE — AT EVERY SITE THAT LEANS ON IT**: Ajani's Mantra was the
  disclaim teeth check's example, a TESTING script in the fuzz registry (the duplicate-oracleId throw refused the
  first gate: `createRegistry([AJANIS_MANTRA, ...SHIPPED])`) and tier3's protection example (Kor Firewalker, the
  same wave); gate run 1 named the two the port had not. The testing copy leaves the fuzz registry the way
  Levitation's, Knighthood's and Ajani's Pridemate's did; the tier3 text rides the Bears.

## D430 — THE COUNTED STATIC: `This creature gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.`, `Equipped creature gets +1/+1 for each charge counter on Excalibur II.`, `Enchanted creature gets +1/+1 for each artifact and/or enchantment you control.`, `Enigma Drake's power is equal to the number of instant and sorcery cards in your graveyard.` — a self pump, an attached pump or a power-only CDA whose amount is a count the row maker's closed reader takes, and the count phrases the family named (2026-09-14)

**10,136 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,094
(+42: 42 rows — Enigma Drake, Spellheart Chimera, Haughty Djinn, Storm-Kiln Artist, All That Glitters,
Excalibur II, Conclave's Blessing, Sima Yi, Wei Field Marshal, Shambling Suit, Zendikar Incarnate, Iron Man,
Master of Machines, Madame Hydra, Reanimated, Snow Villiers, Uurg, Spawn of Turg, Borderland Behemoth,
Nim Shambler and their kin).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,524 → **6,566**; the REFUSED ledger 1,773 → **1,771** (4
added by reason from the port, 8 the classifier's counted mirror offered on cards whose other line the row
maker refuses, 14 STALE entries the guard named removed). Fixtures 7,232 → **7,274** (7,109 by name + 158
tokens). `scriptableToday` 1,864 → **1,861**; the select pool 0 → 8 → 0; the ladder `[1861, 1867, 3251, 4857,
6188]`. Bot reach 4,212 → **4,224** from 304. A mechanical wave on Opus 5 — no engine seam: the `ptModify`
and `cda` static layers and the row maker's count reader (D371/D418) already held every piece.

### The measurement chose it — the two count families

`probe-counted430.cjs` over the leftover permanents: 161 cards carry `<subject> gets +N/+N for each X` (39
one-piece) and 146 a P/T CDA (41 one-piece); against the row maker's closed count reader as it stood, 25 self
pumps, 9 equipped, 4 enchanted and 27 power-only CDAs read (the both-CDA form has been a row kind since D371
— its 28 are blocked by other lines), and the refused phrases named the widening: `instant and sorcery cards
in your graveyard` 6, `Auras (and Equipment) attached to it` 8, `<kind> counters on it` 9, `artifacts and/or
enchantments you control` 3, the subtype nouns (Rats, Humans, Spirits, Squirrels ...), the experience and
poison counters. The wide run with the readers built rowed 46 (25 with a counted static; the rest the wider
vocabulary harvest reached), and the wave landed 42.

### The change — three row kinds, four count phrases, one classifier mirror

- **`make-rows130.cjs`**: `pumpPer` (`~ gets +N/+M for each X`, a creature), `attachedPer` (`Enchanted |
  Equipped creature gets +N/+M for each X` — read BEFORE the generic attached static, which refused the body;
  the side is `host`, since the count's own `who` is the counted controller), `cdaPower` (`~'s power is
  equal to the number of X`); `parseCount` / `pluralCount` take `instant and sorcery cards in your graveyard`
  (two types, the Ritual), `artifacts and/or enchantments you control` (two types, Sol Ring), `<kind> counters
  on it | ~ | this creature | this Aura | this Equipment` (`countersOnSelf`, put by hand in the suite), and every
  subtype the fixture map holds as a count noun by its plural (`NOUN` grows from `subtype-fixtures.json`; the
  singulars derived, Elves → Elf, Allies → Ally). Refused by name: a counted SHRINK whose baseline kills the
  creature (Dread Slag's 9/9 at -4/-4 per card under the opening seven), a germ token beside a counted
  attached pump (the germ proof reads the token at 2/2), an anthem beside another statics block.
- **`gen-oneshot130.cjs` / `gen130-extras.cjs`**: the counted kinds ride the CDA's block and its count helpers
  (`countOf_N` gains `types` and `countersOnSelf`); the def is a `ptModify` static scaling the count (`chars.power
  += n * N`) — for the attached pump on the host — or a `cda` static setting power alone; the suite reads both
  halves of the baseline (`cda0`, `cdaT0`), adds one counted object (a put, a card to hand, a counter by hand),
  and asserts the delta; the Aura is held in hand and cast onto the Bears, the Equipment equipped onto it
  (`attachLines`, shared with the attached static).
- **`primitives.ts`**: the three shapes in `ROW_STATICS` over `ROW_COUNT_ONE` / `ROW_COUNT_MANY` — the reader's
  vocabulary spelled as one alternation each (singular under `for each`, plural under `the number of`).

### The wave — 42 rows

46 rowed; 4 refused by reason after the first port (Vampirism's anthem beside its attached block; Kemba's
Banner's germ; Dread Slag and Grim Strider's shrinks); 8 the classifier's mirror offered on cards whose other
line refuses, ledgered by the wide run's reason; 14 stale entries removed. Engine regression 127 files /
14,431 green; leftover diff 42 newly complete, 0 regressed; no vocabulary widening; no wave name appears in a
non-card test (D429's lesson, grepped before the gate).

### Traps

- **A COUNTED SHRINK DIES AT THE BASELINE**: a negative per-count pump over the hand or the board kills the
  creature before the suite reads it (the graveyard card's printed P/T came back as the baseline); the row
  maker refuses the shape except over the permanent's own counters, which start at zero.
- **THE COUNT'S `who` IS NOT THE ATTACHED SIDE**: spreading a parsed count into a row overwrote the attached
  pump's `who` with the counted controller (`you`), and the Equipment's row lost its Equip line; the side is
  `host` now.
- **A GENERIC READER BEFORE A SPECIFIC ONE REFUSES IT**: `Enchanted creature gets +1/+1 for each ...` reached the
  attached static's `grantBody` first and was refused as a body outside the vocabulary; the counted reader
  stands before it.

## D431 — THE PLAYER QUEUE'S RETURN VERB, AND THE CASTER'S OWN SACRIFICE: `When this land enters, return a land you control to its owner's hand.` (the bounce lands), `When this creature enters, return a creature you control to its owner's hand.`, `At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature.` — the D390 queue over the battlefield takes a third verb, and the `you` scope its own sacrifice (2026-09-14)

**10,185 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,136
(+49: 49 rows — the ten Ravnica bounce lands (Dimir Aqueduct, Selesnya Sanctuary, Rakdos Carnarium,
Orzhov Basilica, Azorius Chancery, Simic Growth Chamber, Golgari Rot Farm, Gruul Turf, Izzet Boilerworks,
Boros Garrison) and Guildless Commons; the return-a-creature entries — Fleetfoot Panther, Whitemane Lion,
Cavern Harpy, Horned Kavu, Shrieking Drake, Stampeding Wildebeests, Roaring Primadox, Species Gorger,
Riptide Chimera and their kin; the caster's own sacrifices — Devouring Strossus, Daemogoth Titan,
Kjeldoran Dead, Lesser Gargadon, Foul Spirit, Commander Greven il-Vec, Smothering Abomination and their
kin).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,566 → **6,615**; the REFUSED ledger 1,771 → **1,780** (3 added by reason from
the port, 6 the widened vocabulary offered that no row reaches). Fixtures 7,274 → **7,329** (7,157 by name +
158 tokens). `scriptableToday` 1,861 → **1,870**; the select pool 0 → 6 → 0; the ladder `[1870, 1876, 3262,
4868, 6201]`. Bot reach 4,224 → **4,233** from 305; `botPool` assisted 1,860 → 1,866; `oracleParse`
`effect:partial` 5,211 → 5,256 (the sentences the widening reads inside a longer spell). An engine seam on
Opus 5 by the user's choice — bounded to the queue D390 built.

### The measurement chose it — the exact-text twins

The leftover by EXACT line text (`d430`'s twin histogram): among the one-piece permanents `When this land
enters, return a land you control to its owner's hand.` 11 — the bounce lands, in a fifth of the format's
decks — beside `Return a creature you control to its owner's hand.` under the entries (Fleetfoot Panther's
kin) and `Sacrifice a creature.` as a whole trigger payload (8 in the multi-piece histogram); the D390
queue already asked a player to choose a permanent the noun admits, and the D426 `you` scope already
asked the caster alone. Two vocabulary rules and one verb.

### The seam — one verb through the queue

- **`state.ts`** `PendingAsks.verb: 'sacrifice' | 'discard' | 'return'`; **`events.ts`** `AsksResolved`
  carries `verb?` (a counter can tell a return from a sacrifice); **`oracle.ts`** `EffectKind`
  `returnChoose` with `EffectSpec.returnChoose?: SacrificeSpec` (the noun the queue offers).
- **`effects.ts`** `askCandidates` / `askBatch` / `queueAsks` take the third verb: a return reads the same
  board as a sacrifice and moves the pick to its OWNER's hand with no reason on the move (a bounce never
  has); the batch's own narration (`returns a land to its owner's hand`); the executor's `returnChoose`
  case queues it exactly as `sacrifice` does. **`handlers.ts`** validates the answer against the queue's
  own verb and the first-ask / next-ask prompts read `zone` off `discard` alone.
- **`effectParse.ts`**: `Return a <noun> you control to its owner's hand.` → `returnChoose` over the `you`
  scope; `Sacrifice a <noun>.` / `You sacrifice a <noun>.` / `Sacrifice two <noun>s.` → the sacrifice queue
  over the `you` scope (D426's discard shape; `Sacrifice ~` stays `sacrificeSelf`); both ASK, so they are
  the sentence's last (`Sacrifice a creature or land. Draw a card.` — Dredge — stays partial).
- `src/engine/returnChoose.test.ts` (+4): the prompt over the caster's lands (a creature refused, the pick in
  hand, `AsksResolved.verb === 'return'`, no reason on the move); one land is returned unasked; the caster's
  own sacrifice is the same queue; the replay hash.
- **The generator**: `returnChoose` joins the assertable and asking kinds; its fodder is the noun's cost
  fixture (a Forest, the Bears) put before the baseline, answered by p1 and read in hand; refused by name: an
  optional trigger whose payload asks (two prompts — Tazeem Raptor) and two asking payloads under one head
  (two queues the suite cannot order — Marsh Crocodile, Razing Snidd). Boros Garrison held four incompleteness
  examples (`engineComplete.test.ts`, `tier3.test.ts`) — Coral Atoll, an unshipped bounce-family land, joined the
  fixtures and holds them (D429's trap, grepped before the gate). Gate run 1 named a second debt: six tokens VOCABULARY

  generator's optional path expects the fire to end in a settle the asking path strips.
- **THE FORCED PICK RAISES NO PROMPT**: one land on the board returns itself unasked (CR 101.4's queue only
  asks where there is a choice) — a suite that waits for the prompt must put two.

## D432 — THE DRAW HEADS' PLAYER, `THEY` AS THE REFERENT, AND THE REFERENT PAYER: `Whenever an opponent draws a card, they lose 2 life.` (Sheoldred), `... this enchantment deals 1 damage to that player.` (Underworld Dreams), `... that player may pay {2}. If the player doesn't, you create a Treasure token.` (Smothering Tithe), `Whenever an opponent casts a spell, you may draw a card unless that player pays {1}.` (Rhystic Study) — the draw heads name the drawing player once per card, the pronouns are the referent, and the referent player is a PAYER (2026-09-14)

**10,208 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,185
(+23: 23 rows — Sheoldred, the Apocalypse, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Underworld Dreams, Fate
Unraveler, Consecrated Sphinx, Mind's Eye, Phyrexian Tyranny, Soul Charmer, Myrsmith, Drake Haven,
Grovetender Druids, Liliana's Devotee, Aphemia, the Cacophony, Pack Guardian, Haunted Library, Rank
Officer, Trudge Garden, Soul Barrier, Spirit Bonds, Zhentarim Bandit, Isolation Cell, Havoc).** Four of
the format's most-played cards in one wave. `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,615 → **6,638**; the REFUSED ledger 1,780 →
**1,773** (5 added by reason from the port, 1 offered that no row reaches, 13 STALE entries the guard named
removed). Fixtures 7,329 → **7,352** (7,181 by name + 164 tokens). `scriptableToday` 1,870 → **1,858** (the
mirror's referent reading filed 12 lines it used to count loosely); the select pool 0 → 1 → 0; the ladder
`[1858, 1864, 3251, 4857, 6188]`. Bot reach 4,233 → **4,243** from 307. An engine seam on Opus 5 by the user's
choice — bounded to D428's referent and D369's payment prompt.

### The measurement chose it — the draw heads

The leftover's draw heads: `Whenever an opponent draws a card` 11 (6 one-piece), `Whenever a player draws a
card` 2, `Whenever you draw a card` 28 (a head since D371 — its cards wait on other lines), `your second card
each turn` 27 (the same); under the opponent's draw the payloads name the drawing player as `that player`,
`they` (`they lose 2 life`), `them` (`deals 1 damage to them`), or as a PAYER (`that player may pay {2}. If
the player doesn't, ...`, `... unless they pay {2}`) — D428's referent one head and two pronouns over, and
D369's payment prompt with the referent as its payer. The wide run with the pieces built rowed 28 (the
payment-with-a-token branch reached the Inspired cycle too).

### The seam — three small pieces over two standing ones

- **The heads** (`playerHeads132.cjs`, `make-rows132.cjs`, `gen-oneshot132.cjs`): `opponentDrawsCard` /
  `aPlayerDrawsCard` over `DrewCards`, `playerOf` = `ev.player`, `perItem` = `ev.cards` (a draw of several
  fires once per card, CR 603.2c); the suite fires them at p2's turn-4 draw step. `they` / `them` / `their`
  join the referent words (`rewriteThey`, the verb conjugated for the singular subject — `they lose` →
  `target player loses`, `they pay` → `target player pays`); every clause of a referent payload may be the
  player (`Target player loses 2 life unless target player pays {2}` names it twice — one pick per clause).
- **`effectParse.ts`**: `UNLESS_RE` takes `target player` and `they` as the payer (`who: 'targetPlayer'`);
  `TARGET_MAY_PAY_RE` reads `Target player may pay COST. If the player doesn't | they don't, X` (Smothering
  Tithe's shape — the same prompt in the other order); `payBody` reads `you create ...` as the imperative.
- **`effects.ts`**: a `payOptional` whose PAYER is the target player but whose body names no target (the
  Treasure for the controller) takes its payer from the object's first player target — the referent's
  injected pick — before the body's own `self` could route it to a null aim (it read `missing` and never
  asked).
- **The generator**: the referent payer lifts the `targetPlayer` refusal (the payer is the head's player, p2;
  the payment lands are dealt on that side); `createToken` is a payment branch (`PAY_BRANCH_KINDS`, the
  board delta); an OPTIONAL trigger whose payload is a payment (Rhystic Study's `you may draw a card unless
  that player pays {1}`) answers the yes first and walks to the payer's prompt.
- **The classifier**: the draw heads in `ROW_PLAYER_HEADS`; the pronoun forms in `ROW_PLAYER_REF`, conjugated
  by `rowRewriteThey`.
- `src/engine/drawHeadPlayer.test.ts` (+3): the opponent's draw names them once per card (and the controller's
  own draw does not); the referent payer is asked and declining makes the Treasure for the controller (the
  payer must be ABLE to pay or the unpaid branch runs unasked — CR 119.4's rule for the prompt); the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Fate Unraveler is a staple (two a seat — {3}{B}, where Underworld Dreams' {B}{B}{B} went uncast at 60 seeds; every seat draws every turn) feeding `drawHeadFires`
  (the floor: stack objects whose ability is a draw head): 33 at 60 seeds; 143 over the gate's 500.

### The wave — 23 rows

28 rowed; 5 refused by reason after the first port (the Inspired untap-step payments — Aerie Worshippers,
Forlorn Pseudamma, God-Favored General, Pheres-Band Raiders — whose fire walks past the prompt; Skywise

none red (466 + 447 + 451 + 457). Engine regression 129 files / 14,582 green; leftover diff 23 newly complete, 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **A PAYER NAMED BY THE HEAD MUST BE ABLE TO PAY, OR NOTHING IS ASKED**: the payment prompt is raised only
  when the payer can meet the price (CR 119.4); a suite that waits for the prompt must put the payer's lands.
- **THE BODY'S `self` HIDES THE PAYER**: an untargeted body (`create a Treasure token`) is a self clause, and
  the aim derivation routed the whole payment to a null aim; the referent payer is resolved before that branch.
- **THE HARVESTER CONJUGATES WHAT THE ROW MAKER CONJUGATES**: `they pay` became `target player pay` in the
  harvest and `target player pays` in the row - two keys for one sentence until the harvester used the same
  rewrite (D398's rule, a third time).

## D433 — THE DRAW-STEP HEADS, `AN ADDITIONAL CARD`, AND THE DRAW AIMED AT A PLAYER: `At the beginning of each player's draw step, that player draws an additional card.` (Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix; Font of Mythos's two), `At the beginning of your draw step, draw an additional card.` (Overbeing of Myth), `Target player draws a card, then discards a card.` (Cephalid Looter), `Each player draws a card.` (Temple Bell, Howling Golem) — the draw-step heads name their player, an additional card is a draw, and a draw can be aimed at a player or over a player scope (2026-09-14)

(+37: 32 rows — Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Overbeing of Myth, Howling
