### The measurement chose it — the draw-step heads and the draw's aim

D432's reportables named it first: the each-player draw-step head (`At the beginning of each player's draw
step, that player draws an additional card` 13 — Nekusar, Howling Mine, Font of Mythos) is D428's referent one
head over, and its payload is a DRAW whose reader had only the caster's own (`draw a card` — `self`). Three
gaps in one shape: the head (`eachPlayerDrawStep` — the active player is the player; `yourDrawStep` — the
controller's), the phrase (`draws an additional card` is `draws a card` at the draw step, where the turn's own
draw has already happened), and the AIM (`Target player draws N cards` — never read; `Each player draws` — a
player scope the draw case did not walk). The wide run with the pieces built rowed 34 — the two heads' 6 and
the aimed and scoped draws under every other head and cost the library already had (`{T}: Target player draws
a card, then discards a card` — the Looters; `Each player draws a card` under an etb, a dies, an attack, an
upkeep; `target player draws a card and loses 1 life`; `target opponent draws a card and you draw three`).

### The seam — three small pieces over two standing ones

- **`effectParse.ts`**: `Target player | opponent draws N cards.` → a `draw` aimed at target index 0; `Each
  player | opponent draws N cards.` → a `draw` over a player scope (D383's shape). And a CONTINUED SUBJECT in
  `conjunctionSplit`: a subjectless right half after a `target player` / `each player` left (`Target player draws
  a card, then discards a card.`, `that player loses 2 life and draws two cards`) is THAT player's — re-read
  with the left's subject, aimed where the left aimed (a referent, no index of its own) — never the caster's
  own discard, which is what the right half read as before.
- **`effects.ts`** `case 'draw'`: scoped → every member in APNAP order (`drawEvents` each); aimed at a player
  target → that player; else the caster's, as before.
- **The heads** (`playerHeads133.cjs`, `make-rows133.cjs`, `gen-oneshot133.cjs`): `eachPlayerDrawStep` over
  `StepBegan` draw (`playerOf` = the active player) and `yourDrawStep` (the controller's own); the row maker
  reads `draws an additional card` as `draws a card` under a draw-step head before the referent rewrite (the
  harvester's `referentForm` the same — D398's rule); the suite fires them at turn 4's (p2's) and turn 5's draw
  steps, with the turn's own draw counted (`P2_DRAW_CROSSED` — a head at or after turn 4's draw step sees p2's
  hand one larger; `yourDrawStep` one more for the row's own) and a `hand2` account for p2's hand (the scoped
  and aimed draws add, a p2 discard and the queue's p2 asks subtract; the assert is `p2hand0 + hand2 + adj`).
- **The classifier**: the draw-step head in `ROW_PLAYER_HEADS`; `rowMakerReads` normalises `an additional card`
  under a draw-step head.
- `src/engine/drawTargeted.test.ts` (+5): the reads (aimed, scoped, the continued subject — and the caster's own
  `Draw a card, then discard a card` keeps its reading); the aimed draw draws for the active player at their
  draw step and not the controller; the continued discard is ASKED of the drawing player (`chooseFromZone` to
  p2); the scoped draw draws for every player; the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Font of Mythos ({4}) and Kami of the Crescent Moon ({U}{U}) are staples, two a seat each (Font alone,
  one a seat, fired 0 times over 60 seeds in the mana-light pools — Bastion Inventor's {5}{U} is counted with no
  floor for the same reason) feeding `drawStepHeadFires` (the floor: stack objects whose ability is a draw-step
  head): 51 at 60 seeds; 537 over the gate's 500.

### The wave — 32 rows

34 rowed; 2 refused by reason after the first port (Nekusar, the Mindrazer and Spiteful Visions — two heads of
one card on the same draw step: the draw-step head's extra draw fires the card's own draw head, the suite reads
one ping where the card deals two — both right, the assert not); 2 the mirror offered ledgered (Faerie
Mastermind's second-card head; Whirlwind Technique's airbend beside its loot); 1 stale entry removed (Unstable
Experiment — a spell the aimed draw completed). The 533 suppression pins run before the gate: 9 red — the D187 spell defs the aimed draw reads whole, retired; the other 524 green (440 + 480 + 469 + 423) — the nine red were the D187 spell defs the aimed
draw made redundant, retired. Engine regression 129 files / 14,646 green; leftover diff 37 newly complete (32 rowed, 5 by the vocabulary),
0 regressed.

### Traps

- **THE TURN'S OWN DRAW IS ALREADY IN THE HAND WHEN THE STEP BEGINS**: a `StepBegan` draw head resolves after
  the turn-based draw; a suite that counts p2's hand from a baseline taken before the draw step counts one
  more than the head drew. `P2_DRAW_CROSSED` carries the offset for every head at or after that step.
- **A SUBJECTLESS RIGHT HALF BELONGS TO THE LEFT'S PLAYER**: `Target player draws a card, then discards a card`
  read the discard as the caster's (a `self` clause) — right for `Draw a card, then discard a card`, wrong
  after a player subject. The split re-reads the half with the subject continued.
- **TWO HEADS OF ONE CARD ON ONE STEP**: a card whose second head fires on the first head's effect (Nekusar's
  ping on the draw its own draw-step head made) is right twice; the generated one-shot asserts one. Refused by
  name, not read around.

## D434 — THE MILL VOCABULARY: `Mill three cards.` (Mental Note, Armored Skaab's kin), `Target player mills two cards.` (Millstone, Tome Scour, Glimpse the Unthinkable), `Each opponent mills three cards.` (Ruin Crab, Chill of Foreboding) — a mill is an effect kind: the caster's own library, the aimed player's, or every member of a player scope in APNAP order (2026-09-14)

**10,323 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,245
(+78: 62 rows — Millstone, Hedron Crab, Ruin Crab, Altar of the Brood, Psychic Corrosion, Codex Shredder,
Sphinx Mindbreaker, Drowned Secrets, Memory Erosion, Geralf's Mindcrusher, Nephalia
Drownyard, Duskmantle, House of Shadow, Ghoulcaller's Bell, Grinding Station, Wall of Lost Thoughts, Sage's Row
Denizen, Vedalken Entrancer, Mindeye Drake, Tolarian Serpent and their kin; and 16 spells the widened vocabulary
completed on its own — Glimpse the Unthinkable, Tome Scour, Thought Scour, Mind Sculpt, Mental Note, Pilfered
Plans, Winds of Rebuke, Chill of Foreboding, Compelling Argument, Dream Twist, Weight of Memory, Thassa's Bounty,
Deal Gone Bad, Ray of Erasure, Sokka's Haiku, Merfolk Secretkeeper).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,661 → **6,723**; the
REFUSED ledger 1,776 → **1,792** (1 added by reason from the port, 15 offered that no row reaches, 0 stale).
Fixtures 7,385 → **7,447** (7,275 by name + 165 tokens). `scriptableToday` 1,861 → **1,878**; the select pool 0
→ 15 → 0; the ladder `[1878, 1884, 3276, 4880, 6209]`. Bot reach 4,255 → **4,266** from 310. An engine seam on
Opus 5 by the user's choice — bounded to D433's aimed and scoped draw, one verb over.

### The measurement chose it — the mill

The D433 wide run's refusal histogram over the whole leftover: 391 permanents and 99 spells carry a `mills N
cards` line — 171 and 67 of them single-line — and the vocabulary had NO mill at all: the generator's own `mill`
row kind (D371) read `Mill N cards.` as a self one-shot (`CardsMoved` off the library top) and nothing else, so
`Target player mills two cards.`, `Each player mills a card.` and `you mill` fell to `effect not a row kind`
(the second-largest class, 1,934). The plain forms are D433's draw one verb over: the same three shapes (own,
aimed, scoped), the same executor branch, the same referent continuation (`Target player mills two cards, then
discards a card`). The wide run with the pieces built rowed 63 (56 plain mills, the rest mills beside a life
gain, a counter, a token or a draw).

### The seam — one kind, three rules, one executor branch

- **`oracle.ts`**: `EffectKind` `mill` (CR 701.13).
- **`effectParse.ts`**: `(?:you )?mill N cards.` (self), `target player | opponent mills N cards.` (aimed at
  index 0), `each player | opponent mills N cards.` (a player scope); `MILL_COUNT` runs to twenty and
  `WORD_NUMBERS` knows eight..twenty (every other rule still gates its own words). D433's subject continuation
  reaches the mill (`mills` was already in its verb list).
- **`effects.ts`**: `case 'mill'` beside the draw's — scoped → every member in APNAP order; aimed at a player →
  that player; else the caster — through `millEvents(state, player, count)` beside `drawEvents`: the top N as
  one `CardsMoved`, top card first; NOT a draw (no `DrewCards` marker, no empty-library flag: a short library
  mills what it has).
- **The generator** (`gen134-vocab.cjs`, `gen-oneshot134.cjs`): `mill` is assertable — p1's and p2's graveyards
  counted off `gy0` / `p2gy0` (a new baseline) plus the fire's own graveyard delta (`gy1Adj` — the self-mill
  row's ledger: an enters row fires by moving the card OUT of the graveyard, a dies row puts it IN, a sacrifice
  or discard cost adds its fodder); a mill beside any other graveyard mover (a destroy, a sacrifice, a discard,
  a damage) and a mill under a head that moves cards there on its own (a leaves, a dies-another, a damage head)
  are refused by reason, not half-asserted.
- `src/engine/mill.test.ts` (+6): the three reads past seven and the continued subject; the aimed mill takes the
  active player's top two, top card first, and none of the controller's; the own mill is the controller's
  library whoever's step fired it; the scoped mill takes one from every player; a ten-card library with two left
  mills two and loses nothing (no `DrewFromEmptyLibrary`); the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Hedron Crab ({U}, landfall — target player mills three) and Millstone ({2}; {2}, {T}: target
  player mills two) are staples, two a seat each, feeding `millsResolved` (the floor: a `CardsMoved` whose every
  move is library to graveyard): 32 at 60 seeds; 312 over the gate's 500.

### The wave — 62 rows

63 rowed; 1 refused by reason after the first port (Teferi's Tutelage — two heads of one card interact: the
enters loot's draw fires the draw head's targeted mill, and the suite answers the discard where the target
prompt stands first); 15 the mirror offered ledgered by the wide run's reason (Argoth's meld, Drowner
Initiate's mill as a payment branch, the quoted grants — Evanescent Intellect, Screaming Shield, Screeching
Sliver — the heads outside the library — Mindscour Dragon's `combat damage to an opponent`, Scrabbling
Skullcrab's Eerie, Restless Reef's `this land attacks` — the filtered heads — Selhoff Occultist, Thieves' Guild
Enforcer — Fleeting Memories' Clue head, Enigma Eidolon's return, Fractured Sanity's cycling trigger, Jace
Beleren's two faces); 0 stale. The 524 suppression pins run before the gate: all 524 green (441 + 493 + 467 + 391) (no hand mill spell ever
shipped — the vocabulary had no mill to suppress). Engine regression 131 files / 14,763 green; leftover diff
78 newly complete (62 rowed, 16 by the vocabulary), 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **A MILL ROW'S GRAVEYARD COUNT OWES THE FIRE'S OWN DELTA**: the generated suite fires an enters row by moving
  the card out of the graveyard and a dies row by putting it in; the self-mill row carried that ledger since
  D371 and the vocabulary mill takes the same one adjustment (`gy1Adj`) — two ledgers would drift.
- **TWO HEADS OF ONE CARD INTERACT (D433's class, one verb over)**: a loot whose draw fires the card's own draw
  head raises two prompts where the walk answers one; refused by name.
- **A `CardsMoved` WITH NO `reason` IS STILL A MILL**: the hand modules and the self-mill rows emit the bare
  event, so the canary counts library-to-graveyard moves, and a `reason: 'mill'` waits for the day the 58 and
  the rows are re-emitted through `millEvents` (D355's rule: a field only some emitters fill is a dead seam).

### The measurement chose it — the `If you do` after a draw or a discard

The D434 wide run's histogram of `X. If you do, Y.` over the leftover (925 lines): after the payments the
vocabulary already reads (`you may pay {M}. If you do` — D369), the two largest are twins — `draw a card. If you
do, discard a card.` 26 and `discard a card. If you do, draw a card.` 22 (+ `draw two cards` and `draw N cards`
variants) — and the vocabulary read the draw and dropped the conditional sentence (`assisted`). The condition is
decidable at resolution: a draw "does" when the library has a card (an empty library still ATTEMPTS the draw —
CR 704.5b's loss flag is set — and discards nothing), a discard "does" when the hand has one. The wide run with
the pieces built rowed 16 — the rest of the 53 lines sit on cards with an unread head (Baral's counter head,
Smuggler's Copter's Vehicle, the `this creature or another` filters) or an unread other line (Scrapwork Mutt's
Unearth, Rubble Rouser's mana line, Melded Moxite's tapped token).

### The seam — two rules, two executor branches, one prompt rider

- **`oracle.ts`**: `EffectSpec.ifDrew?: number` — the draw that precedes and gates a discard. The rummage reuses
  `thenDraw` (D195's field: the draw that rides the prompt and follows the answer).
- **`state.ts`**: `chooseFromZone.thenDraw?: number` — the rummage's draw, carried through the discard prompt
  the way the scry prompt carries its own; absent on every other discard.
- **`effectParse.ts`**: `Draw N cards. If you do, discard M cards.` → a `discard` of M with `ifDrew: N`;
  `Discard N cards. If you do, draw M cards.` → a `discard` of N with `thenDraw: M`. Each is ONE clause (the
  sliding window joins the two sentences), so the ask stays last and the clause count stays whole.
- **`effects.ts`** `case 'discard'`, two branches ahead of the queue: the loot draws first, breaks if the library
  was empty, and discards off the hand AS DRAWN INTO (the drawn card may be the one discarded — a hand no bigger
  than the count goes whole; otherwise the prompt, answered against the post-draw hand); the rummage breaks on an
  empty hand, discards a hand no bigger than the count whole and draws at once, or raises the prompt with
  `thenDraw` on it. The one-ask-per-batch guard stands BEFORE the loot's draw, or a second prompt would leave
  the draw done and the discard undone (D90's half-execution).
- **`handlers.ts`** `answerChooseFromZone`: the lone discard's answer emits `drawEvents` for `thenDraw` after
  the discard moves — off the library the discard never touched, so the pre-answer state serves.
- **The generator** (`gen135-vocab.cjs`, `gen-oneshot135.cjs`): the pair is p1's own discard (no scope, no aim
  — `who` was `p2` for every unscoped discard before); the hand reads `+ ifDrew - amount + thenDraw`, the
  prompt's own assert `dh.length - amount + thenDraw`; and an OPTIONAL trigger whose payload ASKS (every loot
  here is `you may draw a card. If you do, ...`) answers the yes LAST in its fire — or before the combat walk to
  the prompt where the fire carries one — the D432 optional-payment rule one prompt over (the fire had lost its
  settle to the asking rule and the optional rule threw).
- `src/engine/ifYouDo.test.ts` (+7): the reads; the loot draws then asks off the hand as drawn into (the drawn
  card discarded); an empty library draws nothing and discards nothing (the loss flag is set — the attempt was
  real); a hand of one after the draw goes whole, unasked; the rummage asks and the draw follows the answer; an
  empty hand discards nothing and draws nothing; the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Stadium Tidalmage ({3}{U} — enters or attacks: a cast is a fire), Rook Turret ({3} — another
  artifact you control enters) and Riddlesmith ({1}{U} — you cast an artifact spell) are staples, two a seat
  each, feeding `ifYouDoFires` (the floor: stack objects whose label carries the conditional sentence — the
  prompt is no measure, a hand of one asks nothing and the fuzz's hands are small): 10 at 60 seeds;
  56 over the gate's 500. Two canary runs read ZERO first: the counter's regex literal carried a doubled
  backslash mark (a literal backslash, matching nothing) — the applier convention's one mark per backslash
  holds for a `.ts` regex literal, two for a backslash inside a template-literal string.

### The wave — 16 rows

16 rowed, 16 landed on the first port (no refusal); 8 the mirror offered ledgered by the wide run's reason
(Baral's counter head, Gristle Glutton's Blight cost, Projektor Inspector's and Sage of the Falls' `this creature
or another` filters, Smuggler's Copter's Vehicle head on both printings, Izzet Keyrune's artifact damage head,
Wharf Infiltrator's discard head); 0 stale. The 524 suppression pins run before the gate: all 524 green (441 + 493 + 467 + 391). Engine
regression 132 files / 14,802 green; leftover diff 16 newly complete, 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **AN EMPTY LIBRARY STILL ATTEMPTS THE DRAW**: `Draw a card. If you do, discard a card.` with no library sets
  the loss flag (CR 704.5b) and skips only the discard; a test that expected no `DrewFromEmptyLibrary` was wrong.
- **THE LOOT'S DISCARD READS THE HAND AS DRAWN INTO**: the prompt is answered against the post-draw hand, and the
  no-choice branch counts the drawn cards in — a hand of none draws one and discards it whole.
- **AN OPTIONAL TRIGGER WHOSE PAYLOAD ASKS**: the asking rule strips the fire's settle (the prompt is the assert
  lines' to reach) and the optional rule wanted it back; the yes goes last, or before the combat walk.
- **THE HARNESS HAS NO TURN 2 FOR P1**: `advanceUntil(turn 2 && active p1)` in a two-player game runs to the end
  (`gameOver` on the next intent); p1's turns are 1, 3, 5.
- **A REGEX LITERAL IN A PATCHED `.ts` TAKES ONE MARK PER BACKSLASH**: `¤¤.` spells `\.` — a literal backslash —
  in a regex literal, where a template-literal string wants the pair; the fuzz counter read zero twice before the
  staples were suspected and the regex was the fault.

### The measurement chose it — the card in a graveyard as a target

Measured beside D435: 145 leftover cards carry an `Exile target ... card from a|your|an opponent's graveyard`
or `Put target card from a graveyard on the bottom of its owner's library` line — 65 single-line, 60 two-line;
by shape, `card from a graveyard` 65, `creature card from a graveyard` 17, the bottom 14, `an opponent's` 12,
`creature card from your graveyard` 9, the instant-or-sorcery cards 12 — and the vocabulary read none of them
(`manual`: the effect rules had no verb over a graveyard aim but the returns). The target parser already read
every piece — `from a graveyard` as any owner (`controller: 'any'`), `your`, `an opponent's`, the card nouns and
adjectives (D138, D298) — so the seam was two effect kinds over the aim it enforces. The wide run with the
pieces built rowed 42 (25 exiles, 13 bottoms, the rest beside a life gain, a token, a connive).

### The seam — two kinds, two rules, two executor cases

- **`oracle.ts`**: `EffectKind` `exileFromGraveyard` and `graveyardToLibraryBottom` — the TARGET does the
  narrowing (D138's rule): the noun, the adjectives, the owner and the zone are the target parser's, enforced at
  the aim; the effect only moves the aimed card.
- **`effectParse.ts`**: `exile COUNTED target GY_NOUN from (a|your|an opponent's) graveyard.` and `put COUNTED
  target GY_NOUN from (a|your|an opponent's) graveyard on the bottom of (its|their) owner's library.` — beside
  the returns (D298), the same `GY_NOUN`; neither asks; a counted clause (`up to one`) runs once per pick.
- **`effects.ts`**: two cases beside `returnFromGraveyard` — `CardsMoved` from `{ graveyard, owner }` to exile,
  or to the owner's library with `placement: 'bottom'` (the FRONT of the array; `moveTo` is not used — it
  hardcodes `from: battlefield`).
- **The generator** (`gen136-vocab.cjs`): both kinds assertable; the fixture was staged in the clause's
  graveyard already (`fixtureFor` reads the zone and the owner — `a graveyard` stages on p2's side); the asserts
  read the card in exile, or in its owner's library at index 0.
- `src/engine/graveyardTarget.test.ts` (+5): the reads (any, your, an opponent's, counted, the instant-or-sorcery
  noun, the bottom) and the aims they carry; the exile out of an opponent's graveyard; `your graveyard` refusing
  an opponent's card and taking the controller's creature card; the bottom; the replay hash.
- `primitives.node.test.ts`: the "unreadable optional line" example was this very sentence (`you may exile target
  card from a graveyard`) — swapped for a shuffle-in (D117: a test describing the old meaning is rewritten).

### Traps

- **THE TARGET DOES THE NARROWING, THE EFFECT ONLY MOVES**: the two kinds carry no noun, owner or zone of their
  own — `targetParse` enforces `from your graveyard` (an opponent's card refused at the aim) and `creature card`;
  a rule that re-read them would be a second reader to drift.
- **A TEST'S "UNREADABLE" EXAMPLE IS A PIN ON THE VOCABULARY'S EDGE**: the primitives suite's optional-residue
  example was exactly the sentence this seam reads; the example moves, the rule stays (D117).
- **THE CLIENT AIMS ONLY THE PILE'S TOP** (a debt, not this seam's): the zone browser renders its cards with
  `registerSlot={false}`, so the aim veil anchors no buried graveyard card — a human can aim Raise Dead's kin (and
  now these) at the top card alone; the bot and the engine aim any. A client decision of its own.

### The measurement chose it — the spell side

The wide run measures permanents; a spell completes through the vocabulary alone. A probe over the 4,573 leftover
instants and sorceries (2,819 manual, 1,754 assisted) by unread sentence found the keywords (Rebound, Fuse, Storm,
Buyback, Suspend, Retrace, Entwine, Cipher, Foretell, Casualty, Madness, Splice, Overload ...) and, beneath them,
the bare X: 559 leftover spells mention X, 303 of them in a line of one or two sentences, and `num('X')` refused
every one (`Blaze deals X damage to any target.` — `manual`). The X is announced at the cast (`xValue` on the stack
object since the payment problem was built) and D418 already scales a counted sentence by a count read at
resolution — so the seam was one count kind and the substitution D418's `where X is` rule already spelled. Built,
it read 250 more printed faces `auto`; 25 leftover spells are whole (the other 303 sit beside a rider — `X target
creatures`, `Exile the top X cards`, an additional cost of X life, a modal head, `Spend only black mana on X`).

### The seam — one count kind, one gate, one bot policy

- **`oracle.ts`**: `CountExpr` `{ kind: 'spellX' }`; **`count.ts`** `countOf(..., xValue)` returns it; **`effects.ts`**
  passes `obj.xValue ?? 0` — a cast that announced nothing scales to nothing, and the narration says so.
- **`effectParse.ts`**: `matchSpellX` after the plain rules and the counted ones: a sentence with a bare X (no `where
  X is`, no `X/X`) has its X substituted as one (`X cards` → `a card`, `X damage` → `1 damage`, `-X/-X` → `-1/-1`,
  `create X ... tokens` → `create a ... token`), the base is asked of the rules, and a `MULTIPLIABLE` kind (a gain, a
  loss, a draw, a token, a counter, a pump, a damage, `damageEach` and `mill` — the two added) rides with `per:
  { kind: 'spellX' }`. ⚠️ GATED by the face's mana cost carrying `{X}`: `parseEffects(..., xCost)` sets a module flag
  for one synchronous parse (`SPELL_X`, cleared in `finally`); the classifier, the Tier-3 disclosure and the modal
  reader pass `manaCost.xCount > 0`; a trigger payload never does. A bare X elsewhere stays unread.
- **`handlers.ts`** (`chooseX`): a FLASHBACK cast's X stage prices the flashback cost (D307's rule for the cast
  itself) — the printed cost was priced before, and a Devil's Play flashed back for {X}{R}{R}{R} became {X}{R} the
  moment X was named. Found measuring, fixed in one line, pinned.
- **The bot** (`policy.ts`): an `{X}` cast is offered (the `!hasX` filter is gone) and priced from six down to one
  through the whole preview chain (`previewFor(x)`); the first X with a plan is announced on the intent (`xValue`,
  so no prompt is raised); no X, no cast — zero is never announced. `awaiting.ts`'s X = 0 stays the answer for a
  cast the bot did not start.
- **The fuzz**: the driver names X as a coin flip over 0..1 (`simplestAnswer` named zero — the half that scales
  nothing; 0..2 named ONE cast for more over 60 seeds), a value the pool cannot pay refused at the payment and the
  next pick naming another.

### The gate's first run — a library read twice in one resolution

Run 1 was red twice: the three counted-sweep pins above, and fuzz shard 3 — `seed 297 @ event 3247: c226 is in
both hand:p1 and graveyard:p1`, a mill of three followed by a draw in ONE resolution (Thought Scour's, Mental
Note's shape: `Mill two cards. Draw a card.`), both reading the pre-batch library, the draw taking the top card
the mill had just moved. Shipped since D434 and never hit by the driver until now. Every library-top reader
(`draw`, `mill`, `controllerDraws`, the if-you-do pair's draws, `lookAtTop`, `scry` / `surveil`) folds the batch so
far onto a scratch state first — `afterLibraryMoves(state, out)`, the way the explore and proliferate chains do
(D391, D409) — and only when an event so far moved a card into or out of a library. `mill.test.ts` (+1): the draw
takes the card under the milled ones and the invariants hold; seed 297 replays green.

Run 2 was red once more, in the same shard: `seed 225 @ event 4029: c197 is in both battlefield and exile:p1` —
Mechanical Mobster's `Exile up to one target card from a graveyard. Target creature you control connives.` aimed
with the FIRST clause empty: a triggered ability's `StackTargetsSet` carried no clause slots (D299 recorded them for
casts and activations), so `picksFor` read `targets[0]` and the exile took the creature the second clause named,
"from the graveyard", while it stood on the battlefield. The trigger prompt's verdict carries the assignment now
(`StackTargetsSet.targetSlots`, kept by the reducer), and the four graveyard-aimed executors refuse an aim that is
not in a graveyard (CR 608.2b's unaffected target). `graveyardTarget.test.ts` (+1): the optional clause left empty,
the pump lands on the creature, nothing is exiled; seed 225 replays green.

### Traps

- **A LIBRARY'S TOP IS READ AFTER THE CLAUSES BEFORE IT**: two clauses of one resolution that both take from a
  library must see each other's moves; `state` is the pre-batch state, `out` is what happened so far, and a reader
  that ignores `out` moves the same card twice. The fold is the rule for every top reader now.
- **A TRIGGER'S TARGETS CARRY THEIR CLAUSE SLOTS**: a flat target list is assigned to clauses by search, never by
  position (D288); a trigger whose optional first clause is left empty shifted the second clause's pick into the
  first executor's aim until its prompt recorded the assignment the way a cast does.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` CHECKS NOTHING**: the root tsconfig is `files: []` with project references;
  every "tsc green" it printed since D433 was vacuous, and the port scripts' `npx tsc -b` was the real check. Use
  `npx tsc -b`. (It caught `face.manaCost.xCount` on a raw face's string the moment it was asked.)
- **THE PIN'S PARSE LACKS THE FACE'S GATE**: the D187 suppression pins call `parseEffects(text, name, true)` — a
  hand X def's pin holds however whole the vocabulary reads the face; the 27 were found by measuring with the gate
  and retired by name, not by a red pin.
- **A FLASHBACK CAST'S X STAGE PRICED THE PRINTED COST** (pre-existing, fixed): the cast reads the flashback cost,
  the X stage rebuilt the problem from `face.manaCost`.
- **THE RAW FACE'S MANA COST IS A STRING**: `parseFace`'s `face` is the `CardData` face (`manaCost: string`); the
  parsed `manaCost` local is the `ManaCost` — the gate reads the local, and `tier3.ts` tests the raw string for `{X}`.

## D438 — THE BLOCK COUNTS: `This creature can block an additional creature each combat.`, `This creature can block any number of creatures.`, `This creature can't be blocked by more than one creature.`, `This creature can't be blocked except by three or more creatures.` — three CombatDef questions answered over the whole declaration; CR 509.1a's one attacker per blocker enforced for the first time; menace's rule generalised (2026-09-14)

**10,440 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,417
(+23, every one a row off the wide run — 12 `blockCapacity`: Foriysian Brigade, Two-Headed Dragon, Two-Headed Giant
of Foriys, Night Market Guard, Spike-Tailed Ceratops, Knight of Sorrows, Foriysian Interceptor, Selesnya Sagittars,
Ghastbark Twins and the any-number three, Palace Guard, Wall of Glare, Ironfist Crusher; 8 `maxBlockers`: Huang
Zhong, Shu General, Stalking Tiger, Bristling Boar, Charging Rhino, Ironhoof Ox, Norwood Riders, Outland Colossus,
Professional Wrestler; 3 `minBlockers`: Rampaging Ceratops, Troll of Khazad-dûm, Phyrexian Colossus).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,750 → **6,773** (23 in, none out). The REFUSED ledger **1,801** unchanged (nothing offered, nothing
stale; the wide run's unrowable 0 among the rowed). Fixtures 7,506 → **7,529** (the 23 names). `scriptableToday`
**1,888** unchanged (the 23 came off the blocked-elsewhere pool, 21,275 → 21,252 - a mechanism, not a script, kept
them); the select pool 0; the ladder `[1888, 1894, 3277, 4883, 6200]`; layer6 1,015 → 1,007, the restriction split
203 → 195, `attackBlock` 737 → 725. Bot reach 4,309 → **4,328** from 311 (Emmara). An engine seam on Opus 5 by the
user's choice — the CombatDef one question over, three times.

### The measurement chose it — the combat side

The probe over the leftover permanents by exact line: `can't be blocked by more than one creature` 29 cards (11
sole, 16 two-line), `can block an additional creature each combat` 19 (12 sole), `can block any number of creatures`
7 (4 sole), `can't be blocked except by two | three or more creatures` 9 (3 sole) — 64 cards, 30 sole, four lines
the row maker had no kind for because the engine had no question for them. Beneath them the finding that made it an
engine seam rather than a row: **the engine never checked CR 509.1a.** `validateBlockDeclaration` walked the
blocks per attacker (menace's two-or-none, `cantBlock`, the evasions) and never asked how many attackers one
blocker had taken — a Grizzly Bears could block the whole alpha strike, and two engine suites (`project.test.ts`,
`simplestAnswer.test.ts`) had staged exactly that for the combat-order prompts. The rule and the four lines are one
mechanism: a per-blocker capacity (one), a per-attacker ceiling (none) and a per-attacker floor (menace's two).

### The seam — three questions on the CombatDef, folded over the board

- **`api.ts`**: `CombatDef.blockCapacity?(ctx, self, blocker)`, `maxBlockers?(ctx, self, attacker)`,
  `minBlockers?(ctx, self, attacker)` — each `number | null`, `null` where this ability says nothing about that
  creature (a def answers for its own creature and is silent for every other; the scoped forms — `Each creature you
  control ...`, `Enchanted creature ...` — are the same hook answering for others, not this wave).
- **`combat.ts`**: `countsBy(deps, ask, fold)` walks the battlefield's registered combat defs (active zone, the
  source still has abilities — Humility silences the count as it silences the keyword) and folds the answers:
  `blockCapacityOf` takes the LARGEST (default 1 — CR 509.1a), `maxBlockersOf` the SMALLEST (default `null` — no
  ceiling), `minBlockersOf` the largest over menace's printed two (default 1). `validateBlockDeclaration` asks all
  three over the whole declaration, before the per-attacker evasions: a blocker over its capacity (`X can block only
  one creature.` / `X can block up to N creatures.`), an attacker over its ceiling (`X can't be blocked by more than
  one creature.`), an attacker under its floor with any blocker at all (menace's own message when the floor is
  menace's two, `X can't be blocked except by N or more creatures.` otherwise — one check, reason
  `menaceRequiresTwo`, for the keyword and the line).
- **The rows**: four row kinds read by exact line — `~ can't be blocked by more than one creature.` → `maxBlockers`
  1; `~ can block an additional creature each combat.` → `blockCapacity` 2; `~ can block any number of creatures.` →
  `blockCapacity` `Infinity` (the def line spells the literal); `~ can't be blocked except by two | three or more
  creatures.` → `minBlockers` N — all four `COMBAT_KINDS` beside D390's restriction rows, a `combat` def line each
  (`maxBlockers: (_ctx, self, attacker) => (attacker === self ? 1 : null)` and its two siblings). The one-shot suite
  puts two Walking Corpses on the opponent's side — blockers under a `maxBlockers` / `minBlockers` row, attackers
  beside the Bears under a `blockCapacity` row (whose creature blocks on the fourth turn) — and stages the REFUSED
  declaration first: two on a ceiling of one, two on a floor of three, the row's creature on all three at a capacity
  of two (and, at any number, the plain Bears on two — the control); the refusal is read, then the accepted
  declaration (D117: a suite proves the rule by breaking it first).
- `src/engine/blockCounts.test.ts` (+5): CR 509.1a refused on a Bears with no def and lifted to two and to any
  number by a testing def; a ceiling of one refused at two; a floor of three refused at two and taken at three; the
  replay hash. `project.test.ts` and `simplestAnswer.test.ts` rewritten: both staged ONE Serra Angel on TWO attackers
  for the combat-order prompts — legal only because the rule was unchecked — and carry the testing def now.
- **No fuzz staple, no floor**: the driver never blocks (the standing gate item), so no block count can fire under it;
  a canary would read zero by construction. The suites are the proof this decision.

### The wave — 23 rows

The wide run rowed 23 of the 64 (every `~` form whose other lines the row maker already read — Two-Headed Dragon's
flying and menace, Phyrexian Colossus's untap skip and its 8-life untap, Outland Colossus's renown, Knight of
Sorrows' afterlife, Professional Wrestler's Treasure, Troll of Khazad-dûm's swampcycling, Ironfist Crusher's morph);
23 modules ported green on the first port; nothing offered, nothing ledgered, nothing stale. The residue: 47 leftover
cards still carry a block-count line — 20 the plain `~` form beside a line the row maker does not read (a
transform, a must-block, an unread activation), 27 the forms the hook was built for and this wave did not row: the
self forms with a rider (Kemba's Legion's per-Equipment count, a monarch condition, Akawalli's Descend, a Glorfindel
mode), the named selves the `~` substitution misses (Tahngarth, Rocksteady), the SCOPED `Each creature you control
[with power 4 or greater | with a +1/+1 counter | with menace] ...` (10 — Challenger Troll, High Ground, Yuan Shao,
Familiar Ground, Sonorous Howlbonder among them), the Auras and Equipment (8 — Entangler, Alpha Authority, Iona's
Blessing, Echo Circlet, Vorrac Battlehorns, Vanguard's Shield among them) and the spells' `this turn` grants (3 —
Give No Ground, Valor Made Real). The suppression pins run before the gate: all 499 green (440 + 497 + 481 + 289). Engine
regression 135 files / 14,887 green; the bot's and the net's suites 111 green; leftover diff 23 newly complete, 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **CR 509.1a WAS NEVER CHECKED**: the block validator walked the declaration per ATTACKER (menace, the evasions,
  `cantBlock`) and never per BLOCKER; one creature could block every attacker, and two engine suites proved the
  combat-order prompts on exactly that board. A rule the fuzz cannot reach (THE DRIVER NEVER BLOCKS) stays
  unchecked until a seam asks the question; the suites that relied on the gap are rewritten with a testing def,
  not kept (D117).
- **A COUNT HOOK FOLDS, A FLAG DOES NOT**: three defs may answer for one creature (a printed line, a grant, an
  Aura); the validator takes the largest capacity, the largest floor and the smallest ceiling — a `boolean` hook
  would have made the second def's answer depend on registration order.
- **A DEF ANSWERS `null`, NOT `1`, FOR EVERY OTHER CREATURE**: `blockCapacity: () => 2` on a def answers two for
  the whole battlefield; the generated line reads `blocker === self ? 2 : null`, and the scoped forms will read
  their scope there.
- **THE DORMANT `orderAttackers` PROMPT**: a blocker on two attackers assigns damage in its declaration order
  (`attackerOrder` is the order declared; no producer raises the prompt) — the first double-blockers to ship
  make the debt real; a decision of its own.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` CHECKS NOTHING** (D437's trap, met again): the two red suites were found by
  the engine regression, the types by `npx tsc -b`.
- **THE NET SUITE'S COST GROWS FASTER THAN THE REGISTRY**: the four-seat loopback tests ran 14–15 s idle at 4,564
  scripts and 39–43 s at 6,773; under the gate's contention two spilled past their 60 s budget (gate run 1) while
  passing 37/37 alone — growth over hang, so the budget is 120 s now under the ceiling rule (D167/D170/D181):
  the file default AND the five per-test budgets that override it (gate run 2 failed on exactly that). The
  superlinear growth itself is a measurement debt: something in a four-seat table's per-step work scales with the
  registry.
- **THE REGISTRY-SCALING WALK**: five funnels compared every registered def of a kind against every battlefield
  permanent by oracle id; a walk over `defs` is a walk over the REGISTRY, and the registry is 6,773 scripts. A source's
  own script is one map lookup — ask it, never scan for it. Profile before assuming (D388's guess was the wrong funnel).

### The gate's third run — the registry-scaling walk (the mechanism D388's floor owed)

Run 3 was red on the bot tournament's `decisions per second > 10` floor (9.06 under the gate's load; 13 idle at
6,773 scripts, down from 18 at 5,385 and 23.7 at 4,910) — the floor D388 moved for the third time with D180's rule
that a third move earns a MECHANISM. Profiled (the V8 sampler around four tournament games): **80% of the bot's whole
pipeline was one loop** — `staticSourcesFor` comparing every battlefield permanent against every registered static of
the layer by oracle id (N permanents × ~1,000 layer-6 defs per cache-less derive, five layers), and the same walk in
the replacement funnel (`applicableTo`, twice), the static preventions and the two combat walks. Each walk asks the
source's OWN script for its defs now (`scripts.get(oracleId)` — the same sources in the same battlefield order, a
script's defs in the script's own order): 12.6 → **79.2 decisions/s** on the same 220 decisions (6.3×), the engine
regression 14,887 green, and the 60-seed canary byte-identical before and after (336,187 events, every counter equal
per shard). D388's suspect was the replacement funnel; the profile said the layer walk. The fuzz wall's creep
(1,024 → 1,348 s) and the net suite's superlinear growth were the same cost: run 4 read the fuzz at **488.8 s** over 6 shards
(2.7× faster) and the unit stage at 310 s (was 742).

### The measurement chose it — the keyword families, and the cheapest scope

The leftover permanents by keyword line (cards / sole / two-line): cumulative upkeep 80 / 16 / 44, echo 52 / 17 / 31,
exert 36 / 24 / 12, ninjutsu 35, suspend 33 / 13, madness 33, evoke 30, backup 25, soulbond 24, modular 23, cascade
23, `You have no maximum hand size` 23 / 5, exploit 23, ascend 22, dash 22, devour 19, myriad 19, the reveal lands 19
/ 17, vanishing 18, extort 17, fading 17, fabricate 16, unleash 14, scavenge 14, riot 13, enlist 12. The two upkeep
prices share one mechanism the engine already had — D369's `sacrifice it unless you pay` prompt — and their PRICE
FORMS decided the scope: cumulative upkeep prints `{N}` 35, `{C}` 14, `Pay N life.` 5, `{N}{C}` 3, `{C}{C}` 2 —
60 of 80 a mana or life price — and 20 the engine cannot charge (`{W} or {U}` 4, `{S}` 2, Braid of Fire's `Add {R}`,
and 13 singleton verbs: sacrifice a creature, draw a card, flip a coin, an opponent gains 1 life); echo prints a mana
price on 47 of 52 (`Echo—Discard a card.` 2, `Sacrifice two lands.` 1). Beside them, `Each player loses N life.` /
`Each opponent loses N life.` sat on 80 leftover cards (30 sole), unread because the row maker's `Each opponent
loses N life` reader stops at the opponent and the vocabulary had no player scope for a loss — D434 built exactly
that scope for `mills`; the drain rider `You gain life equal to the life lost this way.` (Kokusho, Gray Merchant's
shape without the count) rides the same clause.

### The seam, part 1 — the upkeep prices

- **`readUpkeepPrice(oracleText, keyword)`** (`oracleParse.ts`) is THE ONE READER of a price: a mana string (no `{X}`,
  no `{S}`), `Pay N life.`, or `Pay {M} and N life.` — else null. Four consumers read it and nothing else: `parseKeywords`
  grants `echo` / `cumulativeUpkeep` (two new `TIER2_KEYWORDS`) only when the price reads — `Echo—Discard a card.`
  and `Cumulative upkeep—Add {R}.` stay leftover lines; `engineComplete.clauseAccounted` accounts the clause by it in a
  PRICED branch ahead of the period guard (a life price prints one); `tier3` keeps its note by it; and the keyword
  trigger prices the prompt by it at resolution.
- **`keywordTriggers.ts`**, two entries on D308's table: `cumulativeUpkeep` fires at its controller's upkeep, puts an
  age counter (`CountersChanged` kind `age`) and asks for the printed price times the counters it then carries; `echo`
  fires when the permanent came under its controller's control since the beginning of their LAST upkeep — the one
  memory the engine lacked, `PlayerState.lastUpkeepTurn`, set as the active player's upkeep ENDS (so at the next
  upkeep's beginning it still names the previous one) against the card's `summonedOnTurn`. Both resolve through
  `upkeepPrompt`: `vocabularyEffects('Sacrifice this permanent unless you pay <price>.')` handed to `ctx.vocabulary` —
  D369's `payOptional` with its `sacrificeSelf` body, so the prompt, the bot's answer, the driver's coin flip and the
  client's dialog are the ones every `unless you pay` row already has, and a price nobody can pay is no question (the
  permanent goes, narrated).
- **The bot** (`awaiting.ts`): a price that KEEPS a permanent (`ifNotPaid` holds `sacrificeSelf`) is paid while it is
  no more than the permanent is worth (its mana value) — an echo always, a cumulative upkeep until the age counters
  outgrow the card; a plain tax keeps D126's three.
- `src/engine/upkeepPrices.test.ts` (+5): Shivan Raptor's echo asked once at the next upkeep and never again; declined
  is a sacrifice, unpayable is no question; Illusionary Forces' ages 1, 2, 3 price {U}, {U}{U}, {U}{U}{U}; Gallowbraid's
  1 life then 2; the gate (`readUpkeepPrice` on the printed forms, the keywords on the four fixtures, the accounting).
  `oracleParse`, `tier3`, `primitives`, `botPool` repinned (`keywords:noneTier2` 22,615 → 22,456).
- **Fuzz**: Shivan Raptor and Illusionary Forces staples, two a seat, feeding `upkeepPricesFired` (the floor — the
  trigger on the stack; `upkeepPricesAsked` and `agesAdded` reported): 5 at 60 seeds; 31 over the gate's 500.

### The seam, part 2 — the scoped life loss

- **`effectParse.ts`**: `^each (player|opponent) loses (N) life\.( you gain life equal to the life lost this way\.)?$`
  → a `loseLife` with `scopes: [{ kind: 'player', controller }]` and, for the rider, `gainLost` (a new `EffectSpec`
  flag). **`effects.ts`**: the scoped branch walks the scope's players APNAP through `lifeChanged` (the batch's own
  ledger, so a caster inside `each player` loses and gains on one running total) and hands the caster the sum.
- **The generator** (`gen139-vocab.cjs`): the suite's life accounting reads a scoped loss the way D434's mill reads a
  scoped mill — p1 and p2 under `each player`, p2 alone under `each opponent`, the rider back to p1 — in the main line
  and in a payment branch.
- `src/engine/lifeLossScoped.test.ts` (+3): the parse (both scopes, the rider, the conjunction untouched, `loses life
  equal to the number of cards in their hand` still refused - the count form D418 reads, `loses 1 life for each Zombie`, rowed
  Shepherd of Rot); a three-seat game at 40 life — `Each player loses 2 life` reads 38 / 38 / 38 with p1's event
  first; the drain reads 50 / 35 / 35; the replay hash.

### The wave — 48 rows, and the suite that had to pay

The wide run rowed 49: 30 two-line echo and cumulative-upkeep cards whose other line was already a row — an enters
damage, a draw, a regenerate, a pump, a must-attack, an anthem — and 19 life losses; the first port failed 9: eight scoped losses whose suites asserted p1's life for the caster's `self` (the
generator's accounting read the spec's `self: true` — the scope was invisible to it; fixed above), and Firemaw Kavu,
whose enters damage kills the one Cyclops its leaves damage aims at (skipped, retired, ledgered). ⚠️ THE SUITE PAYS
ITS OWN PRICE: a priced card's generated suite walks through a local `advanceUntil` that answers the card's own echo /
cumulative upkeep prompt with `pay: true` — the harness's `simplestAnswer` DECLINES every price, which sacrifices the
card under test at its first upkeep — with the price's lands staged on p1's side at arming (one basic per symbol, a
Forest per generic, three prices' worth for a cumulative upkeep). 48 green on the second port. The suppression pins
before the gate: all 499 green after the 3 retirements (439 + 497 + 479 + 289). Engine regression 137 files / 14,985 green; leftover diff 74 newly complete (48 rowed, 26 by the seams), 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **THE HARNESS DECLINES EVERY PRICE**: `simplestAnswer` answers `payMana` with `pay: false` (D369's reason — paying
  is the one answer that can be rejected). A suite of a permanent with an upkeep price must pay it itself or lose the
  card under test at the first upkeep the walk crosses; an unpayable price is not even asked (the permanent goes).
- **A PRICE THE ENGINE CANNOT CHARGE IS NOT THE KEYWORD**: the keyword is granted by the price reader, and the
  accounting, the note and the trigger read the same reader — one gate, four consumers. `Echo—Discard a card.` is a
  leftover line, not an echo.
- **READ THE PRINTING, NOT THE MEMORY**: Shivan Raptor's echo is {2}{R}; the first test staged two Mountains for {1}{R}
  and read "the price cannot be paid" — the permanent gone, no prompt — which is the rule working. Commander games
  start at 40 life, so a life assertion written from 20 reads 38 for 18.
- **THE GENERATOR APPLIER'S TWO NEWLINES**: inside an emitted template literal `¤n` spells the escape; BETWEEN emitted
  lines a real newline is needed — two literal `\n` landed in the generator's source and broke its load until found.
  And a SKIP reason with an apostrophe needs double quotes (a single-quoted `payload's` is a syntax error).
- **THE ROW MAKER'S `Each opponent loses N life` STOPS AT THE OPPONENT**: the shape existed for one scope and the
  vocabulary had none; a scope built for one verb (D434's mill) is one rule away for the next.

engine already had in parts: extort is `You may pay {W/B}. If you do, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain that much
life`, which is the pay prompt D369 built with the drain rider D439 read (`vocabularyEffects` reads the sentence whole,
hybrid price and all); modular is `enters with N +1/+1 counters` (a built-in beside the loyalty and defense counters)
and `when it dies, you may put its +1/+1 counters on target artifact creature` (soulshift's shape — optional, targeted,
looks back); scavenge is `{cost}, Exile this card from your graveyard: Put a number of +1/+1 counters equal to this
card's power on target creature. Activate only as a sorcery.` — D329's exile-self price, the parser's `target
creature`, and a printed power the parse carries. The others measured and left: exert 36 / 24 (a client attack
option), suspend 33, madness 33, backup 25, cascade 23 (the continuation seam), dash 22, devour 19, the reveal lands
19 / 17 (an entry reveal price), fabricate 16, unleash 14, riot 13, enlist 12 — and `You have no maximum hand size`
23 / 5, which turned out to wait on a RULE: CR 514.1's cleanup discard is not implemented at all (the spec's cleanup
row lists damage, mana and until-end-of-turn effects and nothing else), so the line changes nothing the engine does
and claiming it would be D90's half-execution in reverse. A rule decision, named, not this wave.

### The seams

- **Extort** (`keywordTriggers.ts`, `TIER2_KEYWORDS`, the canon): a `SpellCast` entry for the controller's own casts
  whose resolution is `ctx.vocabulary(obj, vocabularyEffects('You may pay {W/B}. If you do, each opponent loses 1
  life. You gain life equal to the life lost this way.'), [])` — D369's prompt with the hybrid price, D439's scoped
  loss and rider as the paid body; declined or unpayable, nothing. The bot's answer (a benefit for a mana), the
  driver's coin flip and the client's dialog come with the prompt.
- **Modular** (`withEntryCounters`, the table, `NUMBERED_TRIGGER_KEYWORDS`): the entry built-in reads `Modular N` off
  the printed line and puts N +1/+1 counters beside the loyalty and defense it already put; the dies entry looks
  back, is optional, aims `target artifact creature`, and — because the counters clear as the card leaves the
  battlefield — MEMOISES them: `KeywordTrigger.memo?(ctx, self, ev)` is read at collection against the state the entry
  matched (the pre-event state for a looks-back entry), rides `PendingTrigger.memo` → `StackObject.memo` exactly as
  D428's `player` does, and `resolve` puts `obj.memo` counters on the target if it is still an artifact creature on
  the battlefield. One number, replay-safe, absent on every other object.
- **Scavenge** (`activatedParse.ts`, `ActivatedAbility.scavenge`, `loop.ts`, `legal.ts`): `Scavenge {cost}` is
  synthesized like cycling (D306) — the mana plus `exileSelfFromGraveyard` (D329's price the handler already charges),
  `parseTargetClauses` over the rule's own sentence, `sorceryOnly`, and `scavenge: { line, power }` with the face's
  printed power (`parseFace` hands `baseNumber(face.power)` in; a `*` power or an unreadable price leaves the line
  unsynthesized); the resolution puts that many counters on the target if the clause still admits it; the graveyard
  offer in `legal.ts` no longer requires a registered def for it (it resolves natively); the accounting claims the
  line by `a.scavenge.line`, and the Tier-3 note stands down.
- `src/engine/keywordTriggers3.test.ts` (+6): extort paid drains 1 and gains 1, declined moves nothing, unpayable is
  no question; modular enters with 3 and 1, the dying Bruiser's three go to the Worker (4), declined moves nothing
  and a Bears is no target; Deadbridge Goliath scavenged from the graveyard for {4}{G}{G} puts five counters on the
  Bears and is in exile; the offer is from the graveyard alone, and the accounting claims the three lines.
- **Fuzz**: Syndic of Tithes, two Arcbound Workers and Deadbridge Goliath a seat, feeding `extortsFired` (the floor),
  `modularMoves` and `scavenges` (reported): 11 at 60 seeds; 83 over the gate's 500 — and the two reported counters read ZERO
  over 500 seeds (a Worker rarely dies with a target standing; the driver never spends six mana on a graveyard
  activation at sorcery speed): the modular move and the scavenge are proven by the suite alone, a density
  reportable of the D398 class.

### The wave — 3 rows, and the four the counters shifted

The wide run rowed 7: three the port kept (Syndicate Heavy's Treasure, Life Insurance's vocabulary, Arcbound Condor's
vocabulary) and four Arcbounds — Crusher, Ravager, Slith, Whelp — whose self-counter and self-pump suites read one or
two too many: a modular creature ENTERS with its counters now, and the generated suite's counter and P/T baselines
are the printed base. Skipped by reason, retired, ledgered (a baseline the generator could learn — the entry counters
added to `base` and to every counter expectation — measured as four cards, not this wave). The suppression pins
before the gate: all 496 green (440 + 497 + 484 + 277). Engine regression 138 files / 14,997 green; leftover diff 28 newly complete (3 rowed, 25 by the seams), 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **A HEAD THAT READS THE PRE-EVENT STATE MUST CARRY WHAT IT READ**: a looks-back trigger matches against the state
  before its event and resolves against the state after — the counters of a creature that died are gone by then.
  `memo` is one number read at collection and carried onto the stack object; the label and the item were the only
  other channels, and a number does not belong in either.
- **A SYNTHESIZED ABILITY THAT RESOLVES NATIVELY NEEDS NO DEF, AND THE GRAVEYARD OFFER ASKED FOR ONE**: `legal.ts`
  gated every graveyard activation on `activatedDefRegistered` (a def is what runs the effect); scavenge's counters
  are the loop's own, so the gate takes `scavenge === undefined &&` — the second synthesized ability offered from a
  zone other than the battlefield after cycling.
- **THE PRINTED BASE IS NOT THE BASELINE OF A CREATURE THAT ENTERS WITH COUNTERS**: the generated suites assert
  counters and P/T against the printed base; an entry-counter keyword (modular; graft, devour, fabricate would be the
  same) shifts both, and the row maker refuses the pair until the generator adds the entry counters to its baseline.
- **CR 514.1 IS NOT IMPLEMENTED**: the cleanup step never discards to hand size, so `You have no maximum hand size`
  cannot be claimed — the line exempts a player from a rule the engine does not enforce. The rule is an engine
  decision of its own (every bot game, the fuzz's hands, the tournament's balance).
- **A STAPLE NAME LISTED TWICE COUNTS TWICE**: the fuzz's L1 pool test asserts  PER NAME; two
  Workers a seat is , never the name twice (gate run 1, red on that alone).
- **THE ACTIVATED LABEL IS THE EFFECT TEXT**: a stack object put by an activation is labelled `${name} — ${effectText}`,
  so a counter keyed on the keyword's name reads zero; key it on the rule's sentence.

If you don't, it enters tapped.` — the second ASKED enters-tapped condition after D136's life, the prompt carrying the noun and never the candidates; `When this creature enters or dies, mill three cards.` — one printed line, two defs, the row maker's split (2026-09-15)

### The measurement chose it — the biggest sole count on the table

D439's keyword table left the reveal lands at 19 cards / 17 sole — the largest SOLE count of any family measured —
and the shape was already half built: D136's `you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped` is a condition
that ASKS, with a prompt (`entersChoice`), a handler, a bot answer and a client dialog. A reveal is the same sentence
with a card where the life was: `predicatesOf` reads the noun (`Plains or Island`, `Elemental`, `Giant`, `Dragon`,
`Soldier` — one alternative per `or`), `predicateAdmits` reads a hand card's printed face against it (the one reader,
D389), and the only new fact is WHICH card — an answer the host must check. Beside it, the enters-or-dies head sat on
13 cards (10 sole) as `a filtered head outside the closed reader (an adjective outside the list: this)` — the closed
reader saw `this creature enters or dies` and tried to read it as a filter; D371's enters-or-attacks split is one
line of the head library over.

### The seam — every layer the life price already had, a card where the life was

- **`replacementParse.ts`**: `EntersTappedCondition` gains `{ kind: 'reveal', any, text }` from `As ~ enters, you may
  reveal a <noun> card from your hand. If you don't, it enters tapped.` — the noun through `predicatesOf` (a noun
  the grammar cannot read refuses the line), the printed noun kept for the label. `isAskedCondition` names both asked
  kinds now, and the excluded-type instrument widens with it: `conditionHolds` and the activation `board` condition
  take `Exclude<..., { kind: 'payLife' | 'reveal' }>`, so an asked condition reaching a board query is a `tsc -b`
  error, not a silent tap (D136's rule, kept).
- **`triggers.ts`** (`withEntersTapped`): a reveal price is asked only of a player whose HAND HOLDS a card the noun
  admits (`revealAdmits` — the printed face through `predicateAdmits`, exported for the handler and the driver):
  nothing to show is no question, and the land enters tapped — the life's own rule (a player who cannot pay is not
  asked). The prompt carries `reveal: { any, text }` and `life: 0`; the queue entries carry it too. **The candidates
  never ride the prompt**: a hand is hidden (D137), the answerer reads its own, and a list of ids on a projected
  prompt would tell every seat which cards match.
- **`handlers.ts`** (`answerEntersChoice`, now with `deps`): `pay: true` on a reveal prompt must name `reveal`, a card
  in the answerer's hand the noun admits — else `noSuchCard`; accepted, `CardsRevealed { cards: [it], to: every seat
  }` and a narration, the land untapped, the card in hand. Declined, the tap. The `Intent` grows `reveal?: InstanceId`.
- **The bot** (`awaiting.ts`): reveals the first hand card the noun admits — a reveal costs information and nothing
  else, an untapped land is worth it — else lets the land enter tapped. **The driver** reveals on the paying half of
  D136's coin flip, the card named off the state. **The harness** keeps declining.
- **The client**: a `revealPick` mode — the prompt bar's `Reveal a Plains or Island card` button arms it (`Enter
  tapped` stays the other button), the veil lists the viewer's hand cards the noun admits (the printed face, the one
  reader), one click answers with the card (`aimCommit`), Escape drops it; the describe line says the price.
- `src/engine/revealLands.test.ts` (+3): the condition as parsed (Port Town's two alternatives, Ancient Amphitheater's
  Giant) and the line accounted; a Plains in hand asked, a Forest refused, a nameless `pay` refused, the Plains shown
  to both seats and the land untapped, the replay hash; declined taps it, and a hand with nothing to show is not
  asked and enters tapped.
- **Fuzz**: Port Town three a seat (one Plains and one Island in ~150 cards — the question needs one in hand at the
  drop; one copy read 0 asks at 60 seeds) feeding `revealsAsked` (the floor) and `revealsShown` (reported): 2 at
  60 seeds; 8 over the gate's 500.

### The head — enters-or-dies, enters-or-leaves

`make-rows141.cjs` names `entersOrDies` and `entersOrLeaves` beside D371's `entersOrAttacks` and splits each into two
defs (etb + dies, etb + leavesBattlefield); `gen141-modal.cjs`'s `SPLIT_HEADS` knows both; the self-head set admits
them. The wide run rowed 11: Stitcher's Supplier's and Crow of Dark Tidings' mills, Gulping Scraptrap's proliferate,
Sanguine Evangelist's tokens beside its battle cry, Mouser Foundry's and Experimental Synthesizer's enters-or-leaves
tokens and exiles, the three echo Goblins (their echo the engine's since D439), Flamekin Village's reveal beside its
pump — and Hunting Moa, whose counter on the fixture the dies arm reads absolutely (the etb half put one as the arm
staged the card: two for one), skipped by reason, retired, ledgered.

### The wave — 10 rows, 17 by the seam, 8 stale entries

The suppression pins before the gate: all 496 green (440 + 497 + 484 + 277). Engine regression 139 files / 15,020 green; leftover diff 27 newly complete (10 rowed, 17 by the seam), 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **A PROMPT NEVER CARRIES THE HAND**: a reveal price's candidates are hand cards, and the `AwaitingSet` is projected
  to every seat; the prompt carries the NOUN, the answerer reads its own hand, the host checks the card named. The
  same rule the discard price follows (D137, D415) — a list of ids would have leaked which cards match.
- **AN ASKED CONDITION IS A COMPILE-TIME SET**: `isAskedCondition` and the two `Exclude<...>` types are the
  instrument that keeps a question out of `conditionHolds`; a new asked kind is added to all three or `tsc -b` says
  so. D136 built the instrument for one member; D441 is the first time it had to widen.
- **ONE COPY OF A STAPLE THAT NEEDS A SECOND CARD IN HAND IS NOT FUEL**: Port Town's question needs a Plains or Island
  in hand at the drop — one Plains and one Island in ~150 cards; one copy read 0 asks at 60 seeds, three read 2. A
  staple whose condition is a coincidence of two cards wants the multiplicity (D398's rule, met before the gate).
- **A SPLIT HEAD'S ETB HALF FIRES AS THE DIES ARM STAGES THE CARD**: the generated dies arm puts the card on the
  battlefield and kills it; with the etb half on the same payload, an ABSOLUTE assertion (a counter on the fixture)
  reads two for one. A delta assertion (life, hand, board, from the arm's baseline) reads right. The row maker refuses
  the absolute case by name until the generator reads the etb half's contribution.
- **THE ENTRY CONDITION'S FIRST TEST ASSUMED THE HAND**: `put(g, 'p1', 'Port Town')` with no matching card in hand
  taps silently and never asks — which is the rule; a test of the prompt puts the Plains in hand first.

## D442 — THE CLEANUP DISCARD, AND THE MAXIMUM HAND SIZE: CR 514.1 is the engine's — the active player discards down to their maximum hand size as the cleanup step's first turn-based action, a D137 discard prompt raised before the damage and the until-end-of-turn effects clear; `You have no maximum hand size.` and its five printed kin are read off the battlefield (CR 402.2); a trigger during cleanup gets priority and another cleanup (CR 514.3a's trigger arm) (2026-09-15)

**10,585 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,569
(+16: 11 the hand-size seam completed on its own — Reliquary Tower, Thought Vessel, Spellbook, Decanter of Endless
Water, Graceful Adept, Minamo Scrollkeeper, Thought Eater, Thought Nibbler, Thought Devourer, Locust Miser, Gnat Miser
— and 5 rows: Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur; Tishana, Voice of Thunder; Anvil of Bogardan; Morska, Undersea Sleuth; Trusted
Advisor, whose hand-size lines were the last unread beside a trigger the row maker reads).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,831 →
**6,836** (5 in; every suite green on the first port). The REFUSED ledger 1,816 → **1,818** (Curiosity Crafter's
token-combat head, Venser's Journal's hand-sized gain — the wide run's reasons). Fixtures 7,603 → **7,613**.
`scriptableToday` 1,901 → **1,903**; the select pool 0; the ladder `[1903, 1909, 3297, 4917, 6233]`. Bot reach 4,369 →
**4,374** from 317. A RULE seam on Opus 5 by the user's choice — the loop's step, the prompt, the answer path every
answerer already had, the option, the parser, the accounting, the fuzz counter — and the smallest wave of the arc,
because the rule was the point: every game the engine plays changed.

### The measurement chose it — the rule the 23 cards were waiting on

D440's reportables carried `CR 514.1 UNIMPLEMENTED` beside `You have no maximum hand size` 23 / 5: a line whose only
meaning is an exception to a rule the engine did not have. The probe (`d442/probe-hand.cjs`) sized the family at 55
cards over 30 forms — 23 `You have no maximum hand size.`, 4 `Players have no maximum hand size.`, 7 `Your maximum
hand size is N.`, 5 `... is reduced / increased by N.`, 3 `Each opponent's maximum hand size is reduced by N.`, and
13 with a duration, a chosen player, a counter count or a delirium condition. Before the seam a bot's hand grew
without bound and a Reliquary Tower did nothing; after it the discard is the engine's, and the six printed forms
are one closed reader.

### The seam — a turn-based action that asks

- **`loop.ts`** (`turnBasedActions`, `case 'cleanup'`): the active player's hand against `maxHandSize`; above it,
  `AwaitingSet chooseFromZone { zone: 'hand', rest: null, count: excess, label: 'Cleanup step' }` — D137's discard
  prompt, no ids on it (a hand is hidden) — raised WITHOUT `TurnBasedActionsDone`, so the loop stops on the question
  and the answer re-enters the case with a hand that fits. Then `cleanupActions` (CR 514.2): the turn-long play
  permissions, `DamageCleared`, the D393 control reverts, `UntilEndOfTurnEnded` — the block `endStep` used to emit as
  the step began, moved behind the discard. The answer path is `answerChooseFromZone`'s lone-discard branch,
  untouched: `CardsMoved` with `reason: 'discard'`, so every discard watcher sees a cleanup discard as one.
- **`loop.ts`** (`advance`, the trigger drain): a trigger stacked during cleanup sets `CleanupRepeatSet` the way an
  SBA did since the beginning — players receive priority, the trigger resolves, another cleanup follows (CR 514.3a).
  Before D442 a trigger stacked in cleanup rode into the next turn's upkeep unresolved: unreachable while nothing
  happened in cleanup, reachable the moment a discard watcher (Ivora, Insatiable Heir) could wake there.
- **`turn.ts`** (`maxHandSize`): `GameOptions.maxHandSize` (7; `null` is no maximum) as the base; every battlefield
  permanent that still has abilities (`hasAbilities` — a face-down or Humility-blanked one prints nothing) whose face
  carries `handSize` and names the player (`you` its controller, `each` everyone, `opponents` everyone else): `none`
  wins outright (a player with no maximum hand size is not modified by a reduction — Spellbook's printed ruling), the
  LAST `set` in battlefield order replaces the seven, every `delta` adds, floored at zero; `Infinity` for unlimited.
- **`handSizeParse.ts`** (`parseHandSizeLine`, `parseHandSize`): the six forms anchored at both ends; `You have no
  maximum hand size for the rest of the game.` is a spell effect with a duration the engine has no memory for and
  does not read. `OracleFace.handSize: HandSizeMod | null` (permanents only); `engineComplete` accounts the line by
  asking the field (`face.handSize.line === line`), never re-reading it.
- **`GameOptions.maxHandSize: number | null`** (default 7): CR 402.2's "normally seven" beside `startingLife` and
  `startingHandSize`, where a format's numbers live. The generated card suites play with `null` — the generator's
  counts (hands, graveyards, the watchers on both, across the turn walks) model the card, not the discard; the
  arming says so in one line, and the 21 committed suites the rule broke (13 uncounterables counting p2's graveyard
  at exactly one, the upkeep draws counted on hands across a walk, a graveyard watcher the discard woke) carry the
  same line. Nothing else opts out: the fuzz, the bot's games, the tournament and the net tests play the rule.
- **The answerers** (nothing new to write — the second time a rule landed on prompts already answered): the bot
  discards its worst by mana value (`worstFirst`, the mulligan's order), the harness the first cards of the hand,
  the driver at random, the client through D137's hand-discard mode with `Cleanup step: click N cards in your hand
  to discard.` on the bar.
- `src/engine/cleanupDiscard.test.ts` (+5): the six lines read and the durations refused, the four sole-line
  fixtures accounted; nine cards at cleanup asked for two (`turnBasedActionsDone` still false), one card refused,
  two discarded with `reason: 'discard'`, the next turn begun, the replay hash; a hand of seven not asked and a
  Reliquary Tower lifting eleven; Gnat Miser's reduction across the table (6), Minamo Scrollkeeper (+1), Thought
  Nibbler (−2), Null Profusion's two floored under the deltas to 0, Anvil of Bogardan's `Players` for both seats;
  Ivora's counter under a cleanup discard with the repeat set, the second cleanup, an empty stack at the next turn.
- **Fuzz**: `cleanupDiscards` (the prompts, the floor) and `cleanupRepeats` (reported): 2,108 and 0 at 60 seeds,
  16,279 and 10 over the gate's 500 — the driver's hands run long, and a cleanup trigger fired ten times; no staple,
  the rule is its own fuel.
- **Four engine tests described a game without the rule** (D117): the monarch's and the delayed trigger's draws
  counted on the LIBRARY (a hand is discarded to seven at cleanup); `targets.test.ts`'s walker answers a prompt on
  the way instead of stopping at it; `diffView.test.ts`'s random intent answers a `chooseFromZone`.

### The wave — 5 rows, 11 by the seam

The wide run (16,237 permanents whose leftover is lines alone) rowed 5; the two it offered and refused are ledgered
by its reason. Engine regression 140 files / 15,035 green; bot / net / ui 301 green; the whole card corpus 6,812 of
6,833 green under the rule before the opt-out and all after; leftover diff 16 newly complete (5 rowed, 11 by the
seam), 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **A TURN-BASED ACTION THAT ASKS STOPS THE LOOP WITHOUT FINISHING THE STEP'S ACTIONS**: the cleanup case returns
  the prompt and NOT `TurnBasedActionsDone`; the answer re-enters the same case, which re-reads the hand and only
  then runs CR 514.2. Emitting the done marker with the prompt would clear the damage under a hand still being
  chosen — and the repeated cleanup step (CR 514.3a) relies on `StepBegan` resetting the marker to ask again.
- **A TRIGGER DURING CLEANUP MUST SET THE REPEAT**: `grantsPriority` reads `cleanupNeedsRepeat`, and `priority()`
  ends the step without looking at the stack; a trigger stacked in cleanup with the flag unset rode into the next
  turn. The SBA arm had the flag since D1's cleanup; the trigger arm is D442's — the discard made it reachable.
- **THE GENERATED SUITES DO NOT MODEL THE DISCARD, AND SAY SO**: a rule that changes every game changes every
  count taken across a cleanup; the honest statement is one option line in the arming, not a generator that
  predicts which card the harness discards. A rules test that crosses a cleanup with eight cards in hand counts off
  the library.
- **THE HARNESS DISCARDS THE FIRST CARDS OF THE HAND**: a staged card `put` into the hand is appended, so it
  survives one cleanup; a test that stages two and walks two turns loses one. `findAnywhere` finds it in the
  graveyard afterwards, which is why `put` never failed — and why a count did.
- **THE BATTERY READS THE ANIMATED VIEW, WHICH LAGS THE ENGINE**: its four walkers described a game without the rule
  and sat on `Ben is discarding 1.` for a whole budget - the stops audit broke out at the first cleanup, the may driver
  polled a view whose `awaiting` never caught up. Each answers the discard now, off the seat's own hand through its
  view (a hand is hidden from every other seat), the may driver off the engine snapshot; the stops policy is read over
  priority stops and the discard is its own check (141/141). In a real hotseat game the hand-off follows
  `whoIsNeeded` to the discarding seat; a bot answers its own.
- **THE ISOLATED CORPUS RUN IS 51 MINUTES**: `npx vitest run src/engine/scripts/cards` pays the oracle import per
  file; the gate's `--no-isolate` is the fast path (the unit stage ~5 min). Measure a rule against the corpus
  with `--no-isolate`.

passed / 11 skipped · 500-seed gate, 6 shards, 466.5 s wall · build clean · probe
124/124 · battery 141/141.**

## D443 — EXERT: `You may exert this creature as it attacks. When you do, ...` (CR 701.39) — the attack declaration carries the choice, the prompt lists which attackers a script lets the player exert, the exerted creature misses its controller's next untap step and its `When you do` fires on the `Exerted` event; the bare permission beside `Whenever you exert a creature` is the second printed form (2026-09-15)

**10,601 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,585
(+16, all rows: Hooded Brawler, Khenra Scrapper, Glory-Bound Initiate, Anep, Vizier of Hazoret, Ahn-Crop Crasher,
Rhet-Crop Spearmaster, Gust Walker, Nef-Crop Entangler, Tah-Crop Elite, Watchful Naga, Emberhorn Minotaur,
Bitterblade Warrior and the reflexive form's kin; Trueheart Twins, Resolute Survivors, Vizier of the True, Battlefield
Scavenger with the bare permission beside their `Whenever you exert a creature` head).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 6,836 →
**6,852** (16 in; every suite green once the parser read the Amonkhet printings' named form and reminder). The REFUSED
ledger stays at **1,818** (the select pool 0 — the wide run offered nothing it refused). Fixtures 7,613 → **7,629**.
`scriptableToday` **1,903** (unchanged: exert lines were never scriptable-today); the ladder `[1903, 1909, 3291, 4911,
6227]`. Bot reach 4,374 → **4,382** from 318. An engine seam through every layer on Opus 5 by the user's choice — the
event, the intent flag, the prompt's list, the handler, the bot, the driver, the client's toggle, two generator heads.

### The measurement chose it — the biggest sole count left

After D442 the keyword table (`d442/probe-d443.cjs`) read exert 36 / 24 sole — the largest sole count of any family
still measured (suspend 33 / 13, fabricate 16 / 10, backup 24 / 10, unleash 14 / 9, cascade 23 / 9). Landfall's 102 / 35
is bigger but payload-limited under a head the row maker already has. Exert is one mechanism with three printed
shapes: the reflexive `When you do` (24), the bare permission with a `Whenever you exert a creature` line (5), and the
COST `{T}, Exert this creature:` (7 — left, a cost piece over D168's grammar).

### The seam — the choice rides the declaration

- **`events.ts`** `Exerted { card, player }` — the event the reflexive trigger fires on; the reducer keeps nothing (the
  untap it costs is `UntapSkipSet`, D411's field, emitted beside it). **`intents.ts`** `DeclareAttackers.attackers[i].exert?`.
- **`state.ts`** `declareAttackers.exertable` — the attackers that MAY be exerted, computed by the host (`canExert`,
  loop.ts) because a client cannot: the FACE must print the permission (`OracleFace.exertsOnAttack` — `exertForm`
  reads `You may exert this creature as it attacks.` bare or with `When you do, ...`, the creature's own name on the
  Amonkhet printings, a trailing reminder allowed), the SCRIPT must fire on `Exerted` (a card with the line and no
  script would pay the untap for nothing — D90), and the permanent must still have its abilities. A script that
  merely watches exerts on a creature without the line lets nothing be exerted (CR 701.39a: an effect must allow it).
- **`handlers.ts`** (`declareAttackers`): `exert: true` off an exertable attacker is `illegalAttacker` (recomputed —
  a client's word is not a rule, D139); accepted, after the tap: `UntapSkipSet { skip: true }`, `Exerted`, a narration.
  The `AttackersDeclared` event carries the card and the defender and not the flag.
- **The bot** (`combat.ts`): exerts an exertable attacker whenever some creature of its is NOT attacking — the payload
  is this turn's upside and the price is next turn's untap, so a blocker staying home pays for it; a lone attacker
  keeps its untap. **The driver**: a coin flip per exertable attacker. **The client**: an `Exert <name>` toggle per
  chosen exertable attacker on the prompt bar (`mode.chosen[i].exert`), sent with the declaration.
- **The accounting**: the reflexive line is the def's own claim; the bare permission is accounted when the script
  fires on exerts (`LineClaims.exert`), asked of `exertForm` — never a constant compared against a scrubbed line, which
  is how the named form was missed the first time.
- **The generator**: two heads — `exertAttack` (`event: 'Exerted'`, `ev.card === self`) and `youExertCreature`
  (`ev.player === controller`); the arm declares the attack WITH the exert and proves `skipsUntap` before its settle;
  the bare permission line is skipped when the exert head is rowed beside it; the trigger-line gate admits the sentence.
- `src/engine/exert.test.ts` (+3): the prompt lists the scripted Scrapper and not the Bears, the exert taps, pumps and
  holds the untap through the next untap step (tapped at turn 5's upkeep, untapped at turn 7's), the replay hash; the
  permission is printed and the script must fire — both halves alone refused, the four parser cases; attacking without
  the flag fires nothing.
- **Fuzz**: Gust Walker, Nef-Crop Entangler and Bitterblade Warrior three a seat, the driver exerting every exertable
  attacker it declares, feeding `exerts` (the floor) and `exertTriggers` (both heads' refs): 5 / 5 at 60 seeds — the
  driver rarely attacks, so two copies on a coin flip read 5 over the first gate's 500 and 0 over a 60-seed leg;
  69 exerts and 69 exert triggers over the second gate's 500, the kicked entries 27 (kicked casts 42, from 5 / 2).

### The wave — 16 rows

The wide run (16,232 permanents whose leftover is lines alone) rowed 17; Devoted Crop-Mate's reanimation payload the
vocabulary refused; the first port had the four bare-permission suites red (`can't be exerted`: the Amonkhet printings
name the creature and carry the reminder on the line — the parser read neither) and green once `exertForm` did.
Engine regression 141 files / 15,070 green; bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 16 newly complete (16 rowed, 0 by
the seam — every exert card needs its script), 0 regressed.

### Traps

- **THE PERMISSION IS PRINTED, THE FIRING IS SCRIPTED, AND EXERTABILITY NEEDS BOTH**: a registry-only reader would let
  a `Whenever you exert a creature` creature without the permission line be exerted (nothing allows it, CR 701.39a);
  a face-only reader would let a card with the line and no script pay the untap for nothing (D90). `canExert` asks
  the face, the script and the abilities, and the handler asks the same reader.
- **AN OLDER PRINTING NAMES ITSELF AND KEEPS ITS REMINDER**: `You may exert Trueheart Twins as it attacks. (An
  exerted creature won't untap ...)` — the wide dump's `strip` and `selfRef` hid both from the row maker, and the
  first parser matched neither; the accounting compared a constant against a scrubbed line and missed the named form.
  A reader of a printed sentence takes the short name and drops a trailing reminder, and the accounting asks it.
- **A TARGETED FIRE MUST END IN SETTLE**: the generator's own guard; an assertion appended after the arm's settle
  broke Ahn-Crop Crasher's generation. The exert proof goes before the settle.
- **A STAPLE TABLE CHANGE RESHAPES EVERY POOL, AND A MARGINAL CANARY FLICKERS**: the first gate read the kicked-entry
  floor at 0 over 500 seeds (D403's Ardent Soldier: 1 / 1, 2 / 0, 1 / 0 at the last three 60-seed legs, 2 at D442's
  500) once two exert staples moved the rotation - and the exert floor itself read 0 at 60 seeds after the next
  reshuffle. The third rot earns a MECHANISM (D180): the cast offer says whether one kick is payable
  (`kickerAffordable`, the same solver over base + kicker), the driver kicks exactly then and takes a payable kick over
  any other pick (D408's rule for an alternative cost; the plain branch stays the early turns'), a three-mana kicked
  permanent (Benalish Sleeper) stands beside the four-mana Soldier because the driver's random land drops reach four
  mana rarely; the exert staples are the three two-drops (Gust Walker, Nef-Crop Entangler, Bitterblade Warrior, three
  a seat) and the driver exerts every exertable attacker it declares. 5 / 5 / 5 / 4 at 60 seeds.
- **THE BATTERY REFUSES ANY `prompt(` IDENTIFIER IN src/** (D439's trap, again): a test helper named `prompt` failed the
  static scan at the closeout; `attackPrompt`.
- **A HEREDOC HALVES `\n` INTO A NEWLINE INSIDE A STRING** (invariant 14, again): a test written through the shell
  carried a real line break inside a quoted oracle text and would not parse. The `¤` convention, or a `.cjs` patch.
