## D460 — DISGUISE: `Disguise {cost}` — morph's shape with ward {2} while face down, charged on both sides (CR 702.168) (2026-09-16)

**10,875 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,865
(+10: three by the seam — Defenestrated Phantom, Riftburst Hellion, Bolrac-Clan Basher — and 7 rows: Shady Informant,
Undercover Crocodelf, Exit Specialist, Sanguine Savior, Forum Familiar, Nightdrinker Moroii, Alley Assailant).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,054 → **7,061**. The REFUSED ledger 1,759 → **1,765** (the mirror offered six the row maker
refused, ledgered by reason: a Detective token outside the table, the compound head `enters or is turned face up`,
a subtype anthem, a surveil beside a life gain). Fixtures 7,854 → **7,863**. `scriptableToday` **1,850**; the ladder
`[1850, 1856, 3225, 4845, 6173]`. Bot reach **4,490** from 322. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — morph's shape, one rule over

`measure-kw` on the D458 tree: disguise 43 cards, 10 in reach. The keyword is morph (D309) with one rule more — the
face-down permanent has ward {2} — and the ward tax is a cost the HOST charges and the CLIENT previews (D53): the
two must read the same fact off different data, since an opponent's face-down permanent hides its printing.

### The seam — one flag, one shared constant, two readers

- **`parseMorph`** reads `Disguise {cost}` beside Morph and Megamorph; `OracleFace.disguise` marks it. The cast face
  down for {3}, the turn face up for the cost, the offers and the refusals are D309's unchanged.
- **`DISGUISE_WARD`** (`mana.ts`): the {2} the face-down disguised permanent carries — ONE constant beside
  `wardTaxFrom`, so the host's tax and the client's preview cannot fork.
- **The host** (`handlers.ts wardTaxFor`): a face-down permanent charges the disguise ward off the printing the
  host holds, and NOTHING otherwise — a face-down morph's printed ward is not on the object (CR 708.2), which the
  tax used to read.
- **The view** (`project.ts` / `CardView.disguised`): PUBLIC — the ability that put the permanent face down is known
  to every player (CR 702.168c) — set off the printing the projector holds whoever is looking; `sameCardView`
  compares it.
- **The client** (`client.ts wardFacesFor`): a face-down target charges the disguise ward off the flag and nothing
  otherwise; the printed lookup stays for face-up targets.
- **`engineComplete`** claims the Disguise line beside Morph's.
- **`disguise.test.ts`** (+5): the parse (Museum Nightwatch's flag and cost; Battering Craghorn without); the face-down
  cast and the opponent's view (no identity, the flag, a 2/2); the opponent's Bolt refused short of the ward and
  accepted with {2} more; the turn face up for {1}{W} with the flag gone and the name back; the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Museum Nightwatch ×2 a seat; `disguiseCasts` FLOORED (`> 0` at gate size: 8 at 60 seeds, 21 at 150) and
  `disguiseUnmasks` reported (4 / 9; 52 / 21 at 500).

### The wave — 7 rows

The wide run remade on the seam tree (15,952 permanents) rowed 7 — Shady Informant's death ping, Undercover
Crocodelf's investigate, Nightdrinker Moroii's entry life loss, four `turned face up` payloads through the vocabulary
(Exit Specialist beside its block restriction, Sanguine Savior, Forum Familiar, Alley Assailant) — and all 7 landed
green on the first port (15 tests). Engine regression 153 files / 15,547 green; bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 10 newly complete
(3 by the seam, 7 rowed), 0 regressed.

What the 43 leave behind: the `turned face up` payloads outside the vocabulary (16), the filtered heads (10 — `When
this creature enters or is turned face up`, a compound the library could learn), the Detective token (Museum
Nightwatch), Arno Dorian's subtype anthem, Basilica Stalker's surveil, Fugitive Codebreaker's reduced disguise cost.

### Traps

- **A COST THE CLIENT PREVIEWS IS READ OFF THE VIEW, NEVER OFF A PRINTING IT CANNOT SEE**: the ward of a face-down
  permanent is public information the projection must carry (`disguised`), or the host charges {2} the client never
  showed (D53's exact failure). One constant, two readers, the same sum.
- **A FACE-DOWN PERMANENT HAS NO PRINTED WARD**: the host's tax read the real face of a face-down permanent — a morph
  that prints ward would have charged an opponent a ward it does not have (CR 708.2). Fixed by the same branch.

## D461 — THE ENTERS-OR-TURNED-FACE-UP COMPOUND: `When this creature enters or is turned face up, ...` split into its two library heads (2026-09-16)

**10,880 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,875
(+5, all rows: Ponyback Brigade, Gadget Technician, Rakish Scoundrel, Efreet Weaponmaster, Offender at Large).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,061 → **7,066**. The REFUSED ledger 1,765 → **1,760** (the five rowed cards were ledgered under
the compound head; the stale-entry guard named them and they are gone; the mirror offered nothing new). Fixtures
7,863 → **7,867**. `scriptableToday` **1,845**; the ladder `[1845, 1851, 3220, 4840, 6168]`. Bot reach **4,490** from
322 (unchanged). A generator wave on Opus 5; no engine change.

### The measurement chose it — D460's residue, one head over

The disguise wave left ten cards on `When this creature enters or is turned face up, <payload>` — a head the filtered
reader refused on its `this`. Both halves are library heads (`etb`, `turnedFaceUp` since D309), and D380's compound
splitter already spliced two half-lines back into the walk with one printed index: this compound is one more shape
for it. A face-down permanent has no abilities (CR 708.2), so the enters half never fires on the face-down entry —
exactly the printed rule, with nothing new in the engine.

### The row maker

- **`filterlib.cjs compoundHalves`**: `ENTERS_OR_UP` reads `When (~|this creature) enters or is turned face up, P`
  off the quote-masked line and returns `When ~ enters, P` and `When ~ is turned face up, P`; the walk splices both
  back with the same printed index and the trigger library reads each like any printed line. Two defs carry the
  whole line; the accounting claims it once.

### The wave — 5 rows

The wide run remade on the D460 tree (15,942 permanents) rowed 5 of the 10 — two Thopter / Goblin token makers
(Gadget Technician, Ponyback Brigade) and three vocabulary payloads (Rakish Scoundrel's indestructible, Efreet
Weaponmaster's pump, Offender at Large) — each proven twice (the entry, the turn face up), and all 5 landed green on
the first port (15 tests). Engine regression 153 files / 15,557 green; bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 5 newly complete, 0 regressed.

What the 10 leave behind: the `As this creature enters or is turned face up` REPLACEMENTS (Vesuvan Shapeshifter,
Aquamorph Entity, Crowd-Control Warden — a choice as it enters, not a trigger), Culvert Ambusher's `blocks this turn
if able`, Case of the Pilfered Proof's layout.

### Traps

- **A COMPOUND HEAD IS TWO DEFS ON ONE LINE, AND THE ACCOUNTING MUST SEE ONE**: both halves ride the same printed
  index; a splitter that gave the second half its own line would claim a line the card never prints.
- **THE FACE-DOWN ENTRY IS NOT AN ENTRY THE TRIGGER SEES**: the enters half fires on a face-up entry only, because a
  face-down permanent has no abilities (CR 708.2) — the bus's `hasAbilities` gate says so; no rule was added.

## D462 — NINJUTSU: `Ninjutsu {cost}` — the hand activation that returns an unblocked attacker and enters tapped and attacking (CR 702.49) (2026-09-16)

**10,891 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,880
(+11: four by the seam — Ninja of the New Moon, Mukotai Ambusher, Blade-Blizzard Kitsune, Dokuchi Shadow-Walker —
and 7 rows: Spring-Leaf Avenger, Ninja of the Deep Hours, Moonsnare Specialist, Okiba-Gang Shinobi, Azra Smokeshaper,
Nezumi Prowler, Moonblade Shinobi).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,066 → **7,073**. The REFUSED ledger 1,760 → **1,762**
(the mirror offered two — Ingenious Infiltrator, Prosperous Thief — ledgered by reason: filtered combat-damage heads
the library lacks). Fixtures 7,867 → **7,876**. `scriptableToday` **1,847**; the ladder `[1847, 1853, 3222, 4845,
6176]`. Bot reach **4,492** from 322. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — the largest keyword left that is not a copy, a free cast or a choice

`measure-kw` on the D458 tree: ninjutsu 33 cards, 11 in reach. The keyword is an ACTIVATED ability from the hand
(CR 702.49a) — the mana plus the return of an unblocked attacking creature you control — whose effect puts the card
onto the battlefield tapped and attacking. Every piece but two already existed: D448's synthesized hand / graveyard
activations, D352's return chooser, the cost batch that charges a return. The two: a chooser predicate the board
answers off the combat (an unblocked attacker), and an entry INTO combat.

### The seam — a synthesized activation, one predicate, one event

- **`activatedParse.ts`**: `NINJUTSU_RE` synthesizes the ability (D448's shape) — `costText` the mana plus `Return an
  unblocked attacker you control to its owner's hand`, `returnCost` one creature with the new
  `PermanentPredicate.unblockedAttacker`, the effect native, `ninjutsu: { line }`. 172 more payable activated
  abilities (Commander ninjutsu is another word and stays Tier 3).
- **`legal.ts`**: `returnCandidatesFor` honours the predicate off `combat.attackers` (declared, not `becameBlocked`);
  the hand loop offers a ninjutsu inside `NINJUTSU_STEPS` (blockers declared, combat not over) with the chooser's
  candidates on the offer.
- **`handlers.ts`**: activated from the hand and inside the window, or refused (`wrongZone` / `timingRestriction`);
  the synthesized ability is `defReady` (its return is the engine's own); the returned attacker LEAVES COMBAT with
  the return (`RemovedFromCombat` in the cost batch, CR 506.4); the stack object remembers the defender the returned
  creature was attacking (`StackObject.ninjutsuDefender`), read before the return is charged.
- **`loop.ts`**: the native resolution — the card still in the hand and combat still on, it enters, is tapped and
  joins the attackers (`AttackerAdded`, a new event the reducer appends to `combat.attackers` unblocked; the turn
  record's `attackerIds` stays a record of DECLARATIONS — the ninja never attacked, boast's rule).
- **`engineComplete`** claims the line; **`tier3.ts`** raises no note for it (the ability, the keyword's line).
- **`ninjutsu.test.ts`** (+5): the parse; Mukotai Ambusher — not offered in the main phase and refused there, offered
  once blockers are declared with the Bears unblocked; the Bears home, the Ambusher tapped and attacking p2 and
  the Bears gone from combat, its lifelink damage landing (p2 37, p1 43); a blocked Bears no candidate and the
  activation refused (`illegalReturn`); the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Mukotai Ambusher ×2 a seat; `ninjutsus` REPORTED — 0 at 60 seeds and at 500: the driver's lands are spent by the
  time combat comes (an unaffordable action is not "meaningful", and the seat auto-passes its own window).

### The wave — 7 rows

The wide run remade on the seam tree (15,937 permanents) rowed 7 — three enters payloads (Moonsnare Specialist's
bounce, Azra Smokeshaper's and Nezumi Prowler's keyword grants) and four combat-damage payloads (Ninja of the Deep
Hours' optional draw, Okiba-Gang Shinobi's discard, Spring-Leaf Avenger's graveyard return, Moonblade Shinobi's
Illusion) — and all 7 landed green on the first port (14 tests). Engine regression 154 files / 15,562 green; bot / net / ui 301 green;
leftover diff 11 newly complete (4 by the seam, 7 rowed), 0 regressed.

What the 33 leave behind: the `that player` payloads (Mistblade Shinobi, Throat Slitter, Skullsnatcher, Fallen
Shinobi, Nashi, Ink-Eyes — a referent under a combat-damage head), the filtered combat-damage heads (Ingenious
Infiltrator, Prosperous Thief — ledgered), the copies (Thousand-Faced Shadow, Sakashima's Student, Mist-Syndicate
Naga — Fable's), the counters with a rider (Coiling Stalker, Biting-Palm Ninja, Kappa Tech-Wrecker), Moon-Circuit
Hacker's conditional discard, the planeswalker (Kaito), Silver-Fur Master's cost reduction.

### Traps

- **A CHOOSER PREDICATE MAY READ THE COMBAT, AND IT READS THE DECLARATION**: `unblockedAttacker` is answered off
  `combat.attackers` and `becameBlocked` (sticky, CR 509.1h) — never off a creature's "attacking" look. The one
  function both the offer and the host ask (D168's shape) is where it lives.
- **AN ENTRY INTO COMBAT IS AN EVENT, NOT A FLAG**: the ninja joins `combat.attackers` by `AttackerAdded` and the
  returned creature leaves by `RemovedFromCombat`; the combat state never names a card in a hand, and the damage
  step reads the list it always read.

## D463 — MOBILIZE: `Mobilize N` — Warriors tapped and attacking as it attacks, sacrificed at the next end step (CR 702.179) (2026-09-16)

**10,897 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,891
(+6: three by the seam — Dragonback Lancer, Shock Brigade, Dalkovan Packbeasts — and 3 rows: Nightblade Brigade,
Zurgo's Vanguard, Reigning Victor).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,073 → **7,076**. The REFUSED ledger 1,762 → **1,763** (the
mirror offered one — Venerated Stormsinger — ledgered by reason: a compound dies head the library lacks). Fixtures
7,876 → **7,883** (the Warrior token pinned). `scriptableToday` **1,848**; the ladder `[1848, 1854, 3224, 4847,
6178]`. Bot reach **4,494** from 322. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — an entry into combat, one day after the event for it

`measure-kw` on the D458 tree: mobilize 12 cards, 6 in reach. The keyword is an attack trigger whose tokens enter
TAPPED AND ATTACKING — the one thing the keyword table could not say until D462 gave the engine `AttackerAdded`.
With that event, the rest was already built: the token from `TOKEN_TABLE` (afterlife's shape), the tap, the delayed
trigger (D402) and the vocabulary's own `sacrificeSelf`.

### The seam — a keyword trigger with three events per Warrior

- **`keywords.ts` / the `Keyword` union / `NUMBERED_TRIGGER_KEYWORDS`**: `mobilize` joins; `engineComplete` claims
  the line off the keyword.
- **The `mobilize` entry**: on `AttackersDeclared` naming this creature — N times: a Warrior (`TokenCreated`, the
  `Warrior|1/1|R|Creature|` printing, pinned in `WANTED_TOKENS`), `PermanentsTapped`, `AttackerAdded` with the
  creature's own defender, and a delayed trigger armed on the token (`when: the next end step`, `effects:
  [mobilizeSacrificeSpec()]` — `sacrificeSelf`, so the token sacrifices ITSELF when its own step comes, and a token
  gone earlier fires nothing).
- **`mobilize.test.ts`** (+5): the parse; Dragonback Lancer's one Warrior tapped and attacking p2 beside it with
  both damages landing (36); Dalkovan Packbeasts' three Warriors sacrificed at the end step, the delayed triggers
  gone; the Bears attacking alone making nothing; the replay hash.
- **Fuzz**: Shock Brigade ×2 a seat — the four-mana Lancer was never cast over 150 seeds (a seat holds three basics,
  D445), so the staple is the two-drop; `mobilizeFired` / `mobilizeWarriors` 4 / 4 at 60 seeds (the Warrior count
  read off the LOG: a sacrificed token ceases to exist and is gone from the final state, CR 704.5d); 12 / 12 at 150 —
  `mobilizeFired` FLOORED (`> 0` at gate size; 17 / 17 at 500).

### The wave — 3 rows

The wide run remade on the seam tree (15,926 permanents) rowed 3 — Nightblade Brigade's surveil on entry, Reigning
Victor's pump-and-indestructible on entry, Zurgo's Vanguard's power CDA — and all 3 landed green on the first port
(6 tests). Engine regression green; bot / net / ui green; leftover diff 6 newly complete (3 by the seam, 3 rowed), 0
regressed.

What the 12 leave behind: Venerated Stormsinger's compound dies head (ledgered), Zurgo Stormrender's token-leaves
head, Stadium Headliner's counted damage, Bone-Cairn Butcher's and Zurgo's token statics, Voice of Victory's cast
restriction.

### Traps

- **A TOKEN THAT CEASES TO EXIST IS NOT IN THE FINAL STATE**: a counter that reads `state.cards[id]` for a token the
  end step sacrificed counts nothing (CR 704.5d). The log is the record; the first read said 4 mobilizes and 0
  Warriors.
- **A SEAT HOLDS THREE BASICS, SO A FOUR-DROP IS NEVER A STAPLE**: the Lancer read 0 / 0 over 150 seeds for the
  driver's reason, not the seam's. Pick the cheapest printing of a keyword for the fuzz.

## D464 — THE THIS-OR-ANOTHER COMPOUND: `Whenever this creature or another <subject> dies / enters, ...` split into the self head and the filtered other head (2026-09-16)

**10,915 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,897
(+18, all rows: Blood Artist, Ayara, First of Locthwain, Undead Augur, Zulaport Cutthroat, Arbaaz Mir, Falkenrath
Noble, Thieves' Guild Enforcer, Butcher of Malakir, Arahbo, the First Fang, Dross Scorpion, Qasali Slingers, Mycoid
Shepherd, Pactdoll Terror, Vengeful Dead, Selhoff Occultist, Scion of Opulence, Venerated Stormsinger, Vengeful
Bloodwitch).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,076 → **7,094**. The REFUSED ledger 1,763 → **1,745** (the eighteen rowed cards were
ledgered under the compound in earlier mirrors; the stale-entry guard named them and they are gone; the mirror
offered nothing new). Fixtures 7,883 → **7,901**. `scriptableToday` **1,830**; the ladder `[1830, 1836, 3206, 4829,
6160]`. Bot reach **4,498** from **325** (three new legends — Ayara, Arahbo, Arbaaz Mir — join the commander pool). A
generator wave on Opus 5; no engine change.

### The measurement chose it — the largest compound in the residue, and the aristocrats with it

The wide dump holds 98 lines of `Whenever this creature or another <subject> <verb>, P` — Blood Artist's shape. Both
halves are library heads (`dies` / `etb` for the card itself; D374's filtered `another <subject> dies / enters` for
the other), and D380's compound splitter already spliced two half-lines back with one printed index: this is the
third shape it learns this week (the enters-or-turned-face-up compound was D461's).

### The row maker and the generator

- **`filterlib.cjs compoundHalves`**: `THIS_OR_ANOTHER` reads `Whenever (~|this creature) or another <subject>
  (dies|enters), P` off the quote-masked line and returns `When ~ <verb>, P` (the one-off spelling the library
  prints) and `Whenever another <subject> <verb>, P`; the walk splices both with the same printed index, the
  filtered reader takes the second. `is turned face up` stays out: the filtered reader has no turned-face-up base
  and read the other half as the SELF head (Unblinking Bleb fired its own twice).
- **`gen-oneshot164.cjs`**: two collision top-ups the compound made visible — a filtered head's fixture that shares
  its name with a cost fixture (Ayara's black Muck Rats, eaten by the sacrifice cost and entered by the other half)
  or with the anthem's `yes` fixture (Arahbo's Sanctuary Cat) needs a second listed copy, or `put` finds the one on
  the battlefield and moves it battlefield-to-battlefield — no entry at all (D374's trap, D380's rule); and the
  opponent's graveyard baseline under a head whose arm kills the Cyclops (`p2gyAdj`: Selhoff Occultist's mill read
  2 for 1 — the dead fixture landed there first).

### The wave — 18 rows

The wide run remade on the D463 tree (15,920 permanents) rowed 18 of the 94 — the death drains (Zulaport Cutthroat,
Vengeful Dead, Venerated Stormsinger), the death mills and draws (Selhoff Occultist, Undead Augur), Blood Artist's and
Falkenrath Noble's `any other creature` halves, the enters drains and pumps (Ayara, Pactdoll Terror, Qasali Slingers,
Arbaaz Mir, Thieves' Guild Enforcer), the token makers (Arahbo, Scion of Opulence), Butcher of Malakir's edict, Dross
Scorpion, Mycoid Shepherd, Vengeful Bloodwitch — each proven twice (its own death or entry, another's), and all 18
landed green on the second port (58 tests; the first port's three misses were the generator's — the two fixture
collisions and the p2 graveyard baseline). Engine regression 155 files / 15,623 green; bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 18 newly
complete, 0 regressed.

What the 94 leave behind: the payloads outside the vocabulary (49 — `that creature's power`, the referents, the
counters with riders), the seven multi-face layouts, the filtered subjects the reader lacks (7), the turned-face-up
other halves (4), the Ally / Pirate / Dragon subjects whose payloads did not read.

### Traps

- **A FIXTURE NAME IS A DECK LISTING, AND TWO ROLES NEED TWO LISTINGS**: the same card name for a cost fodder and a
  filtered head's entrant (or an anthem's witness) makes the second `put` find the first copy on the battlefield.
  Every collision top-up lives outside the deck's Set, and this compound added two.
- **THE OTHER HALF'S ARM KILLS THE OPPONENT'S CREATURE, AND THE OPPONENT'S GRAVEYARD GROWS FIRST**: a mill aimed at p2
  under `anyOtherCreatureDies` reads the Cyclops in the graveyard before its own card; the baseline owes the +1.

## D465 — THE CHOSEN CREATURE TYPE: `As this ~ enters, choose a creature type.` asked by the engine, remembered on the object, read by the statics and the filtered heads over `of the chosen type` (2026-09-16)

**10,930 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,915
(+15: 14 rows — Rally the Ranks, Adaptive Automaton, Shared Triumph, Cover of Darkness, Vanquisher's Banner, Engineered
Plague, Chronicle of Victory, Patchwork Banner, Bloodline Pretender, Instruments of War, Steely Resolve, Species
Specialist, Obelisk of Urd, Xenograft — and the second Steely Resolve printing under the same script).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,094 → **7,108**. The REFUSED ledger 1,745 → **1,747** (the mirror offered two the row maker refused:
Kindred Discovery's compound enters-or-attacks head over a filtered subject, Doom Cannon's sacrifice cost over the chosen
type). Fixtures 7,901 → **7,916**. `scriptableToday` **1,832**; the ladder `[1832, 1838, 3208, 4834, 6166]`. Bot reach
**4,508** from **325**. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — the largest static family left that one prompt unlocks

The wide dump holds 53 permanents printing `As this ~ enters, choose a creature type.` (162 in D136's count over the
whole pool; 84 cards carry a consumer line naming `the chosen type`). D147 built the COLOUR clause and refused the
other two shapes by name — "a prompt as theatre, worse than the silence it replaced" — because nothing read the
answer. The generated statics now do: `Creatures (you control )?of the chosen type get / have ...` is D371's scoped
anthem with one more conjunct, `is the chosen type in addition to its other types` is a layer-4 static the `StaticDef`
surface already allowed and no script had used, and D374's filtered heads take `of the chosen type` as a trailing
qualifier like `you control`.

### The engine seam (`apply-ctype-1..7.cjs`)

- **`replacementParse.ts`**: `CHOOSE_TYPE_RE = /^As (?:this [A-Za-z]+|[A-Z][^,]*) enters, choose a creature type\.$/`
  (anchored at both ends like the colour clause; `this Vehicle` prints a capital — Lifecraft Engine — so the noun is
  case-free); `OracleFace.choosesTypeOnEntry`; `engineComplete` claims the line off the flag.
- **`state.ts`**: `CardInstance.chosenType: string | null` beside `chosenColor`, cleared with the battlefield fields;
  the `chooseCreatureType` prompt (player, source, label — no options ride it: the catalogue is
  `OracleDb.creatureTypes`, D310's changeling list, which every client already holds).
- **`triggers.ts withChosenColor`**: the same one-at-a-time entry site raises the type prompt off the second flag — as
  TWO literals, because the awaiting pin reads producers by their literal `kind: '…'` and a ternary over the kind hid
  both.
- **`handlers.ts answerChooseCreatureType`**: refuses a name outside the catalogue (`notACreatureType` — a misspelling
  stored would be a permanent that quietly applies to nothing), the wrong player, nothing waiting; `CreatureTypeChosen`
  and the narration.
- The harness answers **Bear** (the generated suites' fixture is Grizzly Bears); the net script Human; the bot the
  subtype most of its own creature cards print (hand and battlefield, ties alphabetical, Human when nothing says); the
  prompt bar a name field with the table's creature types as suggestions and a `Name it` button. `chosenType.test.ts`:
  the parse, the claim, the prompt, the answer read by an inline static, the refusals, the bounce, the replay hash.

### The generator

- **`gen165-scope.cjs`**: the `chosenType` scope (`Creatures you control of the chosen type`, `Other …`, `Creatures of
  the chosen type`, `All …`), its predicate `chars.typeLine.subtypes.includes(ctx.state.cards[self]?.chosenType ?? '')`
  (the DERIVED subtypes, so a type another static added counts), the Bears fixture, `usesSelf` so the emitter names
  `self` even for a scope that asks no controller.
- **`make-rows165.cjs` / `gen-oneshot165.cjs`**: the `typeAdd` row (`This creature is the chosen type in addition to its
  other types` on the source; `Each creature you control is …` on its controller's creatures) emitted as a
  `layer: 'type'` static that appends the answer to `chars.typeLine.subtypes`; the suite reads the derived subtypes
  (`subs`) and asserts Bear on the source or on the Eel and not on the Cyclops.
- **`filterlib.cjs`**: `of the chosen type` peeled as a trailing qualifier (`chosenType: true`), the `permConjuncts`
  comparison against the source, and `gen165-headfix.cjs admits` narrowing the fixture to a Bear — Vanquisher's Banner
  and Chronicle of Victory cast a Balduvian Bears, Bloodline Pretender's other Bear enters, Species Specialist's dies.

### The wave — 14 rows, 31 tests, green on the first port

Engine regression 156 files / 15,657 green; bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 15 newly complete, 0 regressed.
Fuzz: a Shared Triumph a seat (`creatureTypesChosen` 6 at 60 seeds, 13 at 150, then 0 / 13 on the re-deal — reported, no
floor); Shock Brigade to FOUR a seat after D463's floor read 0 at 60 and 150 on this tree (15 over the D464 gate's 500;
8 in one 20-seed shard at twelve a seat — the mechanism is proven, the rate was the deal; 8 at 150 with four, 41 over
the gate's 500; `creatureTypesChosen` 39 over the 500).

What the 84 leave behind: the mana restriction `Spend this mana only to cast a creature spell of the chosen type` (4 —
the restriction matcher reads no chosen type), `Creatures of the chosen type your opponents control` (Plague Engineer —
no opponents-controlled scope), the charge-counter payloads (Door of Destinies, Rimefire Torque), the compound
enters-or-attacks head (Kindred Discovery), the sacrifice cost over the chosen type (Doom Cannon, Etchings of the
Chosen), the enters-with replacement (Metallic Mimic), the spells-and-cards-elsewhere type-add (Leyline of
Transformation, Arcane Adaptation, Conspiracy), the copy and the cost reduction families.

### Traps

- **A TERNARY OVER A PROMPT KIND HIDES BOTH PRODUCERS**: the awaiting pin scans `kind: '<name>'` constructions; the
  entry site is two object literals, one per kind.
- **THE WALK ANSWERS THE ENTRY PROMPT, `settle` DOES NOT**: `advanceUntil` checks `done` first, so a `settle` after a
  move that raised a prompt returns with it standing; the generated arm enters the card before the turn-3 walk whose
  predicate says `awaiting === null`, and the harness's Bear is what the statics then read.
- **A CLAIMED CLAUSE MOVES A TIER-3 PIN**: Cavern of Souls' entry clause no longer earns the ability-text note
  (`tier3.test.ts`), and the first gate run said so — the unit pins outside the ten the port runs are the gate's to name.
- **A FUZZ RATE READ AT 60 AND 150 IS THE DEAL, NOT THE MECHANISM**: a two-a-seat staple's floor can read 0 on a
  retuned pool while a twelve-a-seat probe fires eight times in twenty seeds; raise the density before the gate.

## D466 — THE BLOCKER PREDICATE: `~ can't be blocked by / except by <subject>` as a `canBlock` over the filter reader's conjuncts on the derived blocker (2026-09-16)

**10,963 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,930
(+33, all rows: Taoist Mystic, Juggernaut, Nick Valentine, Private Eye, Gnat Alley Creeper, Bog Rats, Stromkirk Noble,
Orchard Spirit, Silhana Ledgewalker, Treetop Scout, Lightning Mare, Fen Hauler, Treetop Rangers, Barrenton Cragtreads,
Audacious Infiltrator, Dauthi Horror, Spire Tracer, Dread Warlock, Signal Pest, Noggle Bandit, Zuo Ci, the Mocking Sage,
Stone Spirit, Prowling Nightstalker, Rampart Crawler, River Darter, Plague Mare, Deathcult Rogue, Wanderbrine Rootcutters,
Argothian Sprite, Raven's Run Dragoon, Vine Mare, Mudbrawler Raiders, Skyscythe Engulfer, Sootwalkers).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,108 → **7,141**. The REFUSED ledger stays **1,747** (the mirror offered nothing; the classifier never
counted these lines as scriptable, so `scriptableToday` stays **1,832** and the ladder reads `[1832, 1838, 3176, 4802,
6134]`). Fixtures 7,916 → **7,951**. Bot reach **4,522** from **327** (two new legends). A generator wave on Opus 5; no
engine change.

### The measurement chose it — 66 cards refused FIRST on an evasion line the reader already had the words for

The wide dump holds 135 `~ can't be blocked ...` statics; the row maker read the bare form, the block counts and the
power bound (D438) and refused the rest by name - `by artifact creatures`, `by Walls`, `by blue creatures`, `by creatures
with flying`, `except by black creatures`, `except by creatures with flying or reach`. Every one of those subjects is a
phrase D374's filter reader already parses for a trigger head; what was missing was the one `canBlock` that composes its
conjuncts over the blocker. 66 cards were refused first on such a line; 34 rowed on the D465 lines (33 after the
zero-power guard below).

### The generator

- **`filterlib.cjs`**: `with A or B` as an any-of keyword pair (`keywordsAny`, admitted by either; `permConjuncts`
  writes the disjunction); `permConjuncts` and the Cyclops record exported for the blocker.
- **`make-rows166.cjs`**: `~ can't be blocked (by|except by) <subject>.` → `cantBeBlockedBy` `{ filter, except, gift }`
  after the older readers (the count and power forms keep theirs); a subject naming a controller, a token or a power
  bound is refused; `except by` is refused when the opponent's Cyclops satisfies the exception (its refusal would prove
  nothing); the `by` form derives a blocker the filter admits for the opponent through a new `blocker` fixture base
  (defender allowed, power may be 0 - Steel Wall for Walls, Ornithopter for fliers, Memnite for artifact creatures,
  Aegis Turtle for blue, Crimson Kobolds for red, Wei Scout for horsemanship).
- **`gen166-extras.cjs`**: `canBlock: (ctx, self, blocker, attacker) => attacker !== self || !(<conjuncts over
  ctx.derive(blocker)>)` (`except by` drops the negation); the fire attacks beside the Bears on the third turn and records
  the refused block - the gifted blocker for `by`, the Cyclops for `except by` - then declares none.
- **A zero-power guard**: a SELF damage head (`deals combat damage to a player`, `deals damage to an opponent`, …) on a
  creature with no printed power is refused - Surge Mare, a 0/5, reached the generator for the first time behind its
  evasion line and its trigger suite walked the game out waiting for a prompt its attack could never raise.

### The wave — 33 rows, 75 tests, green on the second port

The first port carried Surge Mare (34) and its damage suite failed as above; the row refused, the module and its
registrations removed (`unport-surge.cjs`), the second port green 33/33. Engine regression 156 files / 15,723 green;
bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 33 newly complete, 0 regressed. No fuzz change.

What the 66 leave behind: `and/or` subjects (Amrou Seekers, Skirk Shaman - artifact creatures and/or white creatures),
`non-Wall creatures`, `creatures with greater power` / `toughness 3 or greater` (a comparison against the attacker, not a
bound), `creatures that share a creature type`, `enchanted creatures`, `creature tokens` (no token blocker the suite can
put), subjects with no quiet fixture (Saprolings, Oxen, Eldrazi Scions), the as-long-as and unless conditions.

### Traps

- **A ROW THAT WAS ALWAYS REFUSED FIRST ON ONE LINE HAS NEVER MET THE GENERATOR ON ITS OTHERS**: widening a reader
  lets its second lines through for the first time; the zero-power damage head was the one that failed, and the guard
  is the row maker's, not the suite's.
- **THE REFUSED BLOCK IS THE PROOF, AND IT NEEDS A BLOCKER THE PREDICATE NAMES**: `by X` is proven on an X the suite
  deals to the opponent, `except by X` on the Cyclops outside X - a row whose exception the Cyclops satisfies is refused
  rather than proven by a block that would have been refused anyway.

## D467 — THE FILTERED COMBAT-DAMAGE HEAD: `Whenever (one or more )?<subject> deals combat damage to a player / an opponent, P` as a filter base, batched or fanned out per source (2026-09-16)

**10,975 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,963
(+12, all rows: Professional Face-Breaker, Moria Marauder, Coastal Piracy, Sharding Sphinx, Ongoing Investigation,
Rampart Smasher, Prosperous Thief, Aya of Alexandria, Ingenious Infiltrator, Curious Altisaur, Ezio, Blade of Vengeance,
Raiders' Spoils).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,141 → **7,153**. The REFUSED ledger 1,747 → **1,736** (eleven of the rowed cards
were ledgered under the filtered combat-damage heads the library lacked - D462's Ninja pair among them; the stale-entry
guard named them and they are gone). Fixtures 7,951 → **7,964**. `scriptableToday` 1,832 → **1,821**; the ladder
`[1821, 1827, 3164, 4790, 6122]`. Bot reach **4,523** from **329**. A generator wave on Opus 5; no engine change.

### The measurement chose it — the largest head family the filter reader had no base for

The wide dump holds 289 filtered combat-damage lines (58 with a vocabulary payload): `a creature you control` 27,
`one or more creatures you control` 22, `a Vehicle you control` 5, `a creature you control with deathtouch` 4, the
Faeries, the artifact creatures, the Ninjas. The library's `creatureCombatDamagePlayer` reads the plain form and
`combatDamagePlayer` the card's own; D374's reader had bases for entering, dying, leaving, tapping, casting, blocking and
sacrificing - never for connecting.

### The generator

- **`filterlib.cjs`**: `HEAD_RE.combatDamagePlayer` (`one or more` optional, the target `a player` / `one or more
  players` / `an opponent`); the caster slot carries `batch|<target>` or `each|<target>`; `combatDamageParts` composes
  the entry's conjuncts (the target a player, damage dealt, `an opponent` against the source's controller, the
  controller, the derived source through `permConjuncts`); `matchesSrc` asks them of the batch; **`perItemSrc`** returns
  the matching sources deduplicated in event order for the singular form (CR 603.2c - each creature that connects is
  its own event to the ability; `one or more` is one trigger per damage step). An any-of SUBTYPE pair (`a Ninja or
  Rogue you control`, `Goblin or Orc creatures`) reads into `subtypesAny`, admitted by either.
- **`make-rows167.cjs`**: the head rides the library's own name (every list keyed on it keeps working); the row carries
  `filterFixturePower` (the p2 life baseline) and `perItemCode` when singular; an opponent's creature (it would attack
  on its own turn) and a token (no fixture) refuse.
- **`gen-oneshot167.cjs`**: the combat fixture is a STILL fixture - down before the baselines - that attacks the
  opponent unblocked on the third turn (the `block` derivation: attack-capable, quiet, admitted - Memnite, Fang of
  Shigeki, Raptor Companion, Triton Shorethief, Mons's Goblin Raiders, Black Widow, Natasha Romanoff); `perItem` is
  emitted off the row; `p2LifeAdjOf` reads the fixture's power.

### The wave — 12 rows, 28 tests, green on the first port

Rampart Smasher rode in on the subtype pair alone (`can't be blocked by Knights or Walls`, D466's predicate).
Engine regression 156 files / 15,747 green; bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 12 newly complete, 0 regressed.
No fuzz change.

What the 289 leave behind: the payloads outside the vocabulary (231 - `that player` referents under a filtered head,
copies, ventures, top-card exiles), the `you` target (the opponent's creature attacking on its turn), the qualifiers the
reader lacks (`with a counter on it`, `with a legendary Equipment attached`, `that entered this turn`, `each with power
greater than its base power`), the compound `enters or deals combat damage` heads, the multi-face layouts, and the
cards whose OTHER line blocks them (Toski's must-attack beside a head whose test attacks with another creature, the
initiative, the corrupted conditions).

### Traps

- **A BATCHED HEAD AND A SINGULAR HEAD ARE TWO DEFS OVER ONE EVENT**: `one or more creatures you control deal combat
  damage` fires once per damage step; `a creature you control deals combat damage` once per creature. The batch is the
  matcher alone; the singular adds `perItem` over the same conjuncts, and a suite with one attacker cannot tell them
  apart - the wording decides, never the count the suite happens to stage.
- **THE COMBAT FIXTURE IS A STILL FIXTURE THAT MOVES**: it waits on the board from the arm like a tap or untap fixture,
  but its fire is an attack that costs the opponent its power - the p2 life baseline reads `filterFixturePower`, not
  the Bears' 2.

## D468 — THE NAMED ENTRY COUNTER: `~ enters with N <kind> counters on it` for any inert counter kind on any permanent, and the self remove-counter activations behind it (2026-09-16)

**10,992 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,975
(+17, all rows: Bladed Ambassador, Sunset Pyramid, Trigon of Rage, Trigon of Corruption, Predation Steward, Gitaxian
Raptor, Necrogen Censer, Tumble Magnet, Incubation Sac, Furnace Strider, Shriekhorn, Trigon of Infestation, Glistener
Seer, Axiom Engraver, Tamiyo's Immobilizer, Trawler Drake, Trigon of Thought).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,153 → **7,170**. The
REFUSED ledger stays **1,736** (the mirror offered nothing). Fixtures 7,964 → **7,982** (7,809 by name + 173 tokens - the
Phyrexian Insect pinned). `scriptableToday` **1,821**; the ladder `[1821, 1827, 3164, 4773, 6105]`. Bot reach **4,531**
from **329**. A generator wave on Opus 5; no engine change.

### The measurement chose it — 159 entry-counter lines, 87 of them a named kind the reader refused

The wide dump holds 159 `~ enters with N <kind> counters on it` lines: 72 are +1/+1 (D371's row), 20 are -1/-1 (D447's),
and 87 name a kind - oil 19, charge 12, shield 8, wish 3, brick, page, mining, story, suspect, cube, spore ... - which the
reader refused wholesale as `enters-with counters on a non-creature` or never matched. Behind them sit 152 self
remove-counter activations (`{2}, {T}, Remove a charge counter from this artifact: Draw a card.`), 58 with a vocabulary
payload, whose COST the engine has charged since D319 and the row maker read since D447 - the entry line was the only
thing keeping them from the generator.

### The generator

- **`make-rows168.cjs`**: the entry reader takes any count word or digit and any kind (`+1/+1`, `-1/-1`, or a lowercase
  word); the P/T kinds keep their creature guard, a named kind rides any permanent - the generated ReplacementDef
  already wrote `CountersChanged` of the kind. **A kind the RULES give a meaning is refused** (`RULES_COUNTERS`: the
  keyword counters of CR 122.1c, shield 122.1i, stun 122.1j, finality, loyalty, defense, level, lore, time, fade, age,
  depletion): the engine reads none of them off `counters`, and an entry replacement putting a shield counter would be a
  claim over a rule nobody runs (D90) - five shield cards stayed out by name.
- **`gen-oneshot168.cjs`**: the entry assert reads the count and, on a creature, a base the named counters do not move;
  under a counted static on the same card (Trawler Drake, `+1/+1 for each oil counter`) the P/T assert is left to that
  static's own suite. D447's entry-covers seeding pays the remove-counter cost off the entry counters.

### The wave — 17 rows, 57 tests, green on the second port

The first port's one miss was Trawler Drake's P/T under its own counted static. Engine regression 156 files / 15,781
green; bot / net / ui 301 green; leftover diff 17 newly complete, 0 regressed. No fuzz change.

What the 87 leave behind: the shield counters (8 - a rule the engine does not carry), the conditional entries (`if you
cast it from your hand` 11, the kicked and modified conditions), the six with no mana cost the test cannot cast, the
`enters tapped with two charge counters` lands (the tapped-and-counters pair), the X and per-count forms on artifacts,
and the consumers outside the vocabulary (`Put a storage counter on this land`, the storage lands' X mana, `It deals 1
damage to any target` under a remove-counter cost - the referent).

### Traps

- **A COUNTER KIND IS A RULE BEFORE IT IS A NAME**: shield, stun, the keyword counters, lore, time and their kin do
  something by the rules the moment they sit on a permanent; a generic entry replacement must refuse them by name,
  because `counters['shield']` in the state is not a shield.
- **A NAMED ENTRY COUNTER UNDER A COUNTED STATIC MOVES THE BASE THROUGH THE STATIC**: the entry assert on P/T is the
  counted static's to make, or the two suites contradict each other on the same board.

passed / 11 skipped · 500-seed gate, 6 shards, 536.2 s wall · build clean · probe
124/124 · battery 141/141.**

## D469 — THE SHIELD COUNTER: CR 122.1i as an engine rule — the damage prevented in the funnel, the destruction replaced at the three destroy sites, the counter spent; the vocabulary puts it (2026-09-16)

**11,001 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 10,992
(+9: 7 rows — Proud Pack-Rhino, Swooping Protector, Brokers Veteran, Wingshield Agent, Disciplined Duelist, Rhox
Pummeler, Dapper Shieldmate — and two spells the vocabulary now reads whole, Boon of Safety and Protection Magic).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,170 → **7,177**. The REFUSED ledger stays **1,736**. Fixtures 7,982 → **7,989**. `scriptableToday`
**1,821**; the ladder `[1821, 1827, 3165, 4767, 6099]`. Bot reach **4,537** from **329**. An engine seam and a
generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — D468 refused it by name, and the refusal named the rule to build

D468's `RULES_COUNTERS` kept the shield counter out of the generic entry replacement because `counters['shield']` in
the state was not a shield: eight entry lines, the `put a shield counter on` payloads (ten sentences the vocabulary
refused for the same reason, D130's closed `CounterKind`) and the 28 lines naming the counter waited on one rule. CR
122.1i is two sentences with two homes the engine already had: the prevention funnel (D368/D382/D427) and the
destroy sites the regeneration shield taught (D330/D383).

### The engine seam (`apply-shield-1..4.cjs`)

- **`prevention.ts withoutPreventedDamage`**: the gate learns a third reason to walk (a damaged permanent carrying a
  shield counter); every entry to such a permanent is prevented whole and ONE counter is spent per damage BODY however
  many entries hit it (a double block is one event, one counter) - `shieldsLeft` carries the count across the batch so
  a second body in the same batch spends the next; the counter comes off as `CountersChanged shield -1` behind the
  body, narrated.
- **`effects.ts`**: the targeted destroy and the sweep remove a counter instead, after indestructible and after a
  regeneration shield (the affected controller's choice between the two replacements is not asked - regeneration
  first, as the older shape).
- **`sba.ts`**: lethal damage met by a shield counter is the `shielded` action - the counter removed, the damage STILL
  MARKED, the next pass asks again (a counter put after lethal damage is spent and the creature still dies, exactly as
  the rules have it).
- **The vocabulary**: `shield` joins `CounterKind` (`oracle.ts`) and `COUNTER_KIND` (`effectParse.ts`) - putting one
  is now a change the board shows, so the closed-list rule that kept charge counters out keeps its reason.
- **`shieldCounter.test.ts`**: a Bolt prevented and the counter spent, the next Bolt lethal; two counters two Bolts;
  a double block one counter; Infernal Grasp and Wrath of God replaced per member; the SBA loop on the Giant Spider;
  the replay hash.

### The generator

- `shield` leaves `RULES_COUNTERS` (the entry rows read); a condition on the card's OWN counter that its entry counters
  already meet (Rhox Pummeler's `trample as long as it has a shield counter`) is staged broken first - the counter
  removed by hand, then put back (D398's rule, decided after the entry line is known); the entry assert leaves the P/T
  to a conditional self static the armed board meets (Dapper Shieldmate's `+2/+0 during your turn`).

### The wave — 7 rows, 18 tests, green on the second port

Engine regression 157 files / 15,802 green; bot / net / ui / data 920 green; leftover diff 9 newly complete, 0
regressed. Fuzz: a Disciplined Duelist a seat; `shieldCountersPut` 2 / `shieldCountersSpent` 0 at 150 seeds (the
two-colour two-drop and the driver's random aim - reported, no floor).

What the 28 leave behind: the counter that moves (Diamond City), the copies (Undercover Operative), the riders
(Family's Favor's until-end-of-turn, Captain America's scoped static), the loyalty ability, the multi-kind entry
(Agent's Toolkit), the noncommander target (Shield Broker).

### Traps

- **ONE DAMAGE EVENT, ONE COUNTER, HOWEVER MANY ENTRIES**: the funnel spends per BODY, not per entry, and carries the
  count across the batch - a per-entry spend would strip two counters from a double block.
- **THE SBA REPLACEMENT LEAVES THE DAMAGE MARKED**: the shield counter replaces the destruction, not the damage that
  caused it; the next pass destroys unless another counter stands, which is the rule and not a loop bug.
- **A VOCABULARY KIND IS ADMITTED THE DAY THE ENGINE READS IT**: `CounterKind` grew from two to three for the reason it
  was two.

passed / 11 skipped · 500-seed gate, 6 shards, 534.1 s wall · build clean · probe
124/124 · battery 141/141.**

## D470 — THE STUN COUNTER: CR 122.1j as an engine built-in over the untap, `stun` in the vocabulary, and the counter put ON a referent (2026-09-16)

**11,021 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,001
(+20: 13 rows — Referee Squad, Alchemax Slayer-Bots, Rowdy Snowballers, Collector's Case, Frostfist Strider, Utrom
Scientists, Cryogen Relic, Shipwreck Patrol, Ice Flan, Fractal Mascot, Grappling Kraken, Waylaying Pirates, Petrifying
Meddler — and seven spells the vocabulary now reads whole: Miraculous Recovery, Freeze in Place, Impede Momentum,
Tranquilize, Big Play, Puncture Bolt, Stunning Shot).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,177 → **7,190**. The REFUSED ledger 1,736 →
**1,740** (the mirror offered four the row maker refused, ledgered by reason). Fixtures 7,989 → **8,002** (7,829 by name
+ 173 tokens). `scriptableToday` 1,821 → **1,827**; the ladder `[1827, 1833, 3171, 4748, 6080]`. Bot reach **4,540** from
**329**. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — D468's list named it, D469 built its sibling

`RULES_COUNTERS` kept the stun counter out for the same reason as the shield: `counters['stun']` in the state was not a
stun. The wide dump holds 69 stun lines - `tap target creature an opponent controls and put a stun counter on it` under
eleven entry heads, the `up to one` and `two counters` variants, three tapped-entry lines. CR 122.1j is one sentence with
one home: the untap. The vocabulary's half turned out to be the larger find - the sentence is TWO clauses whose second
puts a counter ON THE FIRST'S TARGET, and neither the referent reader (D392) nor the trigger bridge (D373) read that.

### The engine seam (`apply-stun-1..4.cjs`)

- **`triggers.ts withStunCounters`**: a built-in over `PermanentsUntapped` in `applyReplacements` - every card in the
  untap that carries a stun counter is held back and loses one (`CountersChanged stun -1`, narrated), the rest untap as
  the event said; the untap step's batch and an untap effect meet the same rule.
- **The vocabulary**: `stun` joins `CounterKind` / `COUNTER_KIND` (the day the engine reads it, D469's rule); and
  **`REFERENT_COUNTER`** - `put a <kind> counter on it` after a targeted clause is rewritten to the previous clause's
  phrase, as the verbs of `REFERENT_OBJECT` are: `Tap target creature an opponent controls and put a stun counter on
  it.` reads as a tap and a counter on the same target (D426's conjunction, D392's referent), and so does `Return target
  creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield. Put a +1/+1 counter on it.` (Miraculous Recovery).
- **The trigger bridge** (`scripts/vocabulary.ts recipientAsSelf`): a trailing `on it.` is the payload's RECIPIENT only
  when no target phrase precedes it; after one, `it` is that target. The blanket rewrite would have put the stun counter
  on the SOURCE - caught by the first port (every stun suite read 0 on the Cyclops), never shipped.
- **`stunCounter.test.ts`**: two counters sit out two untap steps and untap on the third; an untapped stunned creature
  keeps its counter; Ornamental Courage's untap spends one; the replay hash.

### The generator

- `stun` leaves `RULES_COUNTERS`; a block proof (`can't be blocked`, the predicates, the counts) beside a payload that
  taps the opponent's creature is refused (Gilded Scuttler: the entry taps and stuns the Cyclops, the engine skips the
  declare-blockers prompt with no untapped blocker, and the walk runs the game out - the first port's one miss).

### The wave — 13 rows, 29 tests, green on the second port

Engine regression 158 files / 15,832 green; bot / net / ui / data 920 green; leftover diff 20 newly complete, 0
regressed. Fuzz: a Rowdy Snowballers a seat; `stunCountersPut` / `stunCountersSpent` 6 / 6 at 60 seeds, 12 / 11 at 150 -
the floor `stunCountersSpent > 0` at gate size (the staple must be a ROWED card: Deluge Virtuoso is no fixture).

What the 69 leave behind: the tapped entries (`enters tapped with six stun counters` - the tapped-and-counters pair),
the counted forms (`tap X target creatures`, `up to two`, `each of them`), the Sagas and the loyalty abilities, Fear of
Sleep Paralysis's `can't be removed` static, the riders (Dreamdew Entrancer, Kitnap).

### Traps

- **`on it.` AFTER A TARGET IS THE TARGET, NOT THE SOURCE**: the trigger bridge's recipient rewrite must look for a
  target phrase before it; a suite that reads the counter on the wrong permanent is the only thing that catches it.
- **A FUZZ STAPLE MUST BE A FIXTURE THE WAVE SHIPPED**: the staples table resolves names in the fixture oracle; a card
  with the right text but a second unread line is no fixture and fails the canary at once.
- **A BLOCK PROOF BESIDE A TAP OF THE OPPONENT'S BLOCKER WALKS THE GAME OUT**: the declare-blockers prompt is skipped
  with no legal blocker, and the walk that waits for it never returns.

## D471 — THE KEYWORD COUNTER: CR 122.1c read by `derive` at layer 6, the enforced kinds in the vocabulary, and the card's own cycle as a head (2026-09-16)

**11,035 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,021
(+14: 9 rows — Avenging Huntbonder, Void Beckoner, Windcaller Aven, Splendor Mare, Mai, Jaded Edge, Titanoth Rex, Vizier
of Tumbling Sands, Sanctuary Smasher, Avian Oddity — and five spells the vocabulary now reads whole: Fully Grown, Sudden
Spinnerets, Spontaneous Flight, Heightened Reflexes, Wing It).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,190 → **7,199**. The REFUSED ledger
1,740 → **1,738** (Windcaller Aven and Vizier of Tumbling Sands were ledgered under the cycle head the library lacked;
the stale-entry guard named them). Fixtures 8,002 → **8,011**. `scriptableToday` 1,827 → **1,825**; the ladder
`[1825, 1831, 3169, 4734, 6066]`. Bot reach **4,547** from **330**. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — the last counter kind with a rule the engine had not built

D468's `RULES_COUNTERS` named the keyword counters with the shield and the stun; D469 and D470 built those two. The
wide dump holds 101 keyword-counter lines (flying 28, indestructible 24, lifelink 9, deathtouch 8, vigilance 7, trample
7, menace 5 ...): `put a lifelink counter on target creature you control`, `enters with a menace counter`, the Ikoria
mentors and the Aetherdrift Hunt cards. CR 122.1c is one sentence with one home - `derive` - and the vocabulary's half
was the same widening D469 and D470 made twice. Behind five of the payloads sat a head the library lacked - `When you
cycle this card` - whose fire is the engine's own cycling from the hand (D306), so it came along.

### The engine seam (`apply-kwc-1..2.cjs`)

- **`derive.ts`**: at layer 6, beside the until-end-of-turn grants, every counter whose kind is an enforced keyword's
  printed word (`KEYWORD_COUNTERS`: flying, first strike → `firstStrike`, double strike, deathtouch, hexproof,
  indestructible, lifelink, menace, reach, trample, vigilance, shadow) adds that keyword - an ADDITION, like every
  shipped layer-6 effect; `finish()` still clears it under a lose-all-abilities effect (Humility), and a kind the
  engine does not enforce (exalted, decayed) stays inert.
- **The vocabulary**: those words join `CounterKind` (`COUNTER_KINDS` is the one list; `counterKindOf` gates on it)
  and `COUNTER_KIND` (two of them with a space), so `put a flying counter on target creature you control` and `Put a
  trample counter on ~` read.
- **`keywordCounter.test.ts`**: a flying counter is flying and a first strike counter is first strike; removed, the
  keyword goes; an exalted counter grants nothing; Humility takes it away with the rest; the replay hash.

### The generator

- **`cycleThisCard`** - `When you cycle this card, P`: a head over the card's own cycling move (`m.reason ===
  'cycling'`, D377), looked back at from the HAND; the row carries the printed cycling cost, the card starts in hand
  with the cast-this-spell rows, and the fire cycles it (`cyclingIndex`, the helper D306's `youCycle` suites already
  emit). The hand baseline needs no adjustment: the card leaves, the cycling draws.
- `RULES_COUNTERS` keeps only the kinds the engine still does not read; the entry reader takes the two-word kinds.

### The wave — 9 rows, 19 tests, green on the first port

Engine regression 159 files / 15,854 green; bot / net / ui / data 920 green; leftover diff 14 newly complete, 0
regressed. No fuzz change (the keyword counters ride `CountersChanged` like every other kind).

What the 101 leave behind: the `your choice of a flying counter or a reach counter` entries (5 - a prompt), the
`non-Human creature you control` targets (5 - a negated subtype in the target reader), the `remove a menace counter
from it. When you do ...` payloads (a referent under a combat-damage head with a reflexive trigger), the Dominus
counters (indestructible counters put by a Phyrexian-mana cost), the Sagas and the loyalty abilities, the counted
`each creature you control` recipient.

### Traps

- **A KEYWORD COUNTER IS AN ABILITY, NOT A KEYWORD PRINTED**: it is added at layer 6 and it goes with the abilities
  under Humility - reading it in layer 1 beside the printed keywords would have kept a flying counter flying on a
  creature that has lost all abilities.
- **THE CARD'S OWN CYCLE FIRES FROM THE HAND, AND THE HEAD LOOKS BACK**: the cost has moved the card before the bus
  asks; `activeZones: ['hand']` with `looksBack` is the whole trick, and the row starts in hand like a spell it casts.

## D472 — THE LOYALTY ABILITY: CR 606 in the engine — the counters as the cost, once a turn per permanent, at sorcery speed — and the first four planeswalkers (2026-09-16)

**11,040 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,035
(+5: 4 rows — Jace Beleren, Kiora, Behemoth Beckoner, Sarkhan Vol, Vivien of the Arkbow — and Jace Beleren's
two-faced printing, which shares the oracle).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,199 → **7,203**. The REFUSED ledger 1,738 →
**1,733** (the five `planeswalker loyalty ability` entries were the class this seam drains; the stale-entry guard named
them). Fixtures 8,011 → **8,015**. `scriptableToday` 1,825 → **1,820**; the ladder `[1820, 1826, 3164, 4729, 6061]`.
Bot reach **4,548** from **330**. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### Chosen for the app, not the count — nobody could activate a loyalty ability

D471 left the residue flat (every family 5–35 cards). Under it sat a rule with no home: `activatedParse` made every
loyalty cost unpayable ("it needs once-per-turn tracking and a counter cost that do not exist"), `legal.ts` never
offered one, and 296 planeswalkers in the leftover — 4,529 numeric loyalty lines across the database — were Tier 3
in the hand of a human and dead in the bot's. The seam is small (CR 606 is four sentences), the counters and the
per-turn activation record already existed, and the yield is honest: four planeswalkers whose every line reads today,
and every other planeswalker's ability CHARGED correctly from now on, with the note saying the effect is the player's.

### The engine seam (`apply-loy-1..2.cjs`)

- **`activatedParse.ts`**: the loyalty cost reads as a signed number (`+2`, `−3`, `0`; `−` normalised) into
  `loyaltyCost`; the ability is `payable` when the number is known (an `X` cost stays unpaid) and `sorceryOnly` by rule
  (CR 606.3). `OracleFace`'s ability carries `loyaltyCost?: number`.
- **`legal.ts`**: a loyalty ability is offered once a turn per PERMANENT (`turn.activations[`${id}|loyalty`]` — the key
  is the permanent, not the ability, 606.3) and a negative cost only with the counters to pay it (606.5); the sorcery
  timing rides `sorceryOnly`.
- **`handlers.ts`**: the two refusals (`timingRestriction` "has activated a loyalty ability this turn already",
  `cannotAfford` "too few loyalty counters"), and the cost is the counters themselves — a `CountersChanged` of
  `loyaltyCost` on the source as the ability goes on the stack; the stack object carries `loyalty` so the reducer's
  `recordActivation` counts the permanent's turn (`${source}|loyalty`) beside the ability's own key.
- **`tier3.ts`**: a payable loyalty ability takes the charged-for-nothing note by its cost (`Its “+1” ability`) until a
  row runs it; only an unreadable cost keeps the M5 note.
- **`loyalty.test.ts`**: the parse (three costs as numbers, X unpaid); Jace Beleren +2 lands on 5 and a second loyalty
  ability the same turn is refused and unoffered; −1 the next turn with a target, then the counters run out for a
  second −1; sorcery speed on the opponent's turn; the replay hash.

### The generator

- `parseCost` takes a loyalty piece (`out.loyalty`; X refuses); `ACTIVATED_START` admits `+N:` / `−N:` lines; the
  planeswalker refusal is gone; `limits.oncePerTurn` for a loyalty row; `loyaltyBoost` = the counters the fixture must
  add first when a negative cost exceeds the printed loyalty; rows carry `loyaltyBase`; the suite asserts the counters
  after the fire (`loyaltyBase + boost + cost`).

### The wave — 4 rows, 16 tests, green on the first port

Engine regression 160 files / 15,867 green; bot / net / ui / data 920 green; leftover diff 5 newly complete, 0
regressed. The fuzz: Jace Beleren a staple (two a seat), `loyaltyActivations` counted off `AbilityPutOnStack` objects
carrying `loyalty`, read **21 at 60 seeds and 53 at 150** — floored.

What the 296 leave behind: the emblems (65 — `You get an emblem with "..."`: a player-owned object the engine has
no zone for), the ultimates generally (the `search`, `exile all`, `extra turn`, `each opponent` payloads outside the
vocabulary), the static lines on the newer walkers (`As long as ~ has N or more loyalty counters`), the
planeswalker-as-creature statics (Gideon), the `−X` costs, the `Look at the top N` ultimates, and the emblem-free
walkers whose three abilities still need three vocabularies at once (a row completes only when EVERY line reads).

### Traps

- **THE LOYALTY COST IS THE COUNTERS, CHARGED AS THE ABILITY GOES ON THE STACK**: it is a `CountersChanged` in the
  cost batch, not an effect — a `+1` on a walker at 0 counters is legal (CR 606.5 only refuses a NEGATIVE cost it cannot
  pay), and the SBA (704.5i, `sba.ts` since M5) sees the counters after the cost, so a `−3` at exactly 3 sends the
  walker to the graveyard with the ability still on the stack — the rule as printed; untested by this wave.
- **ONCE A TURN IS PER PERMANENT, NOT PER ABILITY**: the record's key is `${id}|loyalty`, so a `+2` bars the `−1`
  the same turn; the ability's own `${id}|${index}` key is still recorded beside it.
- **A PAYABLE LOYALTY ABILITY WITH NO DEF IS CHARGED FOR NOTHING** — exactly the Krenko precedent (D122): tier3's
  `fourOrMore` pin jumped 24 → 99 because every un-rowed walker now carries one note per ability.

## D473 — THE QUOTED TOKEN: a description that quotes the printing's own rules text, folded before the scrub, keyed and matched exactly, and baked only when the token's ability runs (2026-09-17)

**11,067 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,040
(+27: 21 rows — the Eldrazi Spawn and Scion makers, Nest Invader, Brood Monitor, Emrakul's Hatcher, Kozilek's Predator,
Eyeless Watcher, Blisterpod, Carrier Thrall, Awakening Zone, Pawn of Ulamog, Spawn-Gang Commander among them — and six
spells the vocabulary now reads whole: Call the Scions, Skittering Invasion, Corpsehatch, Spawning Breath, Essence
Feed, Unfathomable Truths).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,203 → **7,224**. The REFUSED ledger stays at **1,733** (the select
offered nothing new). Fixtures 8,015 → **8,039** (the two token printings, Call the Scions, the wave). `TOKEN_TABLE`
400 → **405** keys. `scriptableToday` **1,820**; the ladder `[1820, 1826, 3164, 4729, 6034]`. Bot reach **4,559**
from **330**. An engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — one blocker under 202 lines

The residue after D472 is flat (every payload shape under the library heads reads 2–10 cards; 2,137 payloads over
1,898 shapes). The one coherent family left was the QUOTED TOKEN: 202 leftover lines create a token whose rules text
is not a keyword, printed in quotes — `create a 0/1 colorless Eldrazi Spawn creature token with "Sacrifice this token:
Add {C}."`, `tokens. They have "…"`, `with trample and "…"` — 90 rows with nothing else unread (Eldrazi Spawn 20, Scion
15, Pest 6, Mercenary 5, Rat 4, Pilot 4 …). `scrub` has always blanked the quote before the token parser saw it, so
every such description arrived as a token with a run of spaces where its ability was, and was refused by the Dragon
Egg rule (D133) — correctly, since nothing could say which token it was. The quote IS the answer: it is the printing's
own text.

### The engine seam (`apply-qt-1..6.cjs`)

- **`foldTokenQuotes`** (`tokenParse.ts`): the three printed shapes fold to one clause BEFORE any scrub — `token with
  #qN#.`, `token with flying and #qN#.` — the quote lifted out verbatim into a list; a quote anywhere else is left for
  `scrub` as before. `parseTokenClause(sentence, quotes)` reads the mark back as `TokenSpec.quoted` (a mark with no
  quote behind it, or not last, refuses; the scrubbed run of spaces still refuses); `specKey` carries it as a sixth
  field (`|q=<text>`), every plain key byte-identical.
- **`matchToken`**: a quoted spec matches the printing whose NON-KEYWORD text equals the quote — exact, reminder text
  aside, and the self-reference read as one word: the printing says `this creature` where the newer card quotes `this
  token` (CR 111.4 — the card's wording is the token's; one object). The keyword lines still compare as a set.
- **`effectParse`**: `parseEffectsInner` folds first — before `selfRef`, which would rewrite the quote — and the quotes
  ride beside `SPELL_X` for the length of one parse; the token rule reads them back. The vocabulary's
  `recipientAsSelf` rewrites OUTSIDE the quotes only (the anchored forms on the opening span).
- **The bake** (`tokenTable.node.test.ts`): the quotes travel beside each clause (a mark is numbered per face), and a
  quoted description is baked ONLY when the printing it names is `engineCompleteness`-complete — the quote is the
  CARD'S text, so D90 asks that it run. Five do (the Eldrazi Scion and Spawn, the Elf Druid, the Human Monk, the red
  Wizard — all mana abilities the mana path runs by parse and D325 charges); fifty resolve to a printing and stay
  refused: a Pest whose dies trigger nothing fires, a Rat whose `can't block` nothing enforces, a 0/0 Construct whose
  pump nothing derives.
- **`quotedToken.test.ts`**: Call the Scions resolves by itself into two named Scions, a Scion is sacrificed for {C}
  as printed, the replay hash; `tokenParse.test.ts` proves the fold, the read-back, the key, the match and its two
  refusals.

### The generator

- The row maker re-reads a leftover ending `with` from the printed line the way D454 re-reads `has` / `have` — quote
  and all — and the harvester asks the vocabulary for the whole printed payload; the vocab path pins the token
  printings the rows create (D431's step). A cast-this-spell row whose payload counts the board reads one more: the
  spell itself resolves after its trigger (Spawn-Gang Commander).

### The wave — 21 rows, 48 tests

The first, ungated port rowed 46: Digsite Engineer's 0/0 Construct died on arrival (its `+1/+1 for each artifact`
runs nowhere) and five suites read one token short — D90 with a body on it — which is what put the completeness gate
on the bake; 24 rows were unported and the 21 that remain are the ones whose token really works. Engine regression
161 files / 15,911 green; bot / net / ui / data 924 green; leftover diff 27 newly complete, 0 regressed. The fuzz:
Nest Invader a staple, `spawnTokensMade` / `spawnTokensSpent` **2 / 2 at 60 seeds, 14 / 8 at 150** — floored.

What the 202 leave behind: the fifty quoted printings the engine does not run — the dies triggers (Pest, Devil, Imp,
Ooze, Boar), the can't-block and can-block-only statics (Rat, Fungus, Satyr, Pirate, Robot, Drone, Faerie), the
Mercenary's sorcery-speed pump, the Pilot's crew, the Construct's count — each a TOKEN PRINTING the generator could row
like a card (the printing has an oracle id and text; a def on it would make the token complete and its makers read),
the natural next step; the counted descriptions (`that many`, `X`), the `for each` counts, the `Those tokens have`
form after a count sentence (Glimpse the Impossible), the tokens with a name (`named …`), the copies.

### Traps

- **THE QUOTE IS THE CARD'S TEXT, SO IT MUST RUN**: a quoted description is baked only when the printing is
  engine-complete. Digsite Engineer proved it the expensive way — a 0/0 whose pump nothing derives is binned by the
  state-based action the moment it lands, and the suite read the board one short.
- **FOLD BEFORE THE SCRUB AND BEFORE THE SELF REWRITE**: `selfRef` and `recipientAsSelf` both rewrite `this creature`,
  and the quote contains it; lifted out first, the quote is untouched and the rewrite runs outside it only.
- **THE PRINTING SAYS `this creature`, THE CARD `this token`**: Scryfall's token oracle keeps the older self-reference;
  the comparison reads every self-reference as one word, the key keeps the card's wording verbatim.
- **A MARK IS NUMBERED PER FACE**: the bake carries the quotes beside each clause, so two faces' `#q0#` never meet
  in one key.
- **THE LINES PROBE READS THE LIVE TREE**: a row already ported reads as complete (no leftover), so a re-run of the wave
  chain after a port must reuse the pre-port dump — the wide run's rows served here.

## D474 — ROW THE TOKEN PRINTINGS: a token's own text as a generated script, the ceased token's trigger aimed by last known information, and the makers behind them (2026-09-17)

**11,101 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,067
(+34: 22 rows — the Pest, Rat, Mercenary, Devil, Pilot, Construct and Wizard makers: Sedgemoor Witch, Digsite Engineer,
Urza, Chief Artificer, Lord Skitter, Sewer King, The Prydwen, Steel Flagship, Voracious Vermin, Wanted Griffin, Chocobo
Racetrack among them — and twelve spells the vocabulary now reads whole: Pest Summoning, Dance with Devils, Song of
Totentanz, Devils' Playground, Form a Posse, Wolf's Quarry, Gysahl Greens, Choco-Comet, Into the Fae Court, Mourner's
Surprise, Make Mischief, Lindblum, Industrial Regency // Mage Siege).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,224 → **7,277** (31 TOKEN
PRINTINGS and 22 makers). The REFUSED ledger stays at **1,733**. Fixtures 8,039 → **8,110** (49 token pins, the wave,
Mana-Charged Dragon). `TOKEN_TABLE` 405 → **437** keys (37 quoted). `scriptableToday` **1,820**; the ladder `[1820,
1826, 3164, 4729, 6000]`. Bot reach **4,569** from **333**. A generator wave, an engine seam and a fuzz seam on Opus 5.

### D473 named it — fifty token printings the engine did not run

D473 baked a quoted token description only when the printing it names is engine-complete, and five were: the mana
tokens. The other fifty resolved and stayed refused — a Pest whose dies trigger nothing fired, a Rat whose `can't
block` nothing enforced, a 0/0 Construct whose pump nothing derived — and behind them 130 makers. A token printing is
a card in every way the generator cares about: an oracle id, a printed text, a fixture by set and collector number.
So the row maker rows it, the def claims its line, `engineCompleteness(printing)` holds, the bake admits the
description, and the makers read.

### The generator (`apply-gen-3..5.cjs`, `zz-token-pool474.node.test.ts`)

- **The token mode**: `CRT_TOKENS` names the pool (the printings the quoted descriptions name that the engine does
  not run, with their makers and leftover lines), keyed by PRINTING id like the lines dump; a row carries `token:
  { printingId, constKey }` and a unique module (`pestToken1ae25997`); the printing's `this token` is read as `this
  creature` for parsing (the heads and the vocabulary know that word) while `printed` stays verbatim for the claim.
- **The token arm**: the fixture const is the pin's (`PEST_1AE25997_TOKEN`), never the name's; the token is never
  dealt or put — it is CREATED by `ManualCreateToken` where a card is put, late for a step head (the Spirit's draw
  counter would otherwise see turn 3's draw); a sacrificed or dead token is ABSENT (CR 704.5d), so the graveyard
  assert reads its absence; `put` is imported only when used.
- **The makers' suites register their tokens' scripts** (`token-scripts474.json`): the Construct's own count pump is
  what keeps the 0/0 on the board the suite counts — the game's registry holds both, and so must the suite's; a token
  under a paid payload (`You may pay {2}. If you do, create …`) is found in the branches. A cast-instant fire (the
  Ritual) adds no permanent to the board assert.
- 31 token printings rowed (dies triggers, attack triggers, the landfall Bird, the noncreature-cast Wizard, the
  can't-block and blocks-only-flying statics, the Mercenary's sorcery-speed pump, the Skeleton's regenerate, the
  Dragon's pump, the Construct's count, the Human Knight's threshold, the must-attack Alien, the Fish and Ninja
  evasion, the Beast's alone restriction); 18 refused by reason (the Pilots' crew, the Spirit's block restriction,
  the Assassins, the Cleric's named return, the Dragon Spirit's damage head, the Illusions, the Nightmares, the
  Warrior, the Wolf, the Elemental's named return, the Goblin's scope, the Horse's grant — and the Ooze, whose
  `Create two 1/1 green Ooze creature tokens` reads its own name as `~`).

### The engine seam (`apply-lki-1..2.cjs`) — a ceased token's trigger aims by last known information

The Devil's `When this token dies, it deals 1 damage to any target` found its source DELETED by the time the trigger
was put on the stack — `TokensCeased` (CR 704.5d) removes the instance — and `targetingSourceFor` returned null, so CR
603.3d removed the trigger as if it had no legal target. A TOKEN's pending trigger now carries `lki` (its printing and
face), the `chooseTargets` prompt carries it on, and the aim, the answer handler, the fuzz driver and the harness read
the face from it when the instance is gone (CR 603.10). A card's trigger is unchanged: no field, the same hash.

### The fuzz seam (`apply-fuzz-1..3.cjs`)

A token printing's script is registered like any other and NEVER DEALT — a token is not a library card, and a name
shared with a card (`Wizard`) would deal the wrong thing: `SCRIPTED_SORTED` skips the oracles whose layout is `token`.
`tokenTriggersFired` counts a created token's own triggered ability put on the stack: **1 at 60 seeds, 5 at 150**
before the staple; a Chocobo Racetrack a seat (each land drop makes a Bird whose own landfall pump fires on the next)
read 2 / 6 — reported, not floored (thin). Spawn made / spent 3 / 2 and 18 / 10.

### The wave — 31 token rows (65 tests) + 22 maker rows (52 tests)

Engine regression 161 files / 16,017 green; bot / net / ui / data 924 green (tier3.test's ability-word post passed
from Sedgemoor Witch, shipped, to Mana-Charged Dragon); leftover diff 34 newly complete, 0 regressed.

What is left: the 18 refused printings (each holds its makers: the Pilots 11, the Spirit 7, the Illusions 3, the
Ooze 3), the makers with a second unread line (~80 of the 130), the counted and named descriptions, the copies.

### Traps

- **A TOKEN'S DIES TRIGGER AIMS BY LAST KNOWN INFORMATION**: the instance is gone before the aim; the pending trigger
  and the prompt carry the printing, and `targetingSourceFor` reads it when `state.cards[source]` is undefined.
- **A TOKEN IS A SCRIPT, NEVER DEALT**: the fuzz derives its rotating pool from the shipped list minus the token
  oracles; the L1 theorem covers the cards alone.
- **THE MAKER'S SUITE REGISTERS ITS TOKENS' SCRIPTS**: a 0/0 Construct under a suite that knows only the maker dies
  on arrival and reads the board one short — the first port of D473 said so before this decision existed.
- **`this token` IS `this creature` FOR PARSING, VERBATIM FOR THE CLAIM**: the heads and the vocabulary know one
  word; the def's text is the printing's own line.
- **A TOKEN ROW IS CREATED, LATE FOR A STEP HEAD, AND ABSENT WHEN IT LEAVES**: `ManualCreateToken` by printing id,
  after the walk for a draw or upkeep head, `toBeUndefined()` where a card reads `graveyard`.
- **A CAST-INSTANT FIRE ADDS NO PERMANENT**: the Ritual resolves and goes; the board reads the payload alone.

passed / 11 skipped · 500-seed gate, 6 shards, 560.2 s wall · build clean · probe
