## D475 — THE EMBLEM: an object in the command zone with the emblem printing's abilities, the walkers' ultimates read against a baked table, the emblem printings rowed like tokens — and the up-to-N and alternative-list clauses the suite stages now (2026-09-17)

**11,125 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,101
(+24 rows: two planeswalkers whose every line reads with their emblem — Vivien Reid, Ajani, Adversary of Tyrants — and
22 cards the suite could not stage before: Reveillark, Krosan Restorer, Angelic Quartermaster, Daily Bugle Reporters,
Agonasaur Rex, Scrap Compactor, Kitesail Cleric, Soul of Innistrad, Tempest Owl, Captain America's Motorcycle among
them).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,277 → **7,314** (13 EMBLEM PRINTINGS and 24 rows). The REFUSED ledger 1,733 → **1,716**
(seventeen entries the guard named — the up-to-N and alternative-list clauses — retired). Fixtures 8,110 → **8,150**.
`EMBLEM_TABLE` **13** keys. `scriptableToday` 1,820 → **1,803**; the ladder `[1803, 1809, 3147, 4712, 5982]`. Bot
reach **4,583** from **334**. An engine seam, a generator wave and a fuzz seam on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — 78 emblem lines, the last structural family outside copy

After D474 the residue was flat again; the emblem was the largest coherent family left (78 leftover lines `You get an
emblem with "…"` on 72 planeswalkers; the database carries 138 emblem records - `Emblem — Gideon`, "Creatures you
control get +1/+1."). D473 and D474 said how: the quote is the printing's own text, the printing is rowed like a card,
the bake admits the description only when the printing is engine-complete. The walkers' other lines are what they
are - a walker completes only when EVERY line reads - so the wave's walker count is honest and small, and the seam's
value is the OBJECT: an emblem in the command zone whose anthem and triggers the engine runs.

### The engine seam (`apply-emb-1..4.cjs`)

- **The object**: `EmblemCreated { card, oracleId, printingId, owner }` puts a card instance into its owner's COMMAND
  zone (CR 114.1) - no permanent, never castable (`castAction` refuses a non-commander there), never ceasing;
  `ManualCreateEmblem` is the Tier-3 tool and the harness's hand.
- **The abilities**: `staticSourcesFor` walks each player's command zone after the battlefield, taking a def that
  declares `command` among its active zones (an emblem's script does; a commander's never); the trigger bus already
  honoured `activeZones` per instance, so an emblem's `StepBegan` trigger fires from the command zone unchanged.
- **The vocabulary**: `foldTokenQuotes` folds `You get an emblem with "Q"` to `You get an emblem with #qN#.`; the
  `createEmblem` rule reads the mark against `EMBLEM_TABLE` (the printing on `token`), and `effects.ts` emits
  `EmblemCreated` for the controller. `tokenPrintingIdsIn` names the emblem printings beside the tokens, so a game's
  pool holds them (D133's blank-token rule, one object over).
- **The bake** (`emblemTable.node.test.ts`): every quote a Commander-legal card prints, matched to the emblem record
  whose text is the quote (the self-reference `this emblem` and a trailing period aside), baked only when that record
  is engine-complete - D473's rule: the quote is the card's own text.
- **tier3** reads an emblem printing's text as a permanent's (its lines earn ability notes, never a spell's "Its
  effect"). `emblem.test.ts`: the fold, a baked emblem read and an unbaked one refused, the object in the command
  zone, the anthem from there (a Bears reads 3/3), the upkeep ping from there, the replay.

### The generator (`apply-gen-1..3.cjs`)

- **Emblem rows** in the token mode: the pool carries `zone: 'command'`, the fixture is the record by NAME (an emblem
  record's name is its walker's), `this emblem` reads as `this creature` for parsing, the suite gives the emblem by
  `ManualCreateEmblem` and finds it in the command zone, and every zone the module declares is `command`. Thirteen
  rowed (the anthems of Elspeth, Gideon, Garruk, Sorin, Vivien Reid, Domri Rade; the end-step tokens of Kiora and
  Ajani; the cast pings of Chandra ToD, Narset, Chandra Spark Hunter; Tezzeret BoF's draw; Venser's exile); Oko's
  `of the chosen type` refused by name (the type is the walker's choice, not the emblem's).
- **The suite stages two clauses it refused before**: a printed list whose alternatives differ is aimed at the first
  alternative some fixture satisfies, checked against ALL of that alternative's types (Vivien's `artifact, enchantment,
  or creature with flying`: a flier); an up-to-N clause with a minimum of 0 or 1 is aimed at ONE fixture (declaring one
  is a legal answer, every effect on it runs once). A once-a-turn activation whose payload ASKS (Vivien's look) is
  probed for the limit in the test, after the answer. A quoted loyalty line (`−8: You get an emblem with "…"`) is
  indexed by its scrubbed text, as the leftover reports it; `createEmblem` is asserted in the command zone.

### The wave — 13 emblem rows (26 tests) + 24 rows (61 tests)

Engine regression 162 files / 16,095 green; bot / net / ui / data 925 green; leftover diff 24 newly complete, 0
regressed. The fuzz: an emblem script is never dealt (layout `other` joins `token` outside the rotating pool);
`emblemsGiven` **0 at 60 and 150 seeds** (an ultimate is seven loyalty away; the driver activates whichever is offered),
reported.

What the 78 leave behind: 81 quotes with NO emblem record in the database (Koth, Fire of Resistance; Huatli, Radiant
Champion; Garruk, Caller of Beasts …) - an emblem's characteristics are its ability's (CR 114.3), so a synthesized
printing would be the honest answer, outside the DB-guarded fixtures; 45 emblem printings the row maker refused (the
hand-size and untap statics, the reach-through grants `Swamps you control have '{T}: Add {B}{B}{B}{B}'`, Jace's
counter, the copy emblems, the game-losing Vraska); the walkers whose other lines the vocabulary lacks (Elspeth's
`Destroy all creatures with power 4 or greater`, Gideon's animate, Teferi's tuck).

### Traps

- **AN EMBLEM'S ABILITIES ARE READ FROM THE COMMAND ZONE**: `staticSourcesFor` walks the command zone after the
  battlefield, and only a def declaring `command` is taken there - a commander's script declares none.
- **THE EMBLEM'S FIXTURE IS BY NAME, ITS SUITE'S SELF BY INTENT**: an emblem record's name is its walker's plus
  `Emblem`, unique; the suite gives it by `ManualCreateEmblem` and reads the command zone.
- **THE CHOSEN TYPE IS THE WALKER'S, NOT THE EMBLEM'S** (CR 114.3): Oko's emblem row would read its own `chosenType`
  as null - refused by name.
- **AN ALTERNATIVE'S TYPES ARE ALL-OF, THE CLAUSE'S ANY-OF**: the staged fixture is checked against every type of the
  alternative it serves.
- **A ONCE-A-TURN PROBE CANNOT RUN UNDER THE PAYLOAD'S OWN PROMPT**: the refusal would be the prompt's; an asking
  payload is probed after the answer.

**Verified: `verify.cjs --full` (sharded) — ALL FIVE GATES: 7535 files, 35893
passed / 11 skipped · 500-seed gate, 6 shards, 534.4 s wall · build clean · probe
124/124 · battery 141/141.**

## D476 — THE TRIGGER'S OWN NUMBER: a damage head memoises the damage its source dealt, the number rides the trigger onto the stack, and `that much` / `that many` in the payload reads it (2026-09-17)

**11,146 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,125
(+21 rows: Professor Hulk, Exalted Angel, Mourning Thrull, Glint-Eye Nephilim, Cold-Eyed Selkie, Olivia's Attendants,
Rapacious One, April, Reporter of the Weird, El-Hajjâj, Zebra Unicorn, Living Hive, Kjeldoran Gargoyle, Warrior Angel,
Towering-Wave Mystic, Crosstown Courier, Emberwilde Caliph, Horned Cheetah, Fear of Failed Tests, Mindscour Dragon,
Elsha, Threefold Master, Flayed Nim).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,314 → **7,335**. The REFUSED ledger 1,716 → **1,715**
(Mindscour Dragon, ledgered under the combat-damage-to-an-opponent head, retired by the guard). Fixtures 8,150 →
**8,171**. `scriptableToday` 1,803 → **1,802**; the ladder `[1802, 1808, 3146, 4711, 5977]`. Bot reach **4,589** from
**336**. An engine seam, a generator wave and a fuzz seam on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — 120 lines whose count is the event's own

After D475 the residue was flat; the densest bounded family left was the payload counted by its own head: 120 leftover
lines (57 sole rows) say `Whenever this creature deals (combat) damage (to a player | to an opponent | to a creature),
you gain that much life` / `draw that many cards` / `create that many <tokens>` / `target player mills that many
cards` / `you lose that much life`. The vocabulary read every one of those payloads with a NUMBER in it since D437's
spell X; what it could not read was a count the resolution cannot see - the damage the head's event dealt is gone by
the time the ability resolves (CR 603.2, the event; CR 608.2, the resolution). D440 had built exactly this plumbing for
a keyword (modular's counters, read off the pre-event state and carried as `PendingTrigger.memo` → `StackObject.memo`);
D476 opens it to scripts. The yield estimate was ~14 one-line rows; the wide run found 21.

### The engine seam (`apply-num-1.cjs`, `apply-num-2.cjs`)

- `TriggerDef.memo?: (ctx, self, ev) => number` (api.ts) - a number read off the EVENT as the trigger fires;
  triggers.ts stamps `memo: def.memo(ctx, id, event.body)` onto the pending trigger beside D474's `lki`; loop.ts
  carried a pending `memo` onto the stack object already (D440).
- `CountExpr { kind: 'memo' }` (oracle.ts); `countOf(..., xValue, memo)` (count.ts) returns `Math.max(0, memo)`;
  effects.ts passes `obj.memo ?? 0` beside `obj.xValue`.
- effectParse.ts: `HEAD_MEMO` (the caller's flag, as `SPELL_X` is), `substituteThatMuch` (`that many cards` → `a
  card`, `that much life` → `1 life`, `that much damage` → `1 damage`, `that many +1/+1 counters` → `a +1/+1 counter`,
  `-1/-1` likewise, `create that many <tokens>` → `create a <token>`), `matchThatMuch` chained after `matchSpellX`: the
  substituted base must read whole and be MULTIPLIABLE with no count of its own, and the spec keeps the printed text
  with `per: { kind: 'memo' }`. `parseEffects(text, name, isSpell, warn, xCost, memo = false)`;
  `vocabularyEffects(payload, name, { memo })` passes it through `recipientAsSelf`.
- `memoCount.test.ts` (2 tests): the vocabulary refuses `You gain that much life.` with no memo and reads it as
  `gainLife` × memo with one (`Sacrifice that many creatures.` stays refused either way); a Bears carrying the def
  attacks unblocked, deals 2, its controller gains 2 (the number, not one), `obj.memo` reads 2 off the log, the replay.

### The generator (`apply-gen-1..4.cjs`)

- make-rows176: two heads join - `dealsDamage` (`Whenever ~ deals damage,` - any damage) and `combatDamageOpponent`;
  both in the zero-power guard (the arm's unblocked attack deals the printed power - a 0-power creature's head cannot
  fire there). The count context carries `power`; a per-`memo` effect marks the row `memo`.
- gen176-vocab: `MEMO_HEADS` (the five damage heads + the two); a `memo` count is admitted under one of them on a
  creature with power ≥ 1 and refused elsewhere (`a that-much payload under a head with no number`); `countPlan.memoCount`
  is the power; `countN` returns it; the `VOCAB_` const emits `{ memo: true }`.
- gen-oneshot176: `dealsDamage` is TWO defs on one line, as `dealsDamagePlayer` is (D371's doubling) - combat damage is
  `CombatDamageDealt` and the rest `DamageDealt`, and the bus dispatches a def on its one event; the memo line reads
  the damage self dealt TO THE HEAD'S RECIPIENT (`memoRecipient`: a player, an opponent, a creature, anything).
- A latent D433 slip repaired: the discard queue's `else` that asserts `p1 was not in the scope` belonged to the
  `queueAsksP1` test (D398) and D433's inserted p2 line re-parented it onto `queueAsksP2` - a controller's own scoped
  discard (`draw that many cards, then discard a card`) asserted p1 discarded NOTHING. April's suite caught it; the
  regenerated D472–D475 waves are byte-identical (0 diffs).
- The token-pin guard reads a payload the way its module does: a `{ memo: true }` call site reads `that many` tokens.

### The wave — 21 rows (46 tests)

Ten under the any-damage head - seven `you gain that much life` (Exalted Angel, Mourning Thrull, El-Hajjâj, Zebra Unicorn,
Kjeldoran Gargoyle, Warrior Angel, Horned Cheetah), Emberwilde Caliph's `you lose that much life` beside its must-attack,
Olivia's Attendants' Blood tokens beside its own ping, Towering-Wave Mystic's mill; nine under combat damage to a player
(Professor Hulk, Glint-Eye Nephilim, Fear of Failed Tests, Cold-Eyed Selkie's may, April's draw-then-discard, Living
Hive's Insects, Elsha's Monks, Rapacious One's quoted Spawn - D473's fold under a count - and Crosstown Courier's mill);
Flayed Nim's `that creature's controller loses that much life` under combat damage to a creature (D428's `playerOf` aims
the damaged creature's controller); and Mindscour Dragon's plain four under the new opponent head.

### The fuzz seam (`apply-fuzz-1..2.cjs`)

`memoTriggers` (a triggered object put on the stack with `memo > 0`) reported; a Mourning Thrull a seat ({1}{W/B} 1/1
flier) is the staple; floored `> 0` after 4 at 60 seeds and 12 at 150.

### Traps

- **THE ANY-DAMAGE HEAD IS TWO DEFS.** Combat damage is `CombatDamageDealt`, the rest `DamageDealt`, and the bus
  dispatches a def on its one event: a `Whenever ~ deals damage` def on `DamageDealt` alone never sees an attack. It is
  doubled (`dealsDamage` + `dealsDamageAny`) as `dealsDamagePlayer` is.
- **THE MEMO IS THE HEAD'S RECIPIENT'S DAMAGE.** A trampler's damage to its blocker is not `combat damage to a player`;
  the memo filter mirrors the head (a player, an opponent, a creature, anything), never the whole batch.
- **A `that much` PAYLOAD READS ONLY UNDER A HEAD THAT MEMOISES.** `HEAD_MEMO` is the caller's flag: the wide probe
  passes it for a `that much` payload, the row maker admits it under a damage head on a creature with power alone, the
  token-pin guard reads the call site's `{ memo: true }`. Without the flag the sentence is refused as before.
- **AN `else` FOLLOWS ITS OWN `if`.** A line inserted between an `if` and its `else` re-parents the `else`; D433's did,
  and the generator asserted the wrong player for 43 decisions until a row of that shape came through.

## D477 — THE NUMBER TAKEN: the memo readers on every head whose event carries a number — the damage dealt to the creature, the life gained or lost, another creature's or the attached creature's combat damage (2026-09-17)

**11,173 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,146
(+27 rows: Hornet Nest, Kami of the Honored Dead, Sanguine Bond, Defiant Bloodlord, Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose,
Vilis, Broker of Blood, Old Gnawbone, Body of Knowledge, Boros Reckoner, Spitemare, Jackal Pup, Mogg Maniac, Hungering
Hydra, Ageless Entity, Sunbond, Light of Promise, Pollenbright Wings, Scepter of Celebration, Abomination, Irradiated
Brute, Coalhauler Swine, Saber Ants, Broodhatch Nantuko, Illusory Ambusher, Filthy Cur, Shinka Gatekeeper, Thrashing
Mudspawn, Wall of Hope).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,335 → **7,362**. The REFUSED ledger **1,715** (nothing stale). Fixtures
8,171 → **8,198**. `scriptableToday` **1,802**; the ladder `[1802, 1808, 3146, 4708, 5968]`. Bot reach **4,602** from
**340**. An engine seam, a generator wave and no fuzz change (the D476 counter and staple stand) on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — 34 rows refused for the memo admission alone

D476's wide run refused 34 rows with one reason: `a that-much payload under a head with no number` - the row maker had
read the head, the payload and every other line; only the memo admission (a self damage head on a creature with power)
stood in the way. By head: `isDealtDamage` 19, `youGainLife` 7, `creatureCombatDamagePlayer` 3,
`equippedCreatureCombatDamagePlayer` 2, `youLoseLife` 1, `enchantedCreatureCombatDamagePlayer` 1, `dealsDamage` 1 (a
0-power Phantom Nishoba - stays). Each head's EVENT carries the number: the damage dealt TO the creature
(`CombatDamageDealt` / `DamageDealt` with the creature as target), the life moved (`LifeChanged.delta`), another creature's
or the attached creature's damage to a player. The probe `zz-memo-heads477` measured the wider field too (the aura
`enchanted creature deals damage` 5, `an opponent loses life` 3, `you discard one or more cards` 4 - the next heads).

### The engine seam (`apply-num-1.cjs`)

- `TriggerDef.memo?: (ctx, self, ev, item?) => number` - a per-item firing hands its item (the creature you control that
  dealt the damage under `Whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player`, CR 603.2c); triggers.ts
  passes `item` beside D428's `playerOf`, and the GRANTED-def path (D368) stamps the memo too - it stamped item and
  player, never the memo, so a granted `Whenever you gain life, put that many +1/+1 counters on this creature` (Sunbond,
  Light of Promise on the Bears) read nothing.
- `memoItem.test.ts` (1 test): a Bears and a Hill Giant attack unblocked under a per-item def; two triggers carry 2 and
  3; the controller gains 5; the replay.

### The generator (`apply-gen-1..2.cjs`)

- gen177-vocab: `EVENT_MEMO_HEADS` (the is-dealt heads and their split, the two life heads, the another-creature and the
  two attached heads) admitted beside D476's power-gated self damage heads; `memoArmCount(a, r, plan)` is the arm's
  number per head - the Goblin's 1 or the Cyclops' 5 under combat damage taken, the Bolt's 3 under noncombat, 3 under
  the life arms (`ManualSetLife`), the Bears' 2 under another creature's damage, 2 + the attached static's power under
  the attached heads; `countN` / `countedEffects` take the row.
- gen-oneshot177: `memoFn(trigger)` writes the memo per head - the damage self dealt to the head's recipient (D476), the
  damage dealt to self (`d.target.id === self`), `ev.delta` / `-ev.delta`, the item's damage (or every creature you
  control's when the head has no item), the attached creature's (`attachedTo`).
- The is-dealt-combat-damage arm for a creature the Goblin's block cannot damage: a defender cannot attack and the
  Goblin cannot block a flier, so the opponent's Cyclops (5/2) attacks on its own turn and the creature BLOCKS it - dealt
  5 (Hornet Nest's five Insects, Wall of Hope's five life, Kami of the Honored Dead's five). The `killed` baseline reads 5.
- Two rows refused by name (the D429 table): Brash Taunter (a 1/1 fight the Bears survives - the fight assert reads a
  death, and the suite names `onBoard` the module never imports) and Truefire Captain (a mentor whose mentee is the
  blocking Goblin).

### The wave — 27 rows (81 tests)

Seventeen under the damage taken (Kami of the Honored Dead, Wall of Hope, Filthy Cur, Thrashing Mudspawn - life; Body of
Knowledge, Illusory Ambusher - cards; Hornet Nest, Saber Ants, Broodhatch Nantuko - Insects; Hungering Hydra - counters;
Jackal Pup, Shinka Gatekeeper - damage to you; Boros Reckoner, Spitemare - any target; Mogg Maniac - opponent or
planeswalker; Coalhauler Swine - each player), six under the life moved (Sanguine Bond, Defiant Bloodlord, Vito -
`target opponent loses that much life`; Ageless Entity and the granted Sunbond, Light of Promise - counters; Vilis -
cards), two under another creature's damage (Old Gnawbone's Treasures, Abomination's counters) and two under the attached
creature's (Pollenbright Wings' Saprolings, Scepter of Celebration's Citizens).

### Traps

- **A GRANTED DEF'S FIRING CARRIES WHAT THE PRESENT DEF'S DOES.** D368's granted path stamped item and player and
  stopped there; a hook added to `TriggerDef` (D476's memo) reaches a granted def only when both paths stamp it.
- **THE GOBLIN'S BLOCK CANNOT DAMAGE A DEFENDER OR A FLIER.** A defender cannot attack into it; the Goblin cannot block a
  flier - the suite walks the game to its end waiting for a blockers prompt. Those rows take their combat damage
  blocking the Cyclops on the opponent's turn (dealt 5, the `killed` baseline 5).
- **THE ARM'S NUMBER IS THE HEAD'S, NOT THE CARD'S.** D476 sized a memo by the printed power (the unblocked attack); a
  head whose event is not the creature's own attack has its own number per arm - 1, 5, 3, 2, 2 + a pump.

## D478 — THE SEARCH ROW RESTORED: the permanent noun and the card-or-card alternative in a search, and the row maker admitting a search as an ask again — refused since D390 (2026-09-17)

**11,231 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,173
(+58: 55 rows — the Masques recruiters (Ramosian Sergeant, Ramosian Lieutenant, Ramosian Captain, Ramosian Commander,
Ramosian Sky Marshal, Defiant Falcon, Amrou Scout, Blightspeaker, Cateran Persuader, Cateran Brute, Cateran Kidnappers,

Greater Tanuki, Knight of the Reliquary, Wight of the Reliquary, Elvish Reclaimer, Escape Tunnel, Horizon Seeker,

of the Aldergard), the tutors to the top (Forerunner of the Legion, Forerunner of the Heralds, Forerunner of the Coalition),

Wishes, Rampart Architect, Sun-Spider, Nimble Webber — and 3 sorceries the parser completes: Open the Gates, Map the
Frontier, Circuitous Route).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,362 → **7,417**. The REFUSED ledger 1,715 → **1,695** (23 rowed
entries retired, 3 added). Fixtures 8,198 → **8,257**. `scriptableToday` 1,802 → **1,781**; the ladder
`[1781, 1787, 3123, 4684, 5943]`. Bot reach **4,640** from **343**. A parser seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement found a ninety-decision slip

The residue is flat; the search payloads were the densest coherent family left (345 leftover lines carry one). Classified
against the LIVE parser (the wide run's log truncates a payload at 77 characters - never classify from it), 98 of them
READ already, and the recruiters' `a Rebel permanent card with mana value 3 or less` (24 sole rows) were the largest
unread shape. Then the row maker refused every one of the 98 as `effect not a row kind`: the vocab probe has marked a
search payload `asks` since D390 (its ASK set gained `search` there) while the row maker's `ASK_KINDS` never did - so a
search that is the payload's last effect, which the generator has answered since D359 (`case 'search'`,
`searchFixture`, 159 landed suites answer `AnswerSearchLibrary`), had been refused for ninety decisions. One word.

### The parser seam (`apply-search-1..2.cjs`)

- `permanent` names no card type: a permanent card is one of the six types that go onto the battlefield (CR 110.4).
  `expandPermanent` rewrites `Rebel permanent` to `Rebel artifact or Rebel creature or Rebel enchantment or Rebel land or
  Rebel planeswalker or Rebel battle` before `predicatesOf` sees it - one alternative per permanent type, the qualifier a
  conjunct over all - and `nonland permanent` leaves the land out. A Goblin tribal instant is a Goblin card and no Goblin
  permanent card, and the expansion says so; any other `non-` word stays refused. Local to the search noun: the cost
  readers keep their own `permanent` handling.
- An alternative spelled with its own `card` (`a basic land card or Gate card`, `a basic land card or a Desert card`,
  `up to two basic land cards and/or Gate cards`) folds to the `or` list the reader already takes; `and/or` is admitted
  only under an `up to N` count (there it means any mix, which an `or` list under a count is); a qualifier beside such an
  alternative is refused (it would bind both).
- `searchNoun.test.ts` (4 tests): the six alternatives and their qualifier, the five of nonland, the tribal instant
  refused, the folded alternative and its count, the refusals.

### The generator (`apply-rows-1..3.cjs`)

- `ASK_KINDS` gains `search` (the one word).
- An asking payload under the cycle head is refused (`Krosan Tusker`, `Shefet Monitor`): the cycling ability sits on the
  stack under the trigger, so the settle after the trigger resolves answers the ask with the harness's decline before the
  suite can - the `searchLibrary` prompt is gone by the time the test looks for it.
- The five step heads the wide run refused (each player's end step, each combat, your second main phase, the end of combat,
  each opponent's end step) join the library - measured at 0 rows (their payloads are the hard part: that-player
  conditions, doubled power, blockers at end of combat) and kept for the day a payload reads.

### The wave — 55 rows (140 tests)

Twenty-two recruiters and tutors that put the find onto the battlefield (the Rebels and Mercenaries by mana value, the
Elf, the Goblin, the Merfolk, the legendary Spirit, any permanent through Planar Bridge), the land tutors to the
battlefield tapped or to the hand (the Reliquary pair's `{T}: search` beside their land-count pump, the Gate and Cave
and Desert alternatives, Colossal Rattlewurm's threshold), the three Forerunners' tutor-to-the-top, Corpse Connoisseur's
and Goblin Engineer's graveyard puts (the Engineer skipped: its reanimate names a fixture the suite already deals),
Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, From Beyond's Eldrazi beside its Scion, Ring of Three Wishes, Magitek Infantry's named
search for itself.

### Traps

- **THE WIDE LOG TRUNCATES A PAYLOAD AT 77 CHARACTERS.** A family classified from the log is classified by its prefix;
  the search residue was misread three times before a probe read the leftover against the live parser.
- **A PROBE'S ASK SET AND THE ROW MAKER'S ARE ONE LIST.** The probe marks `asks` off its set, the row maker admits an
  ask off its own; a kind added to one and not the other refuses every row of that kind, silently, as `effect not a row
  kind` - for ninety decisions here. When a kind joins one list it joins both, or the generator's `case` says why not.
- **THE CYCLING ABILITY SITS UNDER ITS OWN TRIGGER.** A settle after the cycle trigger resolves answers whatever the
  trigger asked, because the stack is not empty until the cycling draw resolves too.

## D479 — THE TRIBAL TARGET: a capitalised noun after `target` is a subtype, enforced through `restrict.subtypesAll`, read by the effect rules through a fold to the marker noun — and a vanilla creature of the subtype as the suite's fixture (2026-09-17)

**11,297 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,231
(+66: 56 rows in two ports — the tribal triggers (Venerable Knight, Sanguine Glorifier, Stromkirk Mentor, Stromkirk
Bloodthief, Jade Guardian, Jade Bearer, Deeproot Elite, Vineshaper Mystic, Aeronaut Cavalry, Captain Storm, Advocate of
the Beast, Arashin Foremost, Intrepid Provisioner, Patagia Tiger, Burning-Yard Trainer, Garrison Griffin, Majestic
Heliopterus, Swift Warden, Tributary Vaulter, Voracious Vampire, Poison-Blade Mentor, Blacklance Paragon, Vedalken
Aethermage, Deepchannel Duelist) and the tribal activations (Mad Auntie, Krosan Warchief, Black Poplar Shaman, Elephant
Graveyard, Boneknitter, Vital Splicer - regenerations; Otepec Huntmaster, Snarling Undorak, Krosan Groundshaker, Goblin
Taskmaster, Goblin Burrows, Daru Encampment, Icatian Lieutenant, Air Marshal, Veteran Cathar, Zhalfirin Commander,
Dwarven Lieutenant, Anaba Ancestor, Hearthcage Giant, Olivia's Bloodsworn, Drunau Corpse Trawler, Earth Kingdom Protectors,
Safewright Cavalry - pumps; Wirewood Lodge, Kitsune Diviner, Merfolk Sovereign, Daughter of the Deep, Aquatic Incursion,
Riptide Laboratory, Spectral Shepherd, Ally Encampment, Contested Cliffs) — and 10 spells the target reads: Rend Spirit,
Human Frailty, Markov Retribution, Consuming Bonfire, Fight as One, Crawl from the Cellar, Cleansing Ray, Fever Charm,
Buccaneer's Bravado, Vitality Charm).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,417 → **7,473**. The REFUSED ledger 1,695 → **1,718** (23
added by reason). Fixtures 8,257 → **8,318**. `scriptableToday` 1,781 → **1,801**; the ladder
`[1801, 1807, 3128, 4676, 5936]`. Bot reach **4,672** from **344**. A parser seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — 139 lines, 68 sole rows, one noun

Probed against the live parser (the wide log's rule since D478): 139 leftover lines aim at a creature subtype - `target
Knight you control` 49, `target Vampire` 42, `target Elf card` 28 (D298 read those), `target Zombie creature` 15 - and
68 of them are sole rows. The target parser had explicit entries for a Wall, an Aura, an Equipment, a Vehicle and the
five basics, and D298's rule for `<Subtype> card`; a capitalised noun anywhere else fell to free aim, unconfident.

### The parser seam (`apply-target-1..3.cjs`)

- targetParse.ts: three entries after every explicit one - `<Sub> creature` (kinds creature), `<Sub> permanent` (kinds
  permanent) and the bare `<Sub>` (kinds permanent - a permanent named by its subtype alone is any permanent carrying it,
  CR 205.3d), the subtype read off the noun into `restrict.subtypesAll` as D298's card entry reads it; the engine has
  enforced `subtypesAll` on the candidate's derived subtypes since D297 (`targets.ts`). The singular alone (a word ending
  in `s` is a plural or stays unread); never a word followed by another capitalised one (a card name).
- effectParse.ts: the rules match under the `i` flag, where a capitalised-word class would match any word, so
  `matchSentence` folds `target <Sub>[ creature| permanent][ you control|an opponent controls|you don't control]` to the
  marker noun `#sub#` (six NOUNS entries, longest first) for the length of one match and hands the clause back with its
  PRINTED text - the referent rewrite's own pattern. Sentence-initial `Target` folds too.
- `tribalTarget.test.ts` (4 tests): the specs (kinds, the subtype, the controller, `another`), the effect reading with
  its printed text, the explicit nouns keeping their kinds, the refusals (a plural, a name, a noun before a capital).

### The generator (`apply-gen-1.cjs`)

A clause naming a subtype the fixture table does not hold is served by the cheapest VANILLA creature of that subtype in
the database (`FIX.allCards()`, `plain` - no text at all), non-legendary first: Knight Errant, Falkenrath Reaver, Merfolk
of the Pearl Trident, Jibbirik Omnivore, Balduvian Bears, Fugitive Wizard, Cliffhaven Sell-Sword, Devoted Hero,
Wandering Ones, Gutter Skulk, Mons's Goblin Raiders ... (a Dragon, an Angel, a Spider, a Ninja, a Kavu, a Robot, a Samurai
have none and stay refused by reason). The port's sweep names the derived fixtures for WANTED - and the second port's
sweep had to read the second port's module list (three fixtures missed until it did).

### The wave — 56 rows in two ports (50 + 73 tests)

The first port took the 24 trigger rows the wide pool held; the activated tribal abilities were OUTSIDE the wide pool -
their unread target clause had counted as a spec piece, and the pool takes rows whose remaining pieces are lines alone -
so the leftover was probed again under the new parser and a second wide run rowed 34 more (32 generated; Goblin Engineer
and Ayula skipped for a fixture the suite already deals). The mirror then offered 23 the wave cannot row - subtypes with
no vanilla fixture, the Sliver grants with a tribal target, two tribal anthems, Thraben Exorcism's keyword-qualified
alternative, a Detective token outside the table - each ledgered by reason.

### Traps

- **A SUBTYPE NOUN IS CASE, AND THE RULES ARE NOT.** The effect rules match under `i`; a `[A-Z]` class there matches every
  word. The fold runs on the printed sentence, case-sensitively, and the rules see a marker.
- **A CLAUSE THAT DID NOT READ WAS A SPEC PIECE, NOT A LINE.** The wide pool (`specs.length === 0`) never held the
  activated tribal rows; a parser widening that turns a spec piece into a read line needs the leftover probed again
  before the pool is built, or the second half of the yield is never seen.
- **THE SWEEP READS ONE MODULE LIST.** A second port's derived fixtures are named only by a sweep over the second port's
  list; the port script's sed does not reach the sweep's own file reference.

## D480 — THE TRIBAL MASS: the mass counter and the mass pump over a subtype, read through the scoped anthem's scope (2026-09-17)

**11,318 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,297
(+21 rows: Thalia's Lieutenant, Cordial Vampire, Indulgent Aristocrat, Valiant Veteran, Kazuul Warlord, Earth King's
Lieutenant — the mass counters; Goblin General, Goblin Lookout, Hamlet Captain, Perimeter Sergeant, Belle of the Brawl,
Riot Ringleader, Heron's Grace Champion, Blood-Chin Rager, Stromkirk Condemned, Ezuri, Renegade Leader, Drey Keeper,
Squirrel Wrangler, Gempalm Avenger, Gempalm Strider, Huatli, Dinosaur Knight — the mass pumps).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,473
→ **7,494**. The REFUSED ledger **1,718**. Fixtures 8,318 → **8,340**. `scriptableToday` **1,801**; the ladder
`[1801, 1807, 3118, 4660, 5920]`. Bot reach **4,682** from **345**. A generator wave on Opus 5 - no engine or parser change.

### The measurement chose it — 399 lines with a mass effect over a subtype

Over the post-D479 leftover, 399 lines (68 sole rows) carry a mass effect with a subtype noun: the tribal keyword grants
149 (`Golems you control have indestructible`), the tribal anthems 137 (`Other Pirates you control get +1/+1` - the
row maker's `anthem` kind reads these since D371; the lines are leftover for their cards' OTHER lines), the mass
counter over a subtype 96 (`put a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you control`), the tribal mass pump 9 (`other Humans
you control get +1/+1 until end of turn`). The mass counter and the mass pump were the two row kinds that read
`each creature you control` and nothing narrower; the scoped anthem's scope module (D371) already knew the subtype
phrase, its predicate and its fixture.

### The generator (`apply-rows-1.cjs`, `apply-gen-1..2.cjs`)

- make-rows180: `massCounter` takes `on each (other) <Sub>( creature) you control`, `mass` takes the scoped anthem's
  phrase before the same body (`MASS_SCOPED`: `Other Humans you control`, `Goblin creatures you control`, `Wizards you
  control`) - the scope read by `SCOPE.scopeOf`, a subtype scope alone, the fixture table bounding it (D353's rule: a
  subtype with no fixture is refused by reason - 15 rows in the wide run).
- gen-oneshot180: `counterBody` and `pumpBody` add the scope's conjunct on the DERIVED type line
  (`typeLine.subtypes.includes(sub)`), as the anthem's `appliesTo` reads it; the suite's `yes` is the scope's fixture
  already (`yesNameOf` finds any ability carrying an anthem scope); a scoped `all` never reaches the Cyclops (no Cyclops
  is a Soldier) - asserted untouched; the title names the scope.
- Two rows refused by name: Kumena, Tyrant of Orazca (a tap cost of the scope's own subtype beside the tribal mass
  counter - the tappers and the `yes` fixture are one name) and Temmet, Naktamun's Will (a loot beside a draw head - the
  loot's draw fires the head, the hand assert reads both).

### The wave — 21 rows (63 tests)

Six mass counters (Thalia's Lieutenant's other Humans, Cordial Vampire's Vampires on a death, Indulgent Aristocrat's
Vampires for a sacrifice, Valiant Veteran's Soldiers beside its anthem, Kazuul Warlord's and Earth King's Lieutenant's
Allies) and fifteen mass pumps (the attack lords - Goblin General, Perimeter Sergeant, Belle of the Brawl, Riot
Ringleader, Blood-Chin Rager; the activated - Goblin Lookout's sacrifice, Ezuri's Elves, Stromkirk Condemned's Vampires,
Drey Keeper's and Squirrel Wrangler's Squirrels, Huatli's Dinosaurs; the cycle heads - Gempalm Avenger's Soldiers,
Gempalm Strider's Elves; Hamlet Captain's attack-or-block, Heron's Grace Champion's entry).

### Traps

- **A SCOPED `all` IS NOT THE CYCLOPS'S.** `Soldier creatures get +1/+1` is every Soldier on the battlefield; the mass
  assert's `all` branch read the opponent's Cyclops pumped, and four suites failed until `all` under a scope asserted
  it untouched.
- **THE TAPPERS AND THE FIXTURE ARE ONE NAME.** A tap cost of the scope's own subtype (`Tap five untapped Merfolk you
  control`) deals the same vanilla the scope's `yes` is; the suite's picks and its witness collide. Refused by name
  until the cost fixtures and the scope fixture are kept apart.

## D481 — THE WIDER SCOPE TABLE: every creature subtype with a vanilla creature in the database is a scope the suite can prove (2026-09-17)

**11,334 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,318
(+16 rows: the lords over a subtype the table lacked — Corpses of the Lost (Skeletons), Ogre Slumlord (Rats), Bebop,
Warthog Warrior (Rhinos), Seshiro the Anointed (Snakes), Arno Dorian (Assassins), Shadow-Rite Priest (Clerics), Crested
Sunmare (Horses), Zarda, the Power Princess (Heroes) — and the tribal masses over them: Agent Phil Coulson and Doctor
Spectrum (Heroes), Biogenic Ooze (Oozes), Minwu, White Mage (Clerics), Adeliz, the Cinder Wind and Gempalm Sorcerer
(Wizards), Sethron, Hurloon General (Minotaurs), Bloodstoke Howler (Beasts)).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,494 → **7,510**.
The REFUSED ledger 1,718 → **1,710** (eight rowed lords retired). Fixtures 8,340 → **8,366**. `scriptableToday` 1,801
→ **1,793**; the ladder `[1793, 1799, 3107, 4646, 5906]`. Bot reach **4,689** from **354**. A generator wave on Opus 5 -
no engine or parser change.

### The measurement chose it — 85 subtypes in scope lines, 23 in the table

Over the post-D480 leftover (`d480/measure-scope481.cjs`): 85 creature subtypes appear in anthem, mass and grant scope
lines; the scope module's hand table held 23, and 129 lines (27 sole rows) named a subtype outside it - 61 of those lines
a subtype with a vanilla creature in the database (Hero, Phyrexian, Wizard, Assassin, Rat, Dog, Minotaur, Snake, Demon,
Dwarf, Ooze, Treefolk, Horse, Cleric, Myr ...); Dragon 13, Villain 6, Bird 6 and Spider 4 have none. D353's rule stands -
a subtype with no fixture is not a scope the suite can prove - and the database says which subtypes have one.

### The generator (`apply-scope-1..2.cjs`, `apply-rows-1.cjs`)

- gen181-scope: `widenSubtypeTable` runs at require time over `FIXLIB.allCards()` - every `plain` creature (no text at
  all) with a printed power and toughness offers its subtypes; per subtype the cheapest non-legendary vanilla wins
  (D479's rule for the tribal target), a hand entry above wins over a derived one, and `BASES` learns the derived
  fixtures' bases through `DERIVED_BASES` (the const is declared after the widening runs). The plural is by rule -
  `s`, `es` after s/x/z/ch/sh, `ies` after a consonant-y, the listed `-ves` words and invariants (Merfolk, Kithkin,
  Homarid, Moonfolk ...), Hero → Heroes - because `subtypeByPlural` reads a lord's printed plural; a plural the rule
  gets wrong is a scope no lord reads, never a wrong fixture.
- One row refused by name: Balthor the Stout (an `all` anthem beside a tribal target pump whose fixture is the
  opponent's Barbarian - the fixture reads the anthem too, the pump assert reads the printed base).

### The wave — 16 rows (48 tests)

Eight lords (Skeleton, Rat, Rhino, Snake, Assassin, Cleric, Horse, Hero) - eight entries the REFUSED ledger had held
under the missing-fixture reason, retired by the guard - and eight tribal masses (the Heroes' counters, the Oozes' end
step, the Clerics' life-gain counter, the Wizards' pumps, the Minotaurs', the Beasts' on a face-up turn).

### Traps

- **A DERIVED FIXTURE IS A SCOPE THE SUITE CAN PROVE, A DERIVED PLURAL IS NOT A GUESS.** The fixture is the database's
  own vanilla; the plural is read from print by rule, and a miss (Sphinxes read, `Sphinx` has no vanilla) refuses the
  line rather than aiming the assert at the wrong creature.
- **AN `all` ANTHEM REACHES THE OPPONENT'S FIXTURE OF THE SUBTYPE.** `Other Barbarian creatures get +1/+1` pumps the p2
  Barbarian the tribal target pump aims at; the pump assert adds no anthem bonus for a p2 fixture. Refused by name.

## D482 — THE PLAYER'S SACRIFICE: the queued sacrifice over the one player the clause aims at, and its count (2026-09-17)

**11,354 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,334
(+20: 8 rows — Gatekeeper of Malakir, Sheoldred, Whispering One, Blighted Fen, Ruthless Deathfang, Demon of Loathing,
Cabal Executioner, Destructive Urge, Molder Slug — and 12 spells the vocabulary completes with no script: Chainer's
Edict, Cruel Edict, Diabolic Edict, Barter in Blood, Pharika's Libation, Dromoka's Command, Grave Exchange, Silverquill
Command, Umbral Juke, Rankle's Prank, Angrath's Rampage, Dead Drop).** `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,510 → **7,518**. The REFUSED
ledger 1,710 → **1,713** (three added by reason). Fixtures 8,366 → **8,376**. `scriptableToday` 1,793 → **1,796**; the
ladder `[1796, 1802, 3110, 4649, 5910]`. Bot reach **4,691** from **355**. An engine seam, a vocabulary widening and a
generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — 174 lines, 92 sole rows, one verb

Over the post-D481 leftover, 174 lines (92 sole rows) have a PLAYER sacrifice: `Target player sacrifices a creature of
their choice` 22, `Target opponent ...` 13, a head's `that player sacrifices ...` 17, `Each opponent sacrifices <noun> of
their choice` 22 and `Each player ...` 20 - the last two with a COUNT D390's rule lacked (`two creatures`, `three`, `six`).
D390 had built the queue (every player in scope asked in APNAP order, the batch landing with the last answer); it had
no scope for the one player a clause aims at, and no count.

### The engine seam and the vocabulary (`apply-sac-1..3.cjs`)

- `BoardScope.controller` gains `target` - the player the effect aimed at. `effects.ts` resolves it in `case 'sacrifice'`:
  the aimed target (`obj.targets[effect.targetIndex]`, a player) is handed to `queueAsks` as an `only` list in place of
  the scopes' members; the aim gone, nothing is asked (CR 608.2b).
- effectParse.ts: `Target (player|opponent) sacrifices (an|COUNT) <noun>( of (their|target player's|that player's)
  choice)?` - the choice suffix is the rule's own (CR 701.17a) and a head's referent spells it `of target player's choice`;
  `Each (player|opponent) sacrifices (an|COUNT) <noun> of their choice` takes the count and reads the noun singular. `an`
  is a count of one in both (Simplify's `an enchantment`, Tribute to the Wild's `an artifact or enchantment` - the two
  the first cut regressed and the engine suite caught).
- `playerSacrifice.test.ts` (3 tests): the readings; Cruel Edict aimed at p2 with two creatures asks p2 and takes what p2
  named (the Giant), the Bears stays; aimed at a lone creature it asks nobody; Barter in Blood asks p1 for two of three
  and takes both of p2's unasked; the replay hash. Cruel Edict and Barter in Blood join the fixtures for it.

### The generator and the wave — 8 rows (17 tests) in two ports

The generator's queue asserts read a non-`you` scope as p2's already (`queueAsksP2`), so a `target` scope needed no
change: the trigger and activated rows landed on the first port (Gatekeeper of Malakir's kicked-or-not entry aim,
Sheoldred's each-opponent upkeep, Blighted Fen's sacrifice-a-land activation, Ruthless Deathfang under the
you-sacrifice head, the two combat-damage edicts, Destructive Urge's land). Molder Slug (`that player sacrifices an
artifact` under each upkeep) came on the second port after the `an` fix. Three the mirror offered are ledgered by reason
(Abyssal Gorestalker's two under an ETB, Custodi Lich's monarch head, Trial of Ambition's Cartouche head).

### Traps

- **`an` IS A COUNT OF ONE.** `COUNT` spells `a|one|two|...`; a rule that took the count from it dropped every `an
  enchantment` - two spells regressed in the first cut, caught by `playerQueue.test.ts`'s Simplify pin before the port.
- **A RE-PROBED LEFTOVER FINDS THE ROWS A FIX OPENED.** The `an` fix opened Molder Slug after the first port; the wide
  chain re-run over the re-probed leftover rowed it as a second port (D479's rule again).

## D483 — THE TWO-ZONE SEARCH: a search over the library and the searcher's graveyard, the find moving from where it is (2026-09-17)

**11,381 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,354
(+27: 17 rows — the planeswalker tutors Elspeth's Devotee, Domri's Nodorog, Sorin's Guide, Teferi's Wavecaster,
Niambi, Faithful Healer, Chandra's Firemaw, Ethereal Elk, Garruk's Warsteed, Goldmane Griffin, Ashiok's Forerunner,
Yanling's Harbinger, Tower Winder, Rowan's Stalwarts, Gideon's Resolve, Visage of Bolas, Raven Clan War-Axe, Delivery
Moogle — and 10 spells the vocabulary completes: Jace's Ruse, Tezzeret's Betrayal, Vraska's Scorn, Basri's Aegis, Dovin's
Dismissal, Angrath's Fury, Ral's Dispersal, Liliana's Scorn, Liberating Combustion, Chandra's Outburst).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,518 → **7,535**. The REFUSED ledger 1,713 → **1,714** (one by reason). Fixtures 8,376 → **8,408**.
`scriptableToday` 1,796 → **1,797**; the ladder `[1797, 1803, 3112, 4650, 5911]`. Bot reach **4,699** from **356**. An
engine seam, a vocabulary widening and a generator wave on Opus 5.

### The measurement chose it — 48 lines, 34 sole rows, one prompt

Over the post-D482 leftover, 48 lines (34 sole rows) read `Search your library and/or graveyard for a card named X,
reveal it, and put it into your hand. If you search your library this way, shuffle.` - the planeswalker-tutor
creatures, the Rune tutor, the spells with the same rider after their own clause. D359 had built the search prompt over
the library alone; the graveyard is a public zone, so the widening costs no reveal and no projection.

### The engine seam and the vocabulary (`apply-search-1..2.cjs`)

- `SearchSpec.graveyardToo` and the `searchLibrary` awaiting's `graveyardToo`: effects.ts raises the prompt with it (an
  empty library still asks when the graveyard is searched too); handlers.ts `answerSearchLibrary` takes a card from the
  library OR the searcher's graveyard, the move's `from` per card by the zone it is in, the reveal cleared over the
  library as before; the library counts as searched, so the printed shuffle runs.
- effectParse.ts: `SEARCH_HEAD` reads `search your library( and/or graveyard)? for`; the put clause joins with `, and put`
  (`reveal it, and put it`); the two-sentence tail `. If you search your library this way, shuffle` is the shuffle
  clause. The spec carries `graveyardToo` when the head said so.
- `twoZoneSearch.test.ts` (3 tests): the reading; the Elspeth in the GRAVEYARD found and put into the hand, the library
  shuffled; the Elspeth in the LIBRARY found the way every search finds, a card in neither zone refused; the replay.
  Elspeth's Devotee and Elspeth, Undaunted Hero join the fixtures for it.

### The generator (`apply-gen-1.cjs`) and the wave — 17 rows (36 tests)

A search naming its find that goes to the HAND is served by the named card whatever its text - found, never played, a
planeswalker in the hand sits as still as a vanilla (a named find bound for the battlefield keeps the quiet rule). The
generated suites stage the find in the library and answer from it, as every search suite does. The First Doctor is
ledgered (a cast head with cascade beside its search).

### Traps

- **THE GRAVEYARD IS PUBLIC, THE LIBRARY IS NOT.** The two-zone prompt reveals the library as before and the graveyard
  not at all; the searcher's own graveyard is already everyone's to read. The projection's sorted list is unchanged.
- **A NAMED FIND BOUND FOR THE HAND NEEDS NO QUIET.** The search pool's quiet rule exists because a found card may
  ARRIVE on the battlefield; a card found into the hand is never played by the suite, so a planeswalker serves.
- **A LIBRARY COPY STAGED BEFORE THE DRAW STEPS IS DRAWN** (D232's hazard, met again): the seam test's library copy is
  put there past turn 3's draw, or the search finds it in the hand.

## D484 — THE PROMPT CONTINUATION: a question carries the clauses after it, and the answer runs them (2026-09-17)

(+69: 11 rows — Dimir Cutpurse, Psychic Symbiont, Hopeless Nightmare, Daily Bugle Newspaper, Drowned Rusalka,

(fifteen stale entries retired - Time Wipe, Condescend, Disrupt, Mind Ravel, Force Void, Overrule, Render Speechless, Offering to Asha, Runeboggle, Spell Contortion, Stymied Hopes, Dredge, Brainbite, Renewal, Liliana's Spoils, each read whole now - and five added by reason (Greedy Freebooter, Keen Buccaneer, Ninja of the Hand, Siren of the Silent Song, Surtland Frostpyre)). Fixtures 8,408 → **8,426**. `scriptableToday` 1,797 → **1,787**; the ladder `[1787, 1793, 3102, 4637, 5890]`.
Bot reach **4,716** from **356**. An engine seam on Fable 5.1 - the first of the transition.

### The measurement chose it — the wall every family hit, measured against the live parser

D195's rule - an effect that asks must be the sentence's LAST, or the card lands `assisted`, because `effectEvents`
stopped emitting at an `AwaitingSet` and what followed a question was dropped - was the wall every remaining family
still hit: the search followed by `You gain 2 life`, the edict with `and loses 1 life` (Geth's Verdict), the look with
`You lose 2 life`, the proliferate with `Draw a card` (Contentious Plan), the payment with `Draw a card` (Disrupt).
Measured against the live parser over the post-D483 leftover (`d484/zz-probe-ask484.node.test.ts`): 82 permanent
payloads and 68 spells carry an asking effect before their last clause; the vocabulary reads 30 payloads and 46 spells
WHOLE apart from the rule (discard 8 / 9, search 6 / 8, sacrifice 6 / 6, scry 6, lookAtTop 2 / 7, payOptional 8,
revealHandChoose 5, proliferate 3; two asks in a row 2 / 10) - the rest have an unread tail behind the ask and want
vocabulary, not the seam.

### The engine seam (`d484/patch-state.txt`, `patch-effects-a/b.txt`, `patch-handlers-a/b.txt`, `patch-marker.txt`)

- `EffectContinuation` (state.ts): the clauses after an asking effect, what the executor reads of the resolving object
  (`payMana` snapshots the same fields), a replay-stable id of its own (`<stackId>-c<clause>`, so a resumed clause's
  derived ids - a delayed trigger's, a shield's - never collide with the resolution's), and an `outer` frame. It rides
  `priority.awaiting` on the six prompts the executor raises (`payMana`, `searchLibrary`, `chooseFromZone`,
  `orderCards`, `scryChoice`, `proliferateChoice`), hashed and replayed with the state.
- effects.ts: THE STOP. After each step the executor looks for a question among the events the step added; finding one
  it puts the clauses after the step on it (`continuationOf`, `withContinuation` - a prompt already carrying a frame
  keeps it and takes the new one as its `outer`) and ends. ONE question per batch is still the rule; it is kept by
  stopping, and a second asking clause is simply the first of the continuation. A counted asking clause asks for its
  first pick only (no vocabulary rule prints one).
- `resumeContinuation` (effects.ts): the one funnel every asking answer ends through. The answer's events are folded
  through the pure reducer (D195's scratch, the RNG the answer advanced threaded in so a shuffle before and a draw after
  never share numbers), the frame runs against that state (`ContinuationResumed` marks the log), a frame that asks again
  carries what is left, a frame that ends runs the frame beyond it. When the answer's own events raised the chain's
  NEXT question - the ordering after a look, the next player of a queue, the next explore or connive, the reveal stage
  of an optional search - the continuation is forwarded onto it untouched and nothing runs yet.
- handlers.ts: `answerPayMana` (after the branch), `answerSearchLibrary` (the declined offer, the tutor's top, the
  find), `advanceAsks` (the next player's question takes it; the batch runs it), `answerChooseFromZone` (the look, the
  ordering it chains into, the hand reveal's pick, the discard and its connive chain), `answerOrderCards`, `answerScry`
  (and the explore chain), `answerProliferate` all end through the funnel.
- effectParse.ts: the ask-last rule is gone; `scripts/vocabulary.ts` no longer refuses an ask before the last clause.
- `promptContinuation.test.ts` (8 tests): the readings; Vampiric Tutor's find on top and THEN the life (the shuffle's
  RNG before the resume, the replay after); Contentious Plan's proliferate then the draw; Geth's Verdict's queue then
  the loss (and with one creature, no question and the loss at once); Mind Ravel's discard then the delayed draw armed
  and fired; Disrupt's payment then the draw both ways; Experimental Augury's look, ordering and proliferate in a row -
  the continuation forwarded across the ordering; Basic Conjuration's random bottom then the life gain, replayed.
  Seven spells join the fixtures for it.

### The generator, the retired scripts and the wave — 11 rows

- make-rows184 `vocabReading`: an ask may stand anywhere; every asking effect must be one the suite answers
  (`ASK_KINDS` - a scry or surveil beside another ask stays refused). gen-oneshot184: the once-each-turn probe waits for
  the test's answers whenever the payload asks (`asksAny`). The vocabulary generator's own asserts already read the
  clauses in order: an answer is emitted at the ask's place, the tail's deltas are read after it.
- Seven hand-written spell scripts whose D187 suppression predicate no longer held were RETIRED (`unland484.cjs`,
  D398's rule: a def exists only where the vocabulary cannot): Read the Bones, Cruel Truths, Demon's Due, Diresight,
  Notion Rain, Risky Research, Unhinge - each now runs from its printed text, in printed order.
- The fuzz: Vampiric Tutor a seat (`continuationsCarried` / `continuationsRun`), one a seat read 0 casts over 60 seeds (a ~230-card library, ~10 turns a seed - the same shape D445 met), three a seat read 16 carried / 16 run, so the deal is three and the floors are pinned at 500 seeds.
- The wave: 11 rows (Goblin Engineer and Ayula, Queen Among Bears skipped by the generator as before), 58
  spells the vocabulary completes; the REFUSED ledger fifteen stale entries retired - Time Wipe, Condescend, Disrupt, Mind Ravel, Force Void, Overrule, Render Speechless, Offering to Asha, Runeboggle, Spell Contortion, Stymied Hopes, Dredge, Brainbite, Renewal, Liliana's Spoils, each read whole now - and five added by reason (Greedy Freebooter, Keen Buccaneer, Ninja of the Hand, Siren of the Silent Song, Surtland Frostpyre).

### Traps

- **A QUESTION CARRIES WHAT FOLLOWS IT.** The executor stops behind the first ask; nothing after a question runs before
  its answer, and nothing is dropped. A handler that raises a follow-up question must let the funnel FORWARD the
  continuation (it does so by itself when the follow-up is in the answer's events).
- **A DECLINED OFFER STILL RUNS WHAT FOLLOWS.** `You may search ...` declined, `unless you pay` unpaid: the sentence
  after the question is unconditional, and the funnel runs it either way.
- **A HEREDOC BREAKS ON A LONG TEST FILE.** The seam test could not be written through the shell (a quoted heredoc past
  ~100 lines with apostrophes failed to parse); the Write tool wrote it. The block applier (`blockpatch.cjs`) reads its
  swaps from text files for the same reason - TypeScript with backticks and template holes sits verbatim.

## D485 — THE TOKEN COPY: a token that is a copy of a permanent takes its copiable values (2026-09-17)

**11,467 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,450
(+17: 10 rows — Homunculus Horde, Spawnwrithe, Polyraptor, Mist-Syndicate Naga, Extravagant Replication, Mishra's Self-Replicator, Giant Adephage, Sprouting Phytohydra, Myr Propagator, Elvish Hydromancer — and 7 spells the vocabulary completes: Rite of Replication, Cackling Counterpart, Saheeli's Artistry, Irenicus's Vile Duplication, Self-Reflection, Relm's Sketching, Multiversal Recruitment).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,539 → **7,549**. The REFUSED ledger 1,704 → **1,706** (two added by reason - Sorcerer's Broom (a payment under a sacrifice head whose fire funds the price, Furnace Celebration's class; its generated suite was unlanded) and Copy Catchers (a surveil head outside the library)). Fixtures 8,426 →
**8,440**. `scriptableToday` 1,787 → **1,791**; the ladder `[1791, 1797, 3106, 4641, 5874]`. Bot reach **4,722** from **356**.
An engine seam on Fable 5.1 - the first consumer of CR 707.

### The measurement chose it — the copy family, priced by consumer

The conditional continuation the D484 memory named next measured SMALL against the live parser (`d485/zz-probe-cond485`:
62 gated payloads / 13 spells after an ask, 16 / 1 with everything else readable - 8 rows and Psychic Miasma). The copy
family (CR 707, the plan's Phase 3.3, "COPY waits for Fable") priced by consumer over the post-D484 leftover
(`d485/price-copy485.cjs`): the token copy 259 lines / 106 sole (69 with no exception; `this creature` 31, `it` 11,
`this card` 8, `target creature you control` 7), the spell copy 232 / 97, the clone 64 / 47, `becomes a copy` 83 / 50,
populate 26 / 16, myriad 20 / 7. The token copy is the largest permanent consumer and needs no new prompt: the
target is chosen at the cast, the source is the object's own.

### The engine seam (`d485/patch485-types.txt`, `patch485-derive.txt`, `patch485-effects.txt`, `patch485-bus.txt`, `patch485-fix1.txt`)

- **A COPY IS ITS CARD.** The token's `oracleId`, `printingId` and `faceIndex` ARE the copied object's (`TokenCreated`
  carries the face and `copyOf`), so every script lookup (`scripts.get(oracleId)`), every `derive` and every
  `byPrinting` sees the copy with no second reader - the copied card's triggers fire for the token, its name is the
  token's name. Counters, damage, tapped-ness and every other status stay behind (707.2).
- `CopyExceptions` (oracle.ts) / `CardInstance.copyExceptions` (state.ts): the Legendary supertype dropped, types and
  subtypes added (in CR 205.2a's printed order), keywords added, a P/T set - read at LAYER 1 beside the printing
  (`withCopyExceptions`, derive.ts), so counters and pumps still stack on top. A copy of a copy carries the exceptions
  it found and takes the new clause's on top (707.3, 707.9b - `mergeExceptions`, effects.ts).
- `EffectSpec.copy` (`of: 'self' | 'target'`, the exceptions): `createToken` reads the copied object at RESOLUTION -
  the source (`this creature`, `this card` - wherever its card is) or the clause's aim; a face-down object copies as
  nothing (708.2) and the clause says so (D90); `token` stays null beside it.
- **A CREATED TOKEN ENTERS** (triggers.ts): `TokenCreated` is the token's entry, but a def declares one event kind and
  every enters def is a `CardsMoved` def - so a token copy of Wall of Omens never drew. The bus now offers the created
  token's OWN enters defs an entry view of the creation (a move onto the battlefield from elsewhere; `from` spelled
  exile, which no shipped matcher reads an entry from); a watcher of others' entries listens to `TokenCreated` itself.
- effectParse.ts: the copy rule before the table's (`Create N token(s) that's a copy / are copies of <the source | a
  target>(, except <exceptions>)`), `parseCopyExceptions` (a closed grammar: `it isn't legendary`, `it's an <artifact |
  Spirit ...> in addition to its other types`, `it has <grantable keywords>`, `it's N/N`; a piece outside it refuses the
  whole sentence), the referent `copy of it` (`REFERENT_COPY`), and the kicked-instead token copy as a REFERENT clause
  (`create five of those tokens instead` after a targeted copy took a second target index the cast never declared).
- `tokenCopy.test.ts` (5 tests): the readings and refusals; Cackling Counterpart's copy of a countered Bears is a plain
  2/2 Bears token (owner and controller p1, no counters, `copyOf` in the log); a copy of Wall of Omens draws; Saheeli's
  Artistry's second mode makes an `Artifact Creature` copy and Cackling Counterpart on THAT token keeps the exception;
  Rite of Replication kicked makes five Hill Giants. Three spells join the fixtures.

### The generator and the wave — 10 rows

The row maker admits the copy through the vocabulary (a `createToken` with `copy` and no `token`); the generated suite
counts the token on the board as it counts every token. The fuzz: two Cackling Counterparts a seat
(`tokenCopiesMade`) read 3 token copies over 60 seeds (fuzz60-485; the driver aims it at a creature it controls when it can) - seeds 0-59 are the gate's own first sixty, so the 500-seed floor holds by construction.

### Traps

- **A COPY IS ITS CARD.** Nothing reads a "copy of" pointer at derive or dispatch: the identity fields are the copied
  card's. Only the exceptions ride a field of their own, and only the copy effect writes it.
- **A CREATED TOKEN ENTERS.** Its own enters triggers fire off the bus's entry view; a matcher that read the view's
  `from` as exile would misfire on a created token.
- **A KICKED-INSTEAD TOKEN COPY AIMS WHERE THE BASE AIMED.** The instead clause is a referent, or it takes a target
  index the cast never declared and copies nothing.
- **THE WIDE ROW RUN READS `vocab-ok.json`** (D484's lesson, kept in `chain485.sh`): merge `vocab-ok-wide.json` into it
  before the wide run; pass `CRT_LINES=lines485.json` to the narrow run.

## D486 — THE CLONE: a permanent enters as a copy of another, decided before it enters (2026-09-17)

**11,486 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,467
(+19: 19 clones the seam completes with no script — Clone, Stunt Double, Mirror Image, Phyrexian Metamorph, Sculpting Steel, Copy Artifact, Copy Enchantment, Copy Land, Mirrormade, Vesuva, Echoing Deeps, Glasspool Mimic // Glasspool Shore, Sakashima's Student, Synth Infiltrator, Waxen Shapethief, Jwari Shapeshifter, Body Double, Malleable Impostor, Quicksilver Gargantuan (no row was needed: the line is the engine's)).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,549 → **7,549**. The REFUSED ledger 1,706 → **1,706** (unchanged - the stale-entry guard names nothing and the offer is empty). Fixtures 8,440 →
**8,444**. `scriptableToday` 1,791 → **1,791**; the ladder `[1791, 1797, 3105, 4641, 5874]`. Bot reach **4,725** from **356**.
An engine seam on Fable 5.1 - CR 707's second consumer.

### The measurement chose it — the clone, priced over the post-D485 leftover

`d486/price-copy486.cjs` over the post-D485 leftover: 64 clone lines / 47 sole - `any creature on the battlefield`
(Clone, Stunt Double), `any artifact or creature ... except it's an artifact in addition` (Phyrexian Metamorph), `a
creature you control` (Mirror Image), `any land ... tapped` (Vesuva), `any enchantment` (Copy Enchantment), `any
artifact` (Sculpting Steel), `any nonland permanent` (Clever Impersonator), `any creature card in a graveyard` (Body
Double), and the exceptions the D485 grammar reads. The rest print an exception outside the grammar (`it has` a quoted
ability 9, Sakashima's `other abilities` 3) or a condition on the copy, and stay unread by name.

### The engine seam (`d486/patch486-types(-b,-c).txt`, `patch486-parse.txt`, `patch486-funnel.txt`, `patch486-handlers.txt`, `patch486-clients.txt`)

- **A CLONE IS DECIDED BEFORE IT ENTERS.** `parseEntersAsCopyLine` (replacementParse.ts) reads the line onto
  `OracleFace.entersAsCopy` (the noun by `predicatesOf` - one reader with the search's and the sacrifice's; the scope
  `any` / `you` / `opponent`; the zone; the Vesuva tap; the exceptions by D485's closed grammar) and the accounting
  claims the line the way it claims `entersTapped`. `runReplacementFunnel` HOLDS a move that puts such a card onto the
  battlefield BEFORE the body's built-ins run (`cloneChoiceFor`): the record carries `copyChoice`, and the question
  (`Awaiting.chooseCopy`, built by `askPromptFor` - one builder for the clone's question and CR 616's) lists the
  candidates by the one reader (`copyCandidates`: the permanents the noun admits by their DERIVED characteristics, or
  a graveyard's cards by their printed face; the clone itself excluded; a face-down object is nothing to copy). With
  nothing to copy the card enters as itself and nobody is asked (D137's rule).
- `answerChooseCopy` (handlers.ts) rewrites the held move (`CardMove.asCopyOf`: the copied object's identity fields
  and the exceptions it carries with the face's own on top - 707.3 / 707.9b - or `copyDeclined`) and runs the body
  through the WHOLE funnel from its start: `enteringFace` reads the arriving face as the copy's, so the copied card's
  entry rules run, and the bus then fires the copied card's enters triggers - Clone entering as a Wall of Omens
  draws. The Vesuva form appends the tap after the move.
- reducer.ts: a move with `asCopyOf` rewrites `oracleId` / `printingId` / `faceIndex` and keeps the printed card as
  `CardInstance.original`; a move off the battlefield restores it (707.4 / 400.7) and drops the exceptions.
- Five clients answer the new prompt: the fuzz driver (a random candidate, itself one time in four), the bot (the
  strongest by the view's order), the net script and the harness (the first candidate), the prompt bar (numbered
  buttons and `Enter as itself`).
- `clone.test.ts` (5 tests): the readings and refusals; Clone entering as a Wall of Omens draws and is a Clone again
  when bounced; a declined Clone is a 0/0 the state-based actions bin, a non-candidate refused; Phyrexian Metamorph's
  copy of a countered Bears is an `Artifact Creature` 2/2 with no counter; Vesuva enters tapped as a Forest. Four
  fixtures join.

### The wave — the seam completes, no rows

The clone's line is the ENGINE's now (a face field, a funnel question, a move field), so every card whose only
leftover piece was it lands with no script: Clone, Stunt Double, Mirror Image, Phyrexian Metamorph, Sculpting Steel, Copy Artifact, Copy Enchantment, Copy Land, Mirrormade, Vesuva, Echoing Deeps, Glasspool Mimic // Glasspool Shore, Sakashima's Student, Synth Infiltrator, Waxen Shapethief, Jwari Shapeshifter, Body Double, Malleable Impostor, Quicksilver Gargantuan. No row was generated and none was needed; the classifier offers nothing. The fuzz: a Clone a seat (`clonesEntered`),
a Clone a seat read 4 clones over 60 seeds (fuzz60-486; the driver copies a random creature three times in four) - seeds 0-59 are the gate's own first sixty, so the 500-seed floor holds by construction. The leftover diff names Sorcerer's Broom as regressed only because D485's probe ran before its suite was unlanded.

### Traps

- **A CLONE IS DECIDED BEFORE IT ENTERS.** The move is HELD by the funnel and rewritten by the answer; an apply-then-
  patch would enter the card as itself and miss the copied card's entry rules and enters triggers.
- **A COPY LEAVING IS ITS PRINTED CARD AGAIN.** `original` rides the instance for exactly that move; a token copy has
  none and ceases anyway.
- **THE ONE READER FOR THE CANDIDATES.** The funnel's question and the handler's check both ask `copyCandidates`; a
  second list would let the two disagree (D139).
- **TWO OPTIONAL `faceIndex` FIELDS IN ONE FILE.** The events patch anchored on `readonly faceIndex?: number;` matched
  the D485 token field too; the applier refused (counted), and the anchor took its doc line.

## D487 — THE SPELL COPY: a copy of a spell is a stack object of its own, aimed after it exists (2026-09-17)

**11,490 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 11,486
(+4: 4 cards the seam completes with no script — Reverberate, Twincast, Fork, Expansion // Explosion (no row was needed: the line is the engine's)).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,549 → **7,549**. The REFUSED ledger 1,706 → **1,709** (+3: Dualcaster Mage, Sigil Tracer and Uyo, Silent Prophet - a copy-spell body under a head the suite cannot stage). Fixtures 8,444 →
**8,448**. `scriptableToday` 1,791 → **1,794**; the ladder `[1794, 1800, 3108, 4644, 5877]`. Bot reach **4,725** from **356**.
An engine seam on Fable 5.1 - CR 707's third consumer.

### The measurement chose it — the spell copy, priced over the post-D486 leftover

The copy family after the token copy (D485) and the clone (D486): the SPELL copy at 232 leftover lines / 97 sole
(`d485/price-copy485.cjs`) - `Copy target instant or sorcery spell. You may choose new targets for the copy.`
(Reverberate, Twincast), Fork's `except that the copy is red`, Expansion's `with mana value 4 or less`, and the
heads over the same body (Dualcaster Mage's enters, Sigil Tracer's and Uyo's activations, Doublecast's `When you next
cast`, Increasing Vengeance's `copy that spell twice instead`, Narset's Reversal's `then return it`). The bare body is
the seam; the heads and the riders stay unread by name.

### The engine seam (`d487/patch487-types.txt`, `patch487-parse.txt`, `patch487-effects.txt`, `patch487-loop.txt`, `patch487-handlers.txt`, `patch487-clients.txt`, `patch487-fuzz(-b,-c,-d).txt`)

- **A COPY IS ON THE STACK BEFORE IT IS AIMED.** The parser's `copySpell` rule (effectParse.ts, beside `counter`)
  reads `Copy target instant or sorcery spell(, except that the copy is <colour>).` with the optional second sentence
  `You may choose new targets for the copy.` folded into the clause (`EffectSpec.newTargets`); a noun without
  `instant` or `sorcery` is refused (a permanent spell's copy would resolve into a token, 707.10a - not made). The
  executor (`case 'copySpell'`, effects.ts) builds a NEW `StackObject` from the target: `card` null, `source` the
  copied spell's card, `copyOf` its printing and face (a copy's own where the target is itself a copy), the modes, X
  and kick carried, the targets and slots the original's, `identity` the copy's colours (Fork: `CopyExceptions.colors`),
  a fresh id past every copy the batch already made; `SpellCopied` puts it on top (the reducer: no cast recorded, no
  pending cast ended, every other player yet to see it). Where the clause says so and the copy has targets, the
  question follows in the same batch: `Awaiting.chooseTargets` with `forKind: 'copy'`, `stackId` the copy's, `count`
  0 - the D484 continuation rides it (`withContinuation` learned the kind), so a clause after the copying one runs
  once the targets are settled.
- `chooseCopyTargets` (handlers.ts): an empty answer keeps the original's targets; a full one is validated against the
  copied face's clauses exactly as a trigger's are (`validateTargets`, the copied spell's card the targeting source,
  the copy's colours where set) and rewrites the copy's targets (`StackTargetsSet`); the continuation resumes.
- **A COPY HAS NO CARD.** `resolveTop` (loop.ts) resolves a copy before the card branch: the face off `copyOf` (its
  colours the copy's), fizzle and the still-legal picks decided on it (608.2b), a shipped def or the vocabulary run
  over it with the copied spell's card as `self` / the source - and then it ceases: `StackResolved` with `card` null,
  nothing moves. A counter on a copy moves nothing either (the executor's `counter` already read `victim.card`).
  `candidatesFromState` (targets.ts) reads a copy's types, mana value and colours off its own printing, so a copy is a
  proper `target spell` for the next counter or copy.
- Five clients answer the new prompt: the fuzz driver (keeps one time in three, else a random legal set, keeps when
  none), the harness and the net script (the first legal set, keep when none), the bot (its planned set, keep when
  none or on a retry), the prompt bar (the arrow onto new targets, or `Keep targets`).
- `spellCopy.test.ts` (6 tests): the readings and refusals; Reverberate copying an opponent's Bolt and aiming the copy
  back at them (both resolve, each for three, the copy on top of the original); the empty answer keeps the target
  and an illegal new set is refused; Fork's copy is red; Twincast copying the copy (a copy has a printing of its own);
  a copy whose target has gone fizzles and leaves nothing behind. Four fixtures join.

### The wave — the seam completes, no rows

The copy's line is the ENGINE's now (a parser rule, an executor case, a resolution branch), so every instant or
sorcery whose only leftover piece was it lands with no script: Reverberate, Twincast, Fork, Expansion // Explosion. No row was generated and none was needed; the three the seam made offerable (Dualcaster Mage, Sigil Tracer, Uyo, Silent Prophet - a copy-spell body under a head) are ledgered, because the suite cannot stage a spell on the stack for the body to copy. The fuzz: four
Expansion // Explosions a seat (`spellsCopied`) under two driver rules (see the traps) - four Expansion // Explosions a seat under the two driver rules read 1 copy and 2 clones over 60 seeds (fuzz60-487, canary487d.out; two Reverberates read 0, two Expansions read 0, the copy-first pick alone read 0 - diag487: a copier in hand at 4% of the stack decisions, a spell to copy on the stack at 16%) - seeds 0-59 are the gate's own first sixty, so the 500-seed floor holds by construction, thinly. The leftover diff: 4 newly complete, nothing regressed

### Traps

- **A COPY IS ON THE STACK BEFORE IT IS AIMED.** The copy exists (`SpellCopied`) before its controller is asked; the
  answer rewrites a real object's targets. Asking first would leave nothing for the answer to aim.
- **A COPY HAS NO CARD.** `card` is null and `copyOf` carries the printing; every reader that took `obj.card` for
  the face (the resolution, the stack candidates) reads `copyOf` first. Nothing moves when a copy resolves, fizzles
  or is countered.
- **THE COPY FUEL IS TWO DRIVER RULES.** Reverberate ({R}{R}) read 0 copies over 60 seeds, and so did Expansion //
  Explosion's {U/R}{U/R} half under the uniform pick: the driver held a copier at 4% of its stack decisions and had an
  instant or sorcery on the stack at 16% (`diag487`), and the two never met. So the driver casts a copier FIRST when a
