A keyword action on Fable 5.1 (the model rule: a token the engine had to make and a choice it had to ask), built the
D168 way against the family the ranking after D519 named: five proofs, the tooling, the wave.

### The measurement chose it — the family ranking after D519, read back

The mechanical tail stayed flat; among the keyword actions the whole leftover still carried, amass was the largest whose
sole-line rows were one payload (56 rows mention it: 23 `Amass Zombies/Orcs N.` payloads under an enters, a dies or a
spell, the rest `where X is` forms, `, then` compounds and `When you do` reflexives). Bolster (D511) was the precedent
for the verb - computed candidates, a tie asked, the only one unasked - and D505's scratch state for a candidate the
same clause creates.

### The seam (`src/engine/types/state.ts`, `events.ts`, `oracle.ts`, `reducer.ts`, `derive.ts`, `effects.ts`, `handlers.ts`, `src/bot/awaiting.ts`, `src/data/tokenParse.ts`, `tokenTable.node.test.ts`, `tokenTable.ts`, `effectParse.ts`, `src/engine/fuzz.node.test.ts`)

- **THE VERB** (`amass.test.ts`). `Amass [Subtype] N` (CR 701.47a): if you control no Army creature token, create a 0/0
  black [subtype] Army creature token; choose an Army creature token you control; put N +1/+1 counters on it; it
  becomes the subtype in addition to its other types. The queue's seventh verb: the candidates are COMPUTED
  (`armyTokens` - the Army creature tokens the player controls), read off the state the clauses before it left
  (D505's scratch); none - the table's Army is created first and is the one candidate, unasked; several - the caster is
  asked with the `army` pick (a printed rule, never ids - D137); the batch puts the counters, adds the subtype once
  (`CardInstance.addedSubtypes`, derived at layer 4 with no duration, cleared when the object leaves like the chosen
  type) and says so; the marker `Amassed` on every path, `CreatureSubtypeAdded` the fact. `Amass X`, the `, then`
  forms and a subtype the table has no Army for (`Amass Goblins`) stay unread.
- **THE TOKEN.** No card prints the Army's description (the reminder text's clause carries a condition and a `first`),
  so the baked table had none and a created Army would have been D133's blank: the builder seeds `Create a 0/0 black
  <Subtype> Army creature token.` from every amass line, and the parser, the pool (`tokenPrintingIdsIn`) and the table
  read ONE spelling of it (`amassArmyClause`); the Zombie, Orc and Sliver Armies are pinned to the printings the table
  names. The keyword is capitalised at a sentence head and lower-case under a trigger; the detection reads both.
- **THE FUZZ.** The `amasses` counter; Relentless Advance, Lazotep Reaver and Dunland Crebain two a seat (the Army made
  and grown, the Orc onto a Zombie Army); the floor asks for an amass at gate size (6 amasses over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-520 - the staples Relentless Advance, Lazotep Reaver and Dunland Crebain two a seat); the driver and the
  bot answer the `army` pick off the host's own set (the biggest Army first).

### The tooling (`d520/patch520-tools.cjs`)

The vocab generator asserts an amass by the marker: the Army it names is a creature token under p1 carrying N +1/+1
counters (a fresh 0/0 when p1 controlled none - the board grows by one - else the one Army p1 controls; the suites
stage no second Army, so nothing is asked). The row maker pins the Army an amass makes like a created token's.

### The wave — ten rows and eleven spells

The select offered nothing; the whole-leftover row maker (18,988 line-only rows, `d520/rows520-all.log`) rowed 13 - the three it always rows and 10 of the family: the enters amasses (Lazotep Reaver, Invading Manticore, Dunland Crebain, Aven Eternal), the dies amasses (Grim Initiate, Easterling Vanguard, Herald of the Dreadhorde, Warbeast of Gorgoroth's power-4 scope), Angrath's −2 loyalty line and Saruman the White's second-spell head; the generator built the 10 - 10 suites, 22 tests, green first time. Eleven of the family's spells needed no row: every line parses, so they are complete on the seam alone (the row maker refuses every instant and sorcery as a class, and only the probe diff showed them). Thirty-five cards join the ledger with their reasons (the family's residue, read by name - the `where X is` and `, then` forms, the reflexive `When you do`, the token-scoped statics `Zombie tokens you control have ...`, the heads not in the library); sixteen retire (the eleven spells now complete, five re-reasoned - `amass mechanic` is no longer a reason).

### Traps

- **THE KEYWORD'S TOKEN IS NOBODY'S DESCRIPTION.** A description no card prints is absent from the baked table, and a
  created token the table cannot name is D133's blank; the keyword line seeds it, once, where the parser and the pool
  read it.
- **THE CANDIDATES ARE READ OFF THE SCRATCH STATE.** The Army an amass creates is a candidate of the same clause; a queue
  over the resolution-start state would ask nothing and count nothing.
- **A 0/0 TOKEN LIVES ONLY WITH ITS COUNTERS IN THE SAME BATCH.** The state-based check bins a 0/0 the moment a manual
  create lands; the executor's resolution and a proof's setup put the counters beside the token.
- **A SPELL IS NEVER A ROW.** The row maker refuses every instant and sorcery whatever its lines say; a spell whose
  lines all parse is complete on its own, and only the probe diff shows it.

## D521 — THE RING TEMPTS YOU: a temptation the engine asks, an emblem whose abilities climb with the count (2026-09-22)

**12,138 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,118
(+20: 12 rows - Shortcut to Mushrooms, Took Reaper, Relentless Rohirrim, Stalwarts of Osgiliath, Rohirrim Lancer, Gollum, Patient Plotter, Bilbo, Retired Burglar, Inherited Envelope, Mirrormere Guardian, Fiery Inscription, Uruk-hai Berserker, Enraged Huorn; 8 spells complete on the seam alone - Claim the Precious, Birthday Escape, Ranger's Firebrand, Sam's Desperate Rescue, The Black Breath, Now for Wrath, Now for Ruin!, Bombadil's Song, Soothing of Sméagol (a spell is never a row; every line parses, so `effectMode` is auto); the probe diff is the 20, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,949 → **7,962**. The REFUSED ledger 1,948 → **1,969** (+33 / -12: the family's residue by reason - 9 spells (the temptation before another ask - The Ring Goes South, Ringsight; a conditional temptation - Glorious Gale; a line beside the temptation outside the vocabulary - Slip On the Ring's flicker, Breaking of the Fellowship's bite, Sauron's Ransom's piles, Dreadful as the Storm's base P/T, Horses of the Bruinen's double bounce; Gollum's Bite's graveyard activation) and 24 permanents (the `if you chose a creature other than ~ as your Ring-bearer` condition on the head - Aragorn, Galadriel of Lothlórien, Gandalf, Faramir; the intervening ifs - Sméagol, Galadriel Elven-Queen, Dúnedain Rangers; the sagas - There and Back Again, Scroll of Isildur, War of the Last Alliance, In the Darkness Bind Them, One Ring to Rule Them All; the heads not in the library - Witch-king of Angmar, Call of the Ring, Frodo Baggins, Samwise; Nazgûl's deck rule, Lord of the Nazgûl's protection from Ring-bearers, Frodo's partner, Boromir, Sauron the Necromancer, Ringwraiths, Elrond, Rangers of Ithilien); the twelve retired are the five spells the seam completed and seven re-reasoned; the two Saurons' entries stand). Fixtures 9,000 →
**9,015**. `scriptableToday` 1,889 → **1,885**; the ladder `[1885, 1899, 3194, 4663, 5814]`. Bot reach **4,992** from **388**.
A new subsystem on Fable 5.1 (the model rule: a choice the engine had to ask, a seat's count it had to keep and an
emblem whose abilities unlock on it), built the D168 way against the largest family the ranking after D520 named: six
proofs, the tooling, the wave.

### The measurement chose it — the family ranking after D520, read back

The mechanical tail stayed flat; among the keyword actions the whole leftover still carried, the Ring was the largest
(55 rows mention it, 29 sole-line `The Ring tempts you.` payloads under an enters, a dies, a leaves or a spell's last
sentence; the rest the `Whenever the Ring tempts you` head with the `if you chose a creature other than ~` condition, the
Ring-bearer referents, the sagas). The monarch's 25 `you become the monarch` rows are a parser seam over a subsystem
the engine has (D332) - Opus-shaped, noted for the switch. Bolster (D511) was the precedent for the verb, the poison
counter for the seat, D475's emblem for the object.

### The seam (`src/engine/types/state.ts`, `events.ts`, `oracle.ts`, `intents.ts`, `reducer.ts`, `invariants.ts`, `project.ts`, `derive.ts`, `combat.ts`, `effects.ts`, `handlers.ts`, `manual.ts`, `src/engine/scripts/cards/theRing.ts` + `registry.ts`, `src/data/effectParse.ts`, `tokenParse.ts`, `src/bot/awaiting.ts`, `src/view/types.ts`, `src/ui/hud/PlayerPlate.tsx`, `src/ui/game/ManualTools.tsx`, `src/engine/fuzz.node.test.ts`)

- **THE TEMPTATION** (`ring.test.ts`). `The Ring tempts you.` (CR 701.54a): the caster chooses a creature they control as
  their Ring-bearer. The queue's eighth verb: the candidates are every creature the player controls
  (`ringBearerCandidates`), read off the state the clauses before it left (the Wraith In the Darkness Bind Them just
  made is one); several - the caster is asked with the `ringBearer` pick (a printed rule, never ids - D137); the only
  one goes unasked; none still counts. The batch records `RingTempted { player, times, bearer }` and gives the Ring
  emblem with the first temptation (`EmblemCreated` of the one printing `RING_EMBLEM` names, into the command zone).
  The `Then` form reads; the ask is the sentence's last.
- **THE SEAT.** `players[p].ringTempts` and `players[p].ringBearer` (0 / null at setup): the bearer is cleared where the
  object moves (the reducer's move and control cases - a bearer that leaves is a new object, one another player takes
  stops bearing, CR 701.54a) and the invariant checks it sits on the battlefield under its seat; projected
  (`SeatView.ringTempts` / `ringBearer`), shown on the plate with the bearer named (💍, `data-ring`), set by the
  wrench (`ManualRingTempt`: the count rises, the bearer stays, the emblem arrives with the first).
- **THE EMBLEM.** Four abilities, one per temptation (CR 701.54d). The first is the ENGINE's: the bearer is legendary
  (`derive`, layer 4, read off the seat) and can't be blocked by creatures with greater power (`combat.ts`'s `canBlock`,
  the rejection `ringBearer`, said). The other three are the emblem's script (`theRing.ts`, in the shipped registry,
  three triggers gated on the seat's count and running from the command zone): the attack loot (draw, then discard),
  the blocker's sacrifice at end of combat (a delayed trigger armed with the blocker as its aim - the vocabulary's own
  `sacrificeObj`, unbound from its clause), the combat-damage drain (each opponent loses 3 life). The pool carries the
  emblem for every card the Ring tempts (`tokenPrintingIdsIn`); the fixtures pin the same printing.
- **THE FUZZ.** `ringTempts` / `ringAbilities` counters; Claim the Precious, Birthday Escape, Took Reaper and Relentless
  Rohirrim two a seat; the floor asks for a temptation at gate size (12 temptations over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-521 - the staples Claim the Precious, Birthday Escape, Took Reaper and Relentless Rohirrim two a seat; the emblem's abilities fired none at sixty (the count climbs slowly) - counted, not floored); the driver and the bot answer the
  `ringBearer` pick off the host's own set (the biggest creature first).

### The tooling (`d521/patch521-tools.cjs`)

The row maker reads the temptation head (`Whenever the Ring tempts you, ...`) and knows the payload asks (last in its
sentence); the generator's head library fires it by the wrench, waits for the bearer's ask and answers it with the row
card (a creature on the battlefield) or the first creature p1 controls; the vocab generator asserts the count, the
bearer (p1's or none) and the emblem in the command zone - the board is untouched.

### The wave — twelve rows and eight spells

The select offered nothing; the whole-leftover row maker (18,967 line-only rows, `d521/rows521-all.log`) rowed 15 - the three it always rows and 12 of the family: the enters temptations (Relentless Rohirrim, Stalwarts of Osgiliath, Uruk-hai Berserker, Enraged Huorn), the dies temptations (Took Reaper, Rohirrim Lancer, Mirrormere Guardian), the leaves heads (Gollum, Patient Plotter; Bilbo, Retired Burglar's enters-or-leaves), the artifact and the enchantments that tempt (Inherited Envelope, Shortcut to Mushrooms, Fiery Inscription); the generator built the 12 - 12 suites, 30 tests, green first time. Eight of the family's spells needed no row: every line parses, so they are complete on the seam alone (a spell is never a row; the probe diff showed them). The temptation head landed nothing yet: Nazgûl carries a deck rule the vocabulary does not read, and Gandalf, Faramir, Aragorn and Galadriel gate the head on `if you chose a creature other than ~ as your Ring-bearer` - one condition kind away. Thirty-three cards join the ledger with their reasons (the family's residue, read by name); twelve retire (the five spells now complete, seven re-reasoned - `the Ring mechanic` is no longer a reason).

### Traps

- **AN EMBLEM'S ABILITIES ARE ITS SCRIPT'S, AND A GAME MUST CARRY THE REGISTRY.** The bus walks the command zone, but only
  for the scripts the game's registry holds; the harness defaults to none, the shipped registry carries the Ring.
- **THE FIRST ABILITY IS THE ENGINE'S, NOT THE SCRIPT'S.** A type rewrite on another object and a blocking restriction
  are derive's and combat's, keyed on the seat, so the object and the count cannot disagree.
- **A SEAT'S POINTER IS CLEARED WHERE THE OBJECT MOVES.** The reducer's move and control cases clear the bearer; the
  invariant checks it; no reader re-validates it.
- **A PROOF OF A DELAYED SACRIFICE MUST NOT LET COMBAT KILL THE OBJECT FIRST.** A 2/2 bearer trades with a 2/2 blocker;
  the level-3 proof blocks with a 1/3.

family the ranking after D521 named: five proofs, the tooling, the wave.

### The measurement chose it — the family ranking after D521, read back

D332 built the crown (CR 724: `state.monarch`, `MonarchChanged`, the end-step draw, the combat steal) and hand-wrote one
script for Thorn of the Black Rose. Fifty-four leftover rows print the monarch — 32 of them the sentence that hands the
crown over (`When this creature enters, you become the monarch.` 15, `When this enchantment enters, ...` 12, the named
forms 4, an Aura 1) — and the engine had no vocabulary for it, no chip for it and no tool for it. That is a parser seam
over an existing subsystem: Opus-shaped, and it was the largest such seam on the list.

### The seam (`src/engine/types/oracle.ts`, `events.ts`, `intents.ts`, `project.ts`, `manual.ts`, `effects.ts`, `src/data/effectParse.ts`, `src/view/types.ts`, `src/ui/hud/PlayerPlate.tsx`, `src/ui/game/ManualTools.tsx`, `src/engine/fuzz.node.test.ts`)

- **THE PAYLOAD** (`monarch.test.ts`). `You become the monarch.` and `Target opponent | player becomes the monarch.` are
  the kind `becomeMonarch` (CR 724.2): the named player takes the crown and the previous monarch loses it; a player who
  already wears it becomes nothing — no state moves, so no event and no trigger — and the log says so. The `Then` form
  reads; the turn restriction beside it (Jared Carthalion's `You can't become the monarch this turn.`) stays unread.
- **THE CROWN, SEEN AND SET.** `SeatView.isMonarch`, the plate's 👑 chip (`data-monarch`, titled with what the crown
  does), and `ManualSetMonarch` — which crowns a seat or takes the crown off the table entirely (no rule does that; a
  table setting a board up by hand has to be able to). D122's rule; D332 had shipped the crown enforced and invisible,
  the shape poison shipped in once (D68) and energy avoided (D519).
- **THE CONDITION.** `you're the monarch` / `an opponent is the monarch` / `there is no monarch` join the closed
  condition vocabulary (`gen222-cond.cjs`): the generated helper reads `ctx.state.monarch` (never a derived
  characteristic — D317), and the stage arms both sides of the bound with the wrench.
- **THE UPKEEP HEAD FIRES TWICE** (CR 603.4). `At the beginning of your upkeep, if <condition>, <payload>` is the
  family's commonest shape and the whole leftover's too. It joins D400's refire heads: the suite walks to turn 5's
  upkeep with the condition BROKEN (nothing on the stack), arms it there, and walks to turn 7's — reading every
  baseline at the fire's own step. Only a condition about persistent board state may ride it; a turn-record condition
  would be armed on the wrong turn and is refused by name.
- **THE FUZZ.** The `crownings` counter (every `MonarchChanged`: a payload's, the wrench's, D332's combat steal); Grave
  Venerations, Garrulous Sycophant and Throne Warden two a seat; the floor asks for the crown to move at gate size
  (1 crowning over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-522 - Grave Venerations and Garrulous Sycophant / Throne Warden two a seat; Thorn of the Black Rose (D332's own script) joined the staple for the gate, so the crown moves oftener there).

### The tooling (`d522/patch522-tools.cjs`, `-b`, `-c`, `-d`, `-e`, `-f`)

The condition reader, the helper and the stage; the vocab generator's `becomeMonarch` assert (the seat the clause named
wears it); the upkeep head in the peel list and in the refire set, with its own stage-one walk; the broken side armed
from the condition's own `brk` recipe; the baselines read at the fire's step; and the crown's own end-step draw on the
hand baseline (`handAdj`) for an end-step row gated on wearing it.

### The wave — sixteen rows and one spell

The select offered nothing; the whole-leftover row maker (18,947 line-only rows, `d522/rows522-all.log`) rowed 21 - the three it always rows, 5 of the monarch family (Garrulous Sycophant, Throne Warden, Grave Venerations, Denethor Stone Seer's aimed activation, Éomer King of Rohan's aimed enters) and 13 the upkeep peel unlocked across the whole leftover (Scute Mob, Dragonmaster Outcast, Emeria the Sky Ruin, Convalescence, Convalescent Care, Mirror-Sigil Sergeant, Gixian Skullflayer, Bloodhall Ooze, Complex Automaton, Soul Swallower, Skyline Despot ...). Sixteen landed - 16 suites, 38 tests, green once the broken side was ARMED rather than assumed, the baselines read at the fire's own step and the crown's own end-step draw counted - and TWO were dropped at the trial: Inventors' Fair and Thopter Spy Network, whose other ability arms the very condition their upkeep trigger must break (both ledgered by name). Feast of Succession needed no row. Forty-seven cards join the ledger with their reasons (the family's residue, read by name, and the two dropped rows); one retires (Feast of Succession, whose reason said only `monarch mechanic`).

### Traps

- **THE BROKEN SIDE IS ARMED, NOT ASSUMED.** The row's other abilities arm the board first, and one of them may satisfy
  the condition before the walk; every breakable condition carries a `brk` recipe now, and a row whose condition has
  none is refused by name.
- **THE BASELINES ARE READ WHERE THE FIRE IS.** Two turns between the arm and the fire draw cards.
- **THE CROWN DRAWS A CARD OF ITS OWN** (CR 724.3). Arming the monarch under an end-step head turns on a draw at that
  very step, before the payload resolves.
- **A SUBSYSTEM THE ENGINE ENFORCES BUT NOBODY CAN SEE OR SET.** The crown drew a card every end step for 190
  decisions with nothing on the plate saying so.

## D523 — THE GATED CLAUSE: a sentence whose second reading the board decides (2026-09-23)

**12,173 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,155
(+18: For the Family, View from Above, You're Not Alone, Thoughtweft Charge, Resourceful Return, Life Goes On, Strength of Arms, Fungal Rebirth, Jace's Triumph, Hour of Promise, Sage's Dousing, Pack's Betrayal, Huatli's Spurring, Recalibrate, Slick Sequence, Rabbit Response, Psychic Whorl, Surge of Thoughtweft — all eighteen complete on the seam alone - no row was needed and none was taken (a spell is never a row; every line of each parses now, so `effectMode` is auto); the probe diff is the 18, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` unchanged at **7,978**. The REFUSED ledger 2,015 → **2,079** (+65 / -1: the gated riders whose condition the closed union still does not read - the CAST-TIME facts (`this spell was cast from a graveyard` 13, `five or more mana was spent to cast that spell` 8, `cast from anywhere other than your hand` 3, `that spell's mana value is 5 or greater` 4), the predicates just outside it (`you control a creature with power 4 or greater` 5, `three or more creatures with different powers` 2, `the sacrificed creature's toughness was 4 or greater`, `creatures you control have total power 10 or greater`, `two or more creatures are tied for least toughness`) and the reflexive reads (`it was a creature card` 3); the one retired is Sage's Dousing, which the seam finished). Fixtures 9,035 →
**9,037**. `scriptableToday` 1,884 → **1,914**; the ladder `[1914, 1929, 3220, 4683, 5819]`. Bot reach **5,009** from **390**.
A seam-only decision on Opus 5 (the model rule: a bounded seam with a precedent — D423 built this exact shape for one
condition): three proofs, one tooling line, and no wave at all.

### The measurement chose it — the monarch family's own reportable, read back

D522 ended naming the conditional rider inside a payload as the biggest shape the monarch family left, and the
measurement over the whole leftover agreed: **146 rows carry a rider gated on BOARD state** (`If you're the monarch,
<other> instead`, `Then if you control four or more creatures, <extra>`, `If a creature died this turn, <extra>`), 109
of them sole-line rows — and 55 of them are SPELLS, which need no script at all. D423 had already built the shape for
`If this spell was kicked`: one condition, hard-coded as two booleans on the spec.

### The seam (`src/engine/types/oracle.ts`, `activationConditions.ts`, `effects.ts`, `src/data/activatedParse.ts`, `effectParse.ts`, `src/engine/fuzz.node.test.ts`)

- **THE CONDITION IS ALREADY WRITTEN** (`gatedClause.test.ts`). `ActivationCondition` is the closed union `Activate only
  if ...` has read since D348 and `activationConditionsHold` has evaluated since — `controlCount`, `controlsCommander`,
  the turn record, the board queries. `parseGateCondition` asks that reader for ONE phrase, so a card's rider and its
  activation restriction cannot read the same words two ways. The crown (D522's `state.monarch`) joined the union in
  the same stroke, which also gives `Activate only if you're the monarch` for free.
- **THE GATE.** `EffectSpec.gate` carries the conditions; `gateInstead` says the clause REPLACES the one before it. The
  parser reads all three printed forms against the sentence before them (a referent, the way D423's kicked rider and
  D392's referents are read): `that creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn instead` aims where the base aimed rather
  than declaring a second target the cast never made.
- **WHERE IT IS ASKED.** At resolution, over the board the clauses before it left (CR 608.2): the events so far are
  applied to a scratch state first, exactly as a scope walk reads its members (D505). An unmet gate does nothing and
  says so (D90); a met `instead` gate skips the clause before it, and says that too.
- **THE FUZZ.** The `gatedClauses` counter reads the executor's own narration — a gate that fails changes nothing, so
  there is no event to count — with For the Family and Resourceful Return two a seat and a floor at gate size
  (10 gated clauses over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-523 - For the Family and Resourceful Return two a seat).

### The tooling — one line, and it is a refusal (`d523/patch523-tools.cjs`, `-b`)

A gated clause is not a row payload this wave: the suite arms the board for the ROW's other abilities, never for the
gate, so it would assert whichever branch the arm happened to take. The refusal lives on the vocabulary SNAPSHOT (a
proxy over `VOCAB_OK`), because the first cut guarded one of its four callers and the trigger-payload path took a gated
payload anyway.

### The wave — eighteen spells and no rows

There was no wave, and that is the decision: the row maker REFUSES a payload carrying a gated clause (the snapshot proxy in make-rows223), because the suite arms the board for the ROW's own abilities and would then assert whichever branch the arm happened to take - D522's own trap one layer down. The gate serves SPELLS here, which need no row: the whole-leftover probe found 18 of them complete on the seam alone (For the Family's `instead` rider, Resourceful Return's plain one, Hour of Promise, Fungal Rebirth, Slick Sequence, Sage's Dousing ...), and the whole-leftover row maker offered nothing but the three it always rows and the two D522 dropped. Sixty-five cards join the ledger with their reasons - the riders whose CONDITION the closed union still does not read (13 `cast from a graveyard`, 8 `five or more mana was spent`, the power and toughness predicates, the tied-toughness and total-power counts); one retires (Sage's Dousing, whose reason named an ask that had to be last).

### Traps

- **A GATE IS NOT A ROW PAYLOAD.** And the refusal belongs where the snapshot is read, not at one caller of it.
- **THE CONDITION UNION IS ALREADY WRITTEN.** Two readers of the same words is how they come to disagree; this decision
  added a phrase-level entry point to the one that existed rather than a second vocabulary.
- **A GATE IS ASKED AT RESOLUTION, OVER THE SCRATCH STATE.** The clauses before it have already moved the board.
⚠️ **Reportables** (D523): THE GATE INSIDE A PAYLOAD - the row maker refuses a gated clause because the suite arms the
board for the ROW and would assert whichever branch the arm took, so ~100 rows (the ten Courts among them) wait on a
stage machinery that can arm both sides of a gate a row's other abilities also touch: that is the next tooling
decision, and it unlocks the monarch riders D522 named as well as every `if you control X, do more` rider. Beside it,
the conditions the union still does not read: the CAST-TIME facts (`as you cast this spell` 13 - the modal Wills;

## D524 — THE GATE INSIDE A PAYLOAD: the suite arms the branch it asserts (2026-09-23)

**12,182 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,173
(+9: Court of Grace, Gangrenous Zombies, Zimone Quandrix Prodigy, Screeching Silcaw, Aragorn King of Gondor, Scroll of Avacyn, Tragic Banshee, Slaughterhouse Bouncer, Slimy Piper — nine rows, nine scripts, and every one of them a card D522 or earlier refused because the pump it prints sits behind a gated clause; the probe diff is the 9, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,978 → **7,987**. The REFUSED ledger 2,079 → **2,117** (+40 / -2: the 38 coin flips beside a gate, Flame Discharge's `you controlled a modified creature as you cast this spell`, and Scute Swarm, whose gate the suite must not arm; the two retired are Court of Grace and Aragorn, King of Gondor, both landed by this wave). Fixtures 9,037 →
**9,046**. `scriptableToday` 1,914 → **1,905**; the ladder `[1905, 1920, 3211, 4674, 5810]`. Bot reach **5,012** from **391**.
A TOOLING decision on Opus 5 (the model rule: a mechanical wave with a precedent) — the engine did
not change at all. D523 built the gate and refused every row that carried one; this decision teaches
the suite to ARM it.

### The measurement chose it — D523 named it and priced it

D523's closing measurement put ~100 rows behind one sentence: *the stage machinery cannot arm both
sides of a gate a row's other abilities also touch*. That refusal was correct and it was expensive —
the ten Courts, the metalcraft and landfall riders, the monarch riders D522 left, every
`If you control X, do more` payload. The gate itself was already read, evaluated and narrated; only
the suite could not be trusted to assert it, because it armed the board for the ROW and then read
whichever branch the arm happened to take.

### The tooling (`d524/patch524-cond.cjs`, `patch524-tools.cjs`, `-b`, `-c`, `patch524-guard.cjs`)

- **THE CONDITION, TRANSLATED** (`gen224-cond.cjs`). A payload's gate carries the ENGINE's
  `ActivationCondition`; the suite's stage machinery speaks the generator's own closed condition
  vocabulary. `condFromGate` maps one onto the other for every kind that HAS a meet recipe — the
  crown (D522), a control count, a board predicate, the commander, the hand size, the graveyard
  count, the turn record — and returns null for the rest, so a gate the suite cannot arm is refused
  BY NAME rather than asserted on whichever branch the arm took. `predFromEngine` reads the engine's
  `PermanentPredicate` into the pred shape `fixtureFor` can name a card for.
- **THE READING** (`make-rows224.cjs`). D523's refusal sits on the vocabulary SNAPSHOT, a Proxy over
  `VOCAB_OK` that hides a gated payload from all four readers. `vocabReading` reads the RAW snapshot
  now and arms the gate itself; every other reader (the granted path, the quoted path, D415's
  printed-sentence fallback) still sees nothing. A row refused for its gate says which gate and why.
- **THE ARM** (`gen-oneshot224.cjs`). The gate's deck fixtures ride the row's, and its MEET recipe is
  played per ability BEFORE the baselines — where the intervening if's own recipe is played — so the
  clause the asserts read is the one the board makes true, and its deltas are counted like any other.
- **THE `instead` GATE, ADMITTED** (`gen224-vocab.cjs`). With the gate armed MET, a gated `instead`
  clause REPLACES the one before it (D523's executor skips the base), so `countedEffects` drops the
  replaced clause from the single list the asserts walk.

### The wave — nine rows, and the tenth is the trap

Ten rows generated; nine are green. Scute Swarm failed by six: its gate is
`if you control six or more lands` and its head is landfall, so the six lands the recipe played fired
the ability six times before the ability under test ever fired — and each of those fires COPIED the
source, so the measured land drop fired seven triggers instead of one (expected 15, got 21). The guard
is in the row maker, not in the suite: a `control` gate under a head that watches another permanent
enter is refused by name.

### Traps

- **THE SUITE MUST ARM THE BRANCH IT ASSERTS.** That is the whole decision; the refusal D523 wrote
  was the same sentence read from the other side.
- **A GATE'S RECIPE IS A BOARD CHANGE, AND A BOARD CHANGE CAN BE THE ROW'S OWN TRIGGER.** Scute
  Swarm's six lands are six landfall fires and six copies of the source.
- **THE LEDGER MUST NOT NAME A LINE THE PARSER READS.** The first cut ledgered 44 cards for
  `If this spell was kicked, ... instead` — a shape D423 has read since; they are refused for an
  older reason, and naming the gate would have been a false entry.

## D525 — CASCADE: a keyword that is a cast trigger, run off the spell on the stack (2026-09-23)

**12,192 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,182
(+10: Ardent Plea, Bloodbraid Elf, Heralds of Tzeentch, Boarding Party, Enlisted Wurm, Shardless Agent, Ethersworn Sphinx, Maelstrom Colossus, Annoyed Altisaur, Apex Devastator — all ten complete on the seam alone - a bare keyword line is never a row, and every other line of each already read; the probe diff is the 10, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` unchanged at **7,987**. The REFUSED ledger 2,117 → **2,134** (+17 / -0: every line that GRANTS cascade to spells - `Sliver spells you cast have cascade`, `The first spell you cast each turn has cascade`, Yidris, TARDIS, Dark Apostle and their kin, a spell keyword the derive does not carry for a spell it is not printed on - the two heads that watch for it and Averna's rider on the cascade itself; nothing retired, because a bare keyword line was refused at the classifier and never ledgered, D361). Fixtures 9,046 →
**9,049** (the seam's own: Bloodbraid Elf, Ardent Plea, Apex Devastator). `scriptableToday` 1,905 → **1,919**; the ladder `[1919, 1934, 3225, 4689, 5825]`. Bot reach **5,016** from **391**.
An engine seam on Fable 5.1 — CR 702.85: the keyword table's first entry that fires off the STACK, and the
ability path's first resolution that hands its generator back to the log.

### The measurement chose it — and corrected the plan twice

The D424 measurement over the fresh 19,510-row leftover (`d525/MEASURE-d525.md`). The row maker offers nothing
(5 rows of 18,903 line-only rows), so the wave had to come from a seam. The biggest residue by rows is the
scoped grant of a quoted ability (121 sole-line rows) — but that subsystem is BUILT (D367/D368/D372, D454/D456/D517),
and its residue is a spread of small pieces (the provider referent inside a granted ability 16, the scopes outside
the table 25, quoted bodies outside the vocabulary 24, quoted statics 8). The cast-time facts D523 priced measure
18 every-line rows. Ranked by yield per mechanism, cascade won: 24 every-line rows, 13 of them the bare keyword
line, ONE rule, and every piece with a precedent — the keyword table (D308/D361), the free cast from exile (D489),
the cast begun by an answer (D491), the play permission (D417), the seeded random order (D389).

### The seam (`d525/patch525-engine.cjs`, `patch525-clients.cjs`, `patch525-fuzz.cjs`; `cascade.test.ts` 5 proofs)

- **THE KEYWORD** (`oracle.ts`, `keywords.ts`, `engineComplete.ts`, `tier3.ts`). `cascade` joins `TIER2_KEYWORDS`
  and the canon, so `parseKeywords` reads Scryfall's word and the accounting claims the printed line — each clause of
  `Cascade, cascade, cascade, cascade` IS the keyword. The twice-is-two-abilities rule (D361: the derive carries a
  Set) exempts it, because the entry counts the printings itself (`cascadeCount`). The Tier-3 note retires.
- **THE ENTRY OFF THE STACK** (`keywordTriggers.ts`, `triggers.ts`). The table walked the battlefield only; a
  cast-time keyword's source is the SPELL. `fromStack` makes the bus ask the cast card of a `SpellCast` (zone
  `stack`, its DERIVED keywords, CR 613's silence) — one firing per printing (`perItem`), the mana value AS CAST
  taken at the firing (`memo`: the printed value plus X times the cost's X count, CR 202.3b), because the spell may
  have left the stack by the resolution.
- **THE RESOLUTION** (`cascadeResolve`). The controller's library from the top, each card to exile, until a nonland
  card whose mana value is less than the memo; the rest go to the bottom in a random order NOW (D389's shuffle off
  the generator); the hit waits on the controller — a play permission for this turn (D417) and the free-cast chooser
  over a POOL of one (`chooseFromZone { zone: 'exile', castFree: true, pool: [it] }`). The answer casts it for
  nothing (D491's `beginGrantedCast`, from exile under the permission, above the cascading spell) or bottoms it
  too and expires the permission. A library with no candidate is exiled whole and put back; nothing is asked.
- **THE GENERATOR THROUGH THE ABILITY PATH** (`loop.ts`, `handlers.ts`). `resolveAbility` returned events alone
  and `ctx.random` is a stub, so no ability could consume randomness honestly. It returns `{ events, rng }` now: a
  keyword entry's `resolveRandom` hands the advanced generator back, the three callers record it as `rngAfter`, and
  the delayed-effects branch keeps its executor's generator too (it dropped it before).
- **THE POOL'S READERS** (`handChoice.ts`, `bot/awaiting.ts`, `harness.ts`, the fuzz driver, `PromptBar.tsx`).
  `freeCastCandidates(..., pool)` is the one reader the host, the bot, the harness and the driver share; the bar
  gains a "Cast it" button, because the card sits in exile and no hand click could name it.
- **THE FUZZ.** `cascades` (the triggers queued off a cast spell) and `cascadeCasts` (the exiled candidates cast for
  nothing), Bloodbraid Elf and Ardent Plea two a seat, the floor at gate size (3 cascades over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-525 - Bloodbraid Elf and Ardent Plea two a seat).

### The yield — ten permanents and no rows

There was no wave, and none was needed: the yield is every card whose only unread line was the keyword itself (the three that print it beside a static that GRANTS it to spells - Quandrix, The First Sliver, Imoti - and Aurora Phoenix's head stay in the leftover, ledgered by name). Seventeen cards join the ledger with their reasons: the statics and effects that grant cascade to spells (`Sliver spells you cast have cascade`, `The first spell you cast each turn has cascade`, Yidris, TARDIS, Dark Apostle ...), the two heads that watch for it (Aurora Phoenix, The First Doctor), Averna's rider on the cascade itself.

### Traps

- **A KEYWORD TRIGGER CAN FIRE OFF THE STACK.** The table's walk asked the battlefield; a cast-time keyword's
  source is the spell, in zone `stack`, asked of the `SpellCast` event's own card.
- **THE ABILITY PATH DROPPED ITS GENERATOR.** `resolveAbility` returned events alone, `ctx.random` answers 0, and
  `vocabularyEffects` refuses `at random` for a def — the rule was stated, not enforced, one layer down: a delayed
  clause that drew randomness replayed to a different board. Threaded now, and the replay proof reads `rngAfter`.
- **A POOL, NOT A ZONE.** The free-cast chooser listed the hand; cascade's candidate sits in exile, which is public,
  so the prompt carries the ids and every reader takes them through the one admission the host applies.
- **THE MEASUREMENT OUTRANKS THE PLAN.** D523 named the cast-time facts and D524 named the grant; measured over the
  fresh leftover, one was thin and the other was already built. Ranking by yield per mechanism found the keyword.
- **A KEYWORD PRINTED FOUR TIMES IS FOUR TRIGGERS, AND THE DERIVE CARRIES A SET.** The count is read off the printed
  line at the firing, never stored — the same bound `keywordAmount` states for bushido.

## D526 — MANIFEST: the top card face down as a 2/2, remembered for its flip; the dread's look (2026-09-23)

**12,214 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,192
(+22: fourteen rows — Kathari Remnant, Sultai Emissary, Etherium-Horn Sorcerer, Stormcaller's Boon, Meteoric Mace, Soul-Strike Technique, Maelstrom Wanderer, Scroll of Fate, Qarsi High Priest, Orochi Soul-Reaver, Unsettling Twins, Innocuous Rat, Ingenuity Engine, Bashful Beastie — and eight spells complete on the seam alone — Reality Shift, Soul Summons, Break Down the Door, Unnerving Grasp, Twist Reality, Unwanted Remake, Ethereal Ambush, Manifest Dread; the probe diff is the 22, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 7,987 → **8,001**. The REFUSED ledger 2,134 → **2,177** (+48 / -5: the riders on the manifested card (11 - `then put a +1/+1 counter on it`, `then attach this Equipment to that creature`: a referent to a card the clause MADE, which the vocabulary does not bind), the dread repeated (2), the shuffled piles (2), the counted manifests (2), the face-up verb, the `Whenever you manifest dread` head, the spend restriction naming the flip, and 26 rows the manifest line no longer blocks, entered with THE ROW MAKER'S OWN REASON for each rather than the seam's; the five retired are Ethereal Ambush, Reality Shift, Soul Summons, Unwanted Remake and Unnerving Grasp, all finished by the seam). Fixtures 9,049 →
**9,067**. `scriptableToday` 1,919 → **1,915**; the ladder `[1915, 1930, 3221, 4687, 5822]`. Bot reach **5,025** from **391**.
An engine seam and a generator wave on Fable 5.1 — CR 701.34 over D309's face-down object, with the cascade
keyword's six late rows riding the same wave.

### The measurement chose it — the next Fable subsystem by yield per mechanism

Over the post-D525 leftover (`d526/measure526-manifest.cjs`): manifest touches 64 rows, 28 of them every-line, 12 of
those spells — the most rows behind one mechanism whose pieces all exist. D309 built the face-down object (the derive's
nameless 2/2 with no abilities, the projection that hides the printing from everyone but the controller, `FaceDownSet`),
D389/D493 the look grammar, D504 the `Its controller <verbs>` rewrite, D428 the head's player. What manifest adds is one
memory and one door: the permanent remembers it was MANIFESTED, and a creature card may be turned face up for its
mana cost.

### The seam (`d526/patch526-engine.cjs`, `patch526-fuzz.cjs`; `manifest.test.ts` 5 proofs)

- **THE KINDS.** `manifest` (the top N cards of a library onto the battlefield face down — the caster's own, the
  aimed player's own for `Its controller manifests ...`, or the head's player's library for `that player's library`
  with the caster manifesting) and `manifestDread` (CR 701.34e: look at the top two, one face down, the other into the
  graveyard). `Manifest a card from your hand` is D508's hand put entering face down. The riders on the card the
  clause made (`then put a +1/+1 counter on it`) stay unread — a referent to a MADE object is its own seam.
- **THE MARK.** `CardMove.manifested` rides the entry onto `CardInstance.manifested`, cleared as the permanent leaves;
  `turnFaceUp` and the legal offer price a manifested CREATURE card's flip at its mana cost (a morph cost still serves;
  the megamorph counter is the morph cost's alone); a manifested land has no cost and stays face down.
- **THE DREAD'S LOOK.** `LookSpec.faceDown` and the chooser's `faceDown` carry the pick's entry: the answer path (the
  library look and the hand put alike) moves it face down, manifested, and emits `ManifestedDread` — the marker the
  heads will read and the fuzz counts. Two cards ask; one card is no question and is manifested unasked; none narrates.
- **THE FUZZ.** `manifests` (the face-down entries off a manifest), `manifestDreads` (the markers), `manifestFlips`
  (a face-down card turned up whose printing has no morph cost), Soul Summons and Manifest Dread two a seat, the floor
  on manifests (9 manifests, 3 dreads and 1 flip over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-526 - Soul Summons and Manifest Dread two a seat).

### The tooling (`patch526-tools.cjs`, `-b`)

The vocab probe and the row maker know a dread ASKS; the generator asserts the manifested face-down permanents and the
marker, deals twelve Forests to a manifest row (a seven-card deck is dealt whole, and the opening seven, the row card's
pull and the turn-three draw leave nothing to manifest), and ANSWERS THE DREAD'S LOOK BESIDE ITS ASSERT — the generated
`settle` waits for an empty stack and pending triggers, not for a prompt, so the dread's look stayed up unanswered and
two trial runs read +0 on the board and blamed the deck.

### The wave — fourteen rows and eight spells

Fourteen rows of the fourteen generated: eight the manifest reading rowed (Sultai Emissary, Innocuous Rat and Bashful Beastie's dies heads, Unsettling Twins' enters head, Qarsi High Priest's sacrifice-cost activation, Orochi Soul-Reaver's combat-damage head off the damaged player's library, Scroll of Fate's hand chooser, Soul-Strike Technique's enchanted-creature-dies head) and six the CASCADE keyword unlocked a decision late (Kathari Remnant, Etherium-Horn Sorcerer, Stormcaller's Boon, Meteoric Mace, Maelstrom Wanderer, Ingenuity Engine - their other lines already read). The three dread rows failed two trial runs by +0: the generated `settle` waits for an empty stack and pending triggers, NOT for a prompt, so the dread's look stayed up unanswered - the suite answers it beside its assert now, as the explore and the look already did. Forty-eight cards join the ledger with their reasons; five retire (the seam finished them).

### Traps

- **A PROMPT IS NOT AN EMPTY STACK.** The generated `settle` stops at a prompt; a payload that asks must be answered
  beside its assert, or the assert reads a board the answer never reached — and blames the deck.
- **THE DECK IS DEALT WHOLE.** A generated suite's library is empty at the fire unless the row's extras exceed the
  opening seven, the row card's pull and the draws.
- **A FACE-DOWN PERMANENT REMEMBERS HOW IT GOT THERE.** Morph's flip is the printed morph cost; a manifested creature
  card's is its mana cost; the mark rides the move and clears with the object (CR 701.34c, 702.37).
- **THE LEDGER NAMES THE ROW MAKER'S REASON, NOT THE SEAM'S.** A row the seam now reads but something else blocks is
  entered with what actually blocks it, or the next reader is sent at a seam already built.
- **THE ROW MAKER'S SPELL CHECK KEEPS THE REMINDER TEXT.** It refuses the manifest spells the parser reads whole; a
  spell is never a row, so the probe diff counts them anyway — harmless, and noted.

## D527 — CLASH: the two placements and the verdict (2026-09-23)

**12,223 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,214
(+9: six rows — Oaken Brawler, Springjack Knight, Paperfin Rascal, Adder-Staff Boggart, Bog Hoodlums, Ringskipper — and three spells complete on the seam alone — Release the Ants, Research the Deep, Titan's Revenge; the probe diff is the 9, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,001 → **8,007**. The REFUSED ledger 2,177 → **2,192** (+23 / -8: the heads that watch for a clash (Entangling Trap's `Whenever you clash, tap target creature an opponent controls`, Rebellion of the Flamekin's `Whenever you clash, you may pay {1}`; Sylvan Echoes' was ledgered already - the `Clashed` marker exists, the heads need a library entry), the clash with the DEFENDING player (Marvo, Deep Operative), the `Otherwise` half of the verdict (Pulling Teeth, Captivating Glance), the clash that repeats on a win (Hoarder's Greed), Whirlpool Whelm's `instead` rider with a may and a referent to the bounced card, Mana Clash (a coin flip that only carries the word), and 15 rows the clash no longer blocks - entered with THE ROW MAKER'S OWN REASON for each (twelve spells with a line outside the vocabulary - Lash Out, Spring Cleaning, Weed Strangle, Gilt-Leaf Ambush, Fistful of Force, Revive the Fallen, Recross the Paths, Scattering Stroke, Broken Ambitions, Pollen Lullaby, Redeem the Lost, Woodland Guidance; Sentry Oak's and Fire Juggler's payloads that are not a pump; Nath's Elite's lure line); the eight retired all said `clash mechanic` - Release the Ants, Research the Deep and Titan's Revenge are finished by the seam, and Hoarder's Greed, Lash Out, Recross the Paths, Spring Cleaning and Weed Strangle come back under what actually blocks them). Fixtures 9,067 →
**9,075**. `scriptableToday` 1,915 → **1,914**; the ladder `[1914, 1929, 3220, 4682, 5817]`. Bot reach **5,027** from **391**.
An engine seam and a generator wave on Fable 5.1 — CR 701's clash over D409's chained prompts and D523's gated
clause.

### The measurement chose it — the next Fable subsystem by yield per mechanism

Over the post-D526 leftover: clash touches 33 rows, 30 of them every-line, 18 of those spells — the most rows behind
one mechanism whose pieces all exist. D389 built the scry choice, D409 the explore's two prompts chained through a
carried state, D523 the gated clause (`If you win, ...` is a gate the executor holds), D524 the staged condition the
generator arms. What clash adds is a verdict: two reveals, two placements, a comparison, and a memo the gate can read.

### The seam (`d527/patch527-engine.cjs`, `-b`, `-c`, `-d`, `patch527-fuzz.cjs`, `patch527-clients.cjs`; `clash.test.ts` 5 proofs)

- **THE KINDS.** `clash` (`Clash with an opponent.`): you and the opponent each reveal the top card of your library (a
  `CardsRevealed` to every seat), then each puts it on the top or bottom — two `scryChoice` prompts chained through
  `ClashState`, yours first, then the opponent's (the D409 shape) — and the verdict is `Clashed { won: yourMv >
  theirMv }`; an empty library reveals nothing and cannot win, a tie wins nothing. One opponent is forced; more are
  asked for (`Awaiting.choosePlayer` — the harness and the bot take the first candidate, the PromptBar offers a button
  a seat); none narrates. `returnSelf` (`If you win, return ~ to its owner's hand.`): the card back to its owner's
  hand from the battlefield or the graveyard — and, when the card is the spell, its own fate (`spellFateOf` →
  `'hand'`, the fourth fate beside graveyard, exile and the battlefield).
- **THE GATE.** `clashWon` is an activation condition (`if you win` / `if you won`) the executor's `gateHolds` reads
  off the newest `Clashed` for the controller in the events so far, else off the continuation
  (`EffectContinuation.clash`, `StackObject.clash` — `'won'` | `'lost'`), else false; the D523 gate holds it like any
  other.
- **THE CONTINUATION.** The answers resume the resolution: the first placement asks the opponent's; the second
  finishes the clash, emits `Clashed`, and resumes the continuation with the verdict aboard, so the gated clause runs
  from where the spell now is — the graveyard for a spell, the battlefield for a permanent's trigger.
- **THE FUZZ.** `clashes` (the markers) and `clashWins`; Release the Ants and Research the Deep two a seat; the floor
  on clashes (5 clashes, 4 won over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-527 - Release the Ants and Research the Deep two a seat).

### The tooling (`patch527-tools.cjs`)

The vocab probe and the row maker know a clash ASKS; the generator answers both placements beside its assert (the
cards stay on top) and asserts a `Clashed` for the row's player; `returnSelf` asserts the card in hand, and one fewer
on the board unless the head was a dies; `clashWon` translates to a staged condition whose recipe stacks a Hill Giant
on p1's library and a Forest on p2's — the D524 way, an ARMED gate.

### The wave — six rows and three spells

Six rows of the six generated, every one a clash under a head with a gated rider: the enters heads that put a +1/+1
counter on the creature (Oaken Brawler, Paperfin Rascal, Adder-Staff Boggart, Bog Hoodlums), the attack head that
gives the creature double strike (Springjack Knight), the dies head that returns the card from the graveyard
(Ringskipper — `return this card` joined the self-return rule for it, and the vocabulary snapshot was collected again
so the row maker rowed it). The whole-leftover row maker offered 10 rows of 18,871 once the vocabulary read a clash
— five clash rows beside the five perennial non-landers. Twenty-three cards join the ledger with their reasons;
eight retire — the entries that said `clash mechanic`: three finished by the seam, five re-entered with what actually
blocks them. The regression moved the pins the seam touched: the Awaiting union grew by `choosePlayer`, and the D373
and D497 pins that read the self bounce read `returnSelf` now.

### Traps

- **A GATED SELF-CLAUSE IS NOT THE SPELL'S FATE.** `spellFateOf` scanned the clauses for the self kinds and found the
  gated `return ~ to its owner's hand` behind the clash, so the loop moved the card to the hand as the spell resolved
  — before the clash was asked, whatever its verdict. A clause behind a gate is decided when the gate is, by the
  executor; the scan skips it.
- **RULE-TABLE ORDER.** `Return ~ to its owner's hand` matched the older self-bounce rule first; the new `returnSelf`
  precedes it now, and the pins that read the old kind moved with it — a measured repin, not a regression.
- **THE FIRST CLAUSE DRAWS FIRST.** A proof that stacks the clash card on top of the library loses it to the clause
  before the clash — Research the Deep draws, then clashes; the filler goes above.
- **THE LEDGER'S OLD REASON CAN GO FALSE.** `clash mechanic` retired with the mechanic (eight entries); the cards the
  seam finished leave, the rest come back under the row maker's reason for them — never the seam's.
- **A NAME IS NOT A MECHANISM.** Mana Clash carries the word and flips a coin; the residue script's shape checks ran
  before its name check and mislabelled it, and the ledger line was set by hand.

## D528 — SAGAS: the lore counter, the chapter told as the count reaches it, the sacrifice after the last (2026-09-23)

**12,233 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,223
(+10: ten rows — Summon: Choco/Mog, History of Benalia, War of the Last Alliance, Summon: Fat Chocobo, Binding the Old Gods, Origin of the Hulk, Summon: Ixion, The Birth of Meletis, Summon: Anima, Founding of Omashu; the probe diff is the 10, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,007 → **8,017**. The REFUSED ledger 2,192 → **2,407** (+217 / -2: the Sagas whose chapter bodies the vocabulary does not read, entered with THE ROW MAKER'S OWN REASON for each (`trigger payload not a pump` for most - the grants `X gain "..."`, the `until your next turn` durations, the delayed `Whenever you cast ... this turn` heads, the `For each opponent` walks; the transforming Sagas as `multi-face or unusual layout`; the tokens outside the table; the lines the row maker could not match to the printed text), the heads that watch a Saga (Narci's final-chapter head - the SagaSacrificed marker exists), the lore-counter verbs (Keldon Warcaller), the counted lore (Tom Bombadil), read ahead (Barbara Wright); the one retired said `saga chapter trigger` (Historian's Boon) - the engine has sagas now, and it comes back under the row maker's reason for its first line). Fixtures 9,075 →
**9,087**. `scriptableToday` 1,914 → **1,914**; the ladder `[1914, 1929, 3219, 4681, 5814]`. Bot reach **5,034** from **391**.
An engine seam and a generator wave on Fable 5.1 — CR 714 over the counters, the turn-based actions, the trigger
collector and the state-based actions.

### The measurement chose it — the largest family in the leftover, a new subsystem

Sagas touch 214 rows of the post-D527 leftover, 163 every-line (425 chapter lines) - the largest family in it by far; 10 complete on the seam alone by the payload judge, 13 by the row maker (History of Benalia, Summon: Choco/Mog and Summon: Fat Chocobo read by its mass-pump reader), one dropped at the trial. The other new subsystems by immediate yield: initiative 11, coin flip 9, monstrosity 9, goad 3,
vote 3 (`d528/MEASURE-d528.md`, `measure528.cjs`, the `zz-saga` / `zz-fam` yield probes). The row maker had hidden
every Saga behind `multi-face or unusual layout` (the layout is `saga`, not `normal`), so no measurement by its offer
could see the family; the D424 measurement over the whole leftover did.

### The seam (`d528/patch528-engine.cjs`, `-b`, `patch528-fuzz.cjs`; `saga.test.ts` 3 proofs)

- **THE COUNTER.** A Saga enters with a lore counter (CR 714.2a — the entry funnel, beside the loyalty and the
  modular counters), and as its controller's precombat main phase begins each Saga they control gets one (714.2b —
  a turn-based action in `turnBasedActions`, one `CountersChanged` batch; a phased-out Saga is not there to count).
- **THE CHAPTER.** A chapter ability is a trigger on `CountersChanged` reading the lore count before and after
  (714.2c: before < n ≤ after) — a lore counter from ANY source tells the chapter the count reaches; the defs are the
  card scripts' (`chapter-<line>`), their bodies the vocabulary's; a shared chapter (`I, II, III —`) is one def with
  three numbers.
- **THE SACRIFICE.** A Saga whose count has reached its final chapter (read off the printed chapter lines —
  `sagaFinalChapter`) and which is not the source of a chapter ability pending or on the stack is sacrificed by the
  state-based actions (714.4 — `sagaSacrificed`, the `SagaSacrificed` marker for the heads and the fuzz, a
  narration). A sacrifice: indestructible does not save it.
- **THE FUZZ.** `loreCounters`, `chaptersFired` (the `#chapter-` refs put on the stack), `sagasSacrificed`; Origin
  of the Hulk and The Birth of Meletis two a seat; the floor on chapters (21 lore counters, 21 chapters told and 7 Sagas sacrificed over the first 60 seeds, fuzz60-528 - Origin of the Hulk and The Birth of Meletis two a seat).

### The tooling (`patch528-tools.cjs`)

The row maker admits the saga layout and reads a chapter line as a head (`I — body`, `I, II — body`; a named
sub-heading such as the Summon cards' `Pain — ` stripped) whose ability carries its chapter numbers and whether it is
the FINAL one; `this Saga` is the self subject in the row maker, the payload collector and the vocab probe. The
generator emits the chapter def and ARMS it: chapter I by the entry (the lore counter of 714.2a), a later chapter by one
more lore counter (`ManualSetCounter`) after the earlier chapters were told before the baseline; the board reads the
Saga's own entry (+1 for chapter I) and its sacrifice (−1 after the final).

### The wave — ten rows

Eleven suites generated, ten landed - Book of Mazarbul dropped: its chapter II amasses onto the Army chapter I made, and the suite reads the counters absolutely. The whole-leftover row maker offered 16 rows of 18,871 once the chapter line was a head - eleven sagas beside the five perennial non-landers; ten taken. The ledger takes 217 cards with their reasons and retires 2 - the entry that said `saga chapter trigger`, re-entered under what actually blocks it.

### Traps

- **THE EARLIER CHAPTERS ARE TOLD BEFORE THE BASELINE.** A later chapter's suite cannot fire it without the ones
  before (the count must pass them); the arm tells them first, then measures. A payload that accumulates on an object an
  earlier chapter MADE (an amass onto the same Army) reads the sum — Book of Mazarbul dropped.
- **THE ROW MAKER'S LAYOUT GATE HID A FAMILY.** `multi-face or unusual layout` refused every Saga whole, so no
  measurement by the row maker's offer could see the 163 rows; the measurement over the whole leftover is the one that
  counts, and the ledger's `unusual layout` reasons for Sagas went false with the gate (19 rewritten to the row maker's
  reason for their chapter bodies).
- **A LORE COUNTER FROM ANY SOURCE TELLS A CHAPTER** (CR 714.2c) — the def reads the count, not the turn; the proof
  puts the counters by hand.
- **THE STATE-BASED ACTIONS WAIT FOR THE CHAPTER** (714.4) — the Saga stays while its final chapter ability is pending
  or on the stack; the proof checks the board before settling.
- **A NAMED SUB-HEADING IS NOT A CHAPTER** (`I, II, III — Pain — You draw ...`): stripped after the numerals in the row
  maker, the collector and the final-chapter reader alike; the Saga's parenthetical first line is reminder text, no
  line at all.

## D529 — THE KICK COUNTED: the multikicker's counters per kick, the keyword a kicked creature enters with (2026-09-24)

**12,245 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,233
(+12: twelve rows — Skitter of Lizards, Enclave Elite, Gnarlid Pack, Apex Hawks, Quag Vampires, Flametongue Yearling; Kavu Titan, Duskwalker, Benalish Lancer, Faerie Squadron, Pouncing Kavu, Pouncing Wurm; the probe diff is the 12, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,017 → **8,029**. The REFUSED ledger 2,407 → **2,558** (+155 / -4: the kicker family the wave did not reach, with the row maker's own reason for each (121 - the kicked riders on spells outside the vocabulary, the kicked enters heads whose payload is not a pump, the counted payloads over the kicks the suite cannot stage), the double kickers (18 - `Kicker {A} and/or {B}`: two costs and which was paid), the kickers paid by a cost that is not mana (17 - `Kicker—Sacrifice a creature`, `Kicker—Pay 3 life`), the heads that watch for a kicked spell (8 + 2 gated on `if that spell was kicked`), 5 kicker lines under shapes the row maker never reached; the four retired said `kicker memory` - the engine has had the kick's memory since D403 - and came back under what actually blocks them (Lullmage's Familiar and Merfolk Falconer under the kicked cast head, Ertai's Trickery and Minamo's Meddling under the row maker's spell reason)). Fixtures 9,087 →
**9,098**. `scriptableToday` 1,914 → **1,914**; the ladder `[1914, 1929, 3219, 4669, 5802]`. Bot reach **5,039** from **391**.
A mechanical wave on Opus 5.5 — the row maker and the generator, no engine change: D403 has carried the kick on the
cast, the move and the permanent since it was built.

### The measurement chose it — one keyword the engine has, a flat tail of shapes

The kicker family touches 180 rows of the post-D528 leftover, 129 every-line, 64 of them spells - a flat tail of small shapes over one keyword the engine has had since D403 (the kicked cast, `kicked: N` on the stack object, the move and the permanent). Split by the immediate yield (`d529/zz-kick-d529`): the kicked enters-with with a keyword 6, the multikicker count 5 (+ Flametongue Yearling, which the row maker found), the kicker paid by a cost that is not mana 9 (6 spells), the double kicker 3 to 5, the cast head that watches a kicked spell 2 - the first two need no engine change at all. The new subsystems measured at D528 stay where they were (initiative 11, coin flip 9, monstrosity 9 on
the seam alone), below the mechanical shapes of a keyword the engine already runs — so the decision is Opus's
(`d529/MEASURE-d529.md`).

### The tooling (`d529/patch529-tools.cjs`)

- **THE KICKED KEYWORD.** `If this creature was kicked, it enters with N +1/+1 counters on it and with <keyword>.`
  The row maker's led enters-with form (D403) reads the trailing keyword (`and with trample`, `haste`, `flying`,
  `first strike`, `fear`, ...) as `kickedKeyword`; the generator writes the D403 replacement as before and a static
  of its own — `layer: 'ability'`, the card itself, gated on the kick the permanent remembers
  (`CardInstance.kicked`, set by the entering move and cleared as it leaves). The unkicked stage one proves the keyword
  ABSENT beside the counters; the kicked fire proves it present. One statics block per module: a kicked keyword
  beside another statics block is refused by name.
- **THE MULTIKICKER COUNT.** `This creature enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each time it was kicked.` The row
  maker reads the phrase as the kicks (`kicked: true`, no board count), takes the Multikicker mana off the card's own
  line, and the suite casts it kicked twice (the mana paid each time, `kicked: 2`); the replacement reads the count off
  the entering MOVE, as the led form reads its gate, and the assert reads two counters and the base two higher.

### The wave — twelve rows

Twelve suites generated, twelve landed first time. The whole-leftover row maker offered 17 rows of 18,852 once the kicked enters-with read its keyword and the multikicker count read the kicks - twelve kicker rows beside the five perennial non-landers; twelve taken. The multikicker count: Skitter of Lizards, Enclave Elite, Gnarlid Pack, Apex Hawks, Quag Vampires, Flametongue Yearling. The kicked keyword: Kavu Titan, Duskwalker, Benalish Lancer, Faerie Squadron, Pouncing Kavu, Pouncing Wurm.
The ledger takes 155 cards with their reasons and retires 4 - the entries that said `kicker memory`, re-entered under what actually blocks them.

### Traps

- **A KEYWORD THE KICK GRANTS IS A STATIC ON THE CARD, NOT A REPLACEMENT.** `... and with haste` is not a counter
  the entry puts: the permanent HAS the keyword while it remembers the kick, so the def is a layer-6 static gated on
  `CardInstance.kicked` (which the entering move sets and leaving clears) — and the unkicked stage one is where the
  gate is proven, not only the kicked fire.
- **THE COUNT OF KICKS IS THE MOVE'S, NOT THE BOARD'S.** A multikicker's per-kick counters read the kicks off the
  entering move (the stack object has left the stack by then); a count helper over the board would read nothing.
- **A TRIAL'S WANTED BLOCK IS REMOVED BEFORE THE PORT.** The WANTED adder deduplicates the names but still writes its
  comment line; a port after a trial adds the block again as an empty comment — take the trial's block out first.
- **THE LEDGER'S OLD REASON CAN GO FALSE, YEARS LATER.** `kicker memory` (D185) had been false since D403 gave the
  engine the kick's memory; the four entries came back under what actually blocks them.

## D530 — THE KICKER'S OTHER COSTS: the two-kicker face and the kicker paid by a cost that is not mana (2026-09-24)

**12,256 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,245
(+11: five rows — Archangel of Wrath, Thornscape Battlemage, Sunscape Battlemage, Thunderscape Battlemage, Phyrexian Scuta — and six spells complete on the seam alone — Final Flourish, Stomped by the Foot, Vayne's Treachery, Vicious Offering, Rushing River, Dwarven Landslide; the probe diff is the 11, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,029 → **8,034**. The REFUSED ledger 2,558 → **2,547** (+24 / -35: the thirty-five entries D529 wrote with the double kicker or the kicker paid by a cost that is not mana as their reason retired - the engine charges both now - and the ones still in the leftover came back under what actually blocks them (the row maker's own reason for most: Stormscape, Nightscape and Ana Battlemage's payloads, Bog Down's and Primal Growth's kicked instead clauses, Goblin Barrage's added target; the enters-with under a NAMED kicker - the five volvers; a cast trigger gated on the named kicker - Wastescape Battlemage; a spell clause gated on the named kicker - Illuminate; Arctic Merfolk's return-a-creature kicker the suite cannot pay)). Fixtures 9,098 →
**9,105**. `scriptableToday` 1,914 → **1,919**; the ladder `[1919, 1934, 3224, 4680, 5813]`. Bot reach **5,039** from **391**.
A bounded engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.5 — the two kicker forms D403 left null, over D406's picks.

### The measurement chose it — the kicker family's next shape, with a precedent in the tree

D529's yield probe (`d529/zz-kick-d529`) priced the two forms together at about thirteen: the kicker paid by a cost that is not mana 9 (6 spells reading whole once the line is the cost's), the double kicker 3 to 5 - one extension of D403 over D406's picks. Both forms extend a keyword the engine runs: D403 charges `Kicker {M}` and remembers the count on the
stack object, the move and the permanent; D406 charges an additional cost's chooser verb from the cast's picks. What
D530 adds is WHICH kicker, and a kicker whose price is a verb.

### The seam (`d530/patch530-engine.cjs`, `patch530-fuzz.cjs`; `kickerCosts.test.ts` 5 proofs)

- **THE TWO-KICKER FACE.** `Kicker {A} and/or {B}` reads into `kickerCost` (the first) and `kickerCost2` (the
  second). The cast names which it pays — `CastSpell.kickedWith` (0 the first printed, 1 the second; absent, the first
  `kicked` of them in order) — and `kicked` stays the count (2 = kicked twice, CR 702.33e). The problem prices the
  named costs; the stack object, the entering move and the permanent remember `kickedWith` beside `kicked` (cleared as
  it leaves). A third kick, a count and a named list that disagree, and a named kicker on a one-kicker face are refused
  by name.
- **THE KICKER PAID BY A COST THAT IS NOT MANA.** `Kicker—<cost>.` reads into `OracleFace.kickerVerb`: a leading mana
  piece (`Kicker—{2}{R}, Sacrifice a land.`) and ONE chooser verb or life payment through D415's grammar. A kicked cast
  charges the verb exactly as D406's additional cost — the cast's picks, validated against the offer's own candidates
  and paid in the cost batch — its mana beside the kick and its life on the problem (`Kicker—Pay 3 life.`). Picks with
  no kick are refused, and a kick with no picks.
- **THE ACCOUNTING AND THE PARSER.** Both lines are the engine's when the parser read them (`engineComplete`), and the
  spell text leaves them out (`effectParse`), so a verb-kicked spell whose clauses the vocabulary reads is complete —
  the six above, on the seam alone.
- **THE OFFER.** The UI's kick toggle stays the mana kicker's (`kicker`); the drivers get the second kicker
  (`kickerSecondAffordable`, `kickerBothAffordable`) and the verb kicker (`kickerVerbText`, `kickerVerbAffordable`,
  `kickerPick*` — the first candidates of its verb) by their own fields, each priced by the base cast's solver.
- **THE FUZZ.** The driver names both kickers when both are payable, else the second alone, else the first; a verb
  kicker with the first candidates of its verb (D443's rule, never on a coin) — whenever the card is CHOSEN: the
  first-priority list stays the mana kicker's. The first gate put the new kicks in that list and read D398's
  this-turn floor at 0 over 500 seeds (3, 4, 3 at the three gates before): Final Flourish, cast the moment it was
  payable, sacrificed a creature every time and took the enablers' turns. The new kicks ride the ordinary pick now,
  and the D398 staples are five a seat (D445's repair). `kickerVerbCasts`, `secondKickerCasts`; Final Flourish and
  Thornscape Battlemage two a seat; the floor on the two together
  (26 verb-kicked casts and 7 second-kicker casts over the gate's 500 seeds - Final Flourish and Thornscape Battlemage two a seat; the D398 this-turn floor back at 4 + 3 after the repair).

### The tooling (`patch530-tools.cjs`)

The condition reader takes `it was kicked with its {R} kicker` (`kickedWith`, the printed index the row maker resolves
off the Kicker line) and `it was kicked twice` (`kickedTwice`) as gates on the permanent's memory. The row maker's KICK
PLAN replaces the one-kicker reader — the named kicker's cost, both costs, a kicker paid in life — and the generator's
kicked fire pays the plan and names it (`kicked: N, kickedWith: [...]`).

### The wave — five rows and six spells

Five suites generated, five landed first time. The whole-leftover row maker offered 10 rows of 18,840 once the engine charged a two-kicker face and a kicker paid in life - five kicker rows beside the five perennial non-landers; five taken. The battlemages and Archangel of Wrath prove each named-kicker trigger in its own game (the
unkicked entry first, the trigger silent), Phyrexian Scuta the kicked enters-with paid in life. The ledger retires 35 entries whose reason was a kicker form the engine charges now and takes 24 back under their real blocker.

### Traps

- **THE KICK HAS TWO NUMBERS.** `kicked` is how many, `kickedWith` is which: a one-kicker face never names one, a
  two-kicker face always does once kicked (normalised by the host), and `kicked twice` is the count, not a second
  list.
- **A VERB KICKER IS AN ADDITIONAL COST THAT ONLY APPLIES WHEN KICKED.** The same picks, the same candidates, the same
  cost batch as D406 — so picks with no kick, and a kick with no picks, are both refused, not silently ignored.
- **THE UI TOGGLE IS NOT THE ENGINE'S LIMIT.** The toggle stays the mana kicker's; the drivers reach the new kicks by
  their own offer fields — and a human cannot name the second kicker or pay a verb kicker yet (a reportable, not a
  gap in the engine).
- **A NEW KICK IN THE FIRST-PRIORITY LIST ROTS A THIN FLOOR.** The driver's kicked list is cast before anything
  else; a kick that is almost always payable (a verb kicker with a creature on the board) takes every turn it can,
  and a floor that lives on three events in 500 seeds reads zero. New kicks ride the ordinary pick; the thin floor
  gets a copy more a seat.
- **A RETIRE REGEX MUST READ THE ESCAPES.** D529's retire pattern stopped at `\'` in a reason (`owner\'s hand`); D530's
  reads the escaped reason whole, or an entry with an apostrophe stays behind with a false reason.
