## D531 — CONTROL WITH A DURATION AND THE EXCHANGE: control for good, control the source holds, and the exchange (2026-09-24)

**12,283 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,256
(+27: fifteen rows — Keiga, the Tide Star, Chromeshell Crab, Piper of the Swarm, Sower of Temptation, Eyes Everywhere, Phyrexian Infiltrator, Dragonlord Silumgar, Sliver Overlord, Mind Flayer, Aladdin, Avarice Totem, Roil Elemental, Master Thief, Vedalken Plotter, Jace, Ingenious Mind-Mage — and twelve cards complete on the seam alone — Political Trickery, Archmage's Charm, Slave of Bolas, Shrewd Negotiation, Ritual of the Machine, Momo's Heist, Trade the Helm on the control rules; Highspire Infusion, Glimmer of Genius, Attune with Aether, Tune the Narrative on the energy repair; and the reversible printing Dragonlord Silumgar // Dragonlord Silumgar, which the row's script covers; the probe diff is the 27, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,034 → **8,048**. The REFUSED ledger 2,547 → **2,789** (+245 / -3: the one entry whose reason was a permanent control change retired (Ritual of the Machine - the seam completed it) and the two the energy repair completed left as stale (Glimmer of Genius, Tune the Narrative); the control family's residue came in under what blocks it - a control given to another player (41), a control over every object of a scope (24), a duration outside the two the engine reads (15 - `for as long as ~ remains tapped` the most of them), an exchange of two targets under one phrase (8), a target per opponent (3), a control line under a shape the row maker never reached (12), and the row maker's own reason for the other 142 (the threaten riders `Untap that creature. It gains haste until end of turn.` among them)). Fixtures 9,105 →
**9,121**. `scriptableToday` 1,919 → **1,923**; the ladder `[1923, 1938, 3228, 4685, 5818]`. Bot reach **5,042** from **393**.
A bounded engine seam, one parser repair and a generator wave on Opus 5.5 — D393's control change given the two ends
it lacked, over D453's memory on the permanent.

### The measurement chose it — the biggest control shapes, with a precedent in the tree

D530's yield probe (`d530/zz-next-d531`) priced the control family at 164 every-line (64 of them reading whole beside the mechanism, 16 spells): the permanent control change, the exchange and the durations tied to the source the biggest shapes, the give-away and the other durations behind them. The kicked cast head it priced beside them read 2 of 6. D393 takes control until end of turn and reverts it at cleanup; D453 keeps a control change on the
permanent (`controlledVia`: the source, its entry, the controller to revert to) and the state-based sweep reverts it
when the source leaves or unattaches. What D531 adds is the control with NO end, the memory's two other ends — the
source staying on the battlefield, and the source staying yours — and the exchange.

### The parser repair (`d531/patch531-parser.cjs`)

- **THE REMINDER INSIDE THE SENTENCE.** Scryfall prints energy's reminder inside the sentence it explains (`You get
  {E}{E} (two energy counters).`), and `scrub` blanks reminder text with spaces to keep the offsets — so the sentence
  the effect rules saw was `You get {E}{E}` followed by a run of spaces and the period, and D519's energy rule never
  matched it: every spell that gets energy stayed unread although the engine has run energy since D519. The energy
  reminder has no rules meaning (CR 207.2): `withoutEnergyReminder` REMOVES it before the scrub. Only energy's — a
  blank left by a quoted grant is what keeps a sentence missing its quote from reading as complete (D90). Four spells
  complete on the repair alone (Highspire Infusion, Glimmer of Genius, Attune with Aether, Tune the Narrative).

### The seam (`d531/patch531-engine.cjs`, `patch531-fuzz.cjs`; `controlDurations.test.ts` 5 proofs)

- **CONTROL WITH NO END.** `Gain control of target X.` reads as `control` with `controlFor: 'indefinite'` and resolves
  to `ControlGained` — the controller changes, the permanent's summoning clock restarts (CR 302.6), and no memory is
  kept: nothing gives it back.
- **CONTROL THE SOURCE HOLDS.** `... for as long as ~ remains on the battlefield.` (`whileOnBattlefield`) and `... for
  as long as you control ~.` (`whileControlled`) resolve to `ControlTakenBySource`: D453's `controlledVia` on the
  permanent, now with a MODE and the taker (`by`). The state-based sweep holds the control while the source is on the
  battlefield with the same entry — and, for `whileControlled`, while the taker still controls it; the aura-follow
  (the source attached to the permanent) stays D453's, read only when the memory has no mode. A source already gone
  when the effect resolves takes nothing (CR 611.2b), and says so.
- **THE EXCHANGE.** `Exchange control of target A and target B.` and `Exchange control of ~ and target B.` read as
  `exchangeControl` (the fight's two-target shape: `otherTargetIndex`, the self form on the source). Two objects on
  the battlefield under two different controllers swap them (two `ControlGained`); otherwise nothing happens and the
  log says so (CR 701.10).
- **THE FUZZ.** `controlGained` and `controlHeld`; Political Trickery and Sower of Temptation two a seat; the floor on
  the two together (34 control changes for good or by exchange and 3 held by a source over the gate's 500 seeds - Political Trickery and Sower of Temptation two a seat; D398's this-turn floor at 0 + 4 at the passing gate (2 + 3 at the first) - its sum still above zero, and thin).

### D187's rule — one spell def retired

Invoke the Winds' spell def (D220: `Gain control of target artifact or creature. Untap it.`) reads whole now that the
permanent control change is the vocabulary's, and its suppression pin (D187) turned red in the first gate's unit suite.
The def is retired (`d531/retire531.cjs`, D398's tool): the card stays complete, on the parser, and `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS`
is fifteen rows up and one def down.

### The tooling (`patch531-tools.cjs`, `-b`, `-c`)

The generator's `control` assert names the duration it reads (taken for good — no memory; held while the source holds
— the memory's mode beside the controller; D398's until end of turn), and `exchangeControl` is assertable (the two
objects swap sides when their sides differ). The row maker's static reader no longer takes a control change's `for as
long as` for a static's condition — it is the duration the vocabulary reads.

### The wave — fifteen rows

Fifteen suites generated, fifteen landed first time. The whole-leftover row maker offered 20 rows of 18,825 once control for good, control held while the source holds and the exchange were the engine's - fifteen control rows beside the five perennial non-landers; fifteen taken (six of them only after the row maker stopped reading a control change's duration as a static's condition). Keiga proves the dies trigger that takes a creature for good, Sower of Temptation, Mind Flayer,
Dragonlord Silumgar, Roil Elemental, Aladdin and Master Thief the control a source holds, Chromeshell Crab, Vedalken
Plotter, Eyes Everywhere, Phyrexian Infiltrator and Avarice Totem the exchange, and Piper of the Swarm, Sliver Overlord
and Jace, Ingenious Mind-Mage the activated control for good. The ledger retires the one entry whose reason was a permanent control change and the two the energy repair completed, and takes the control family's residue in (245) under the shape that blocks each card.

### Traps

- **THE REMINDER INSIDE THE SENTENCE.** A reminder the scrub blanks in the MIDDLE of a sentence leaves spaces no rule
  reads; energy's reminder has no rules meaning and is removed before the scrub. Any other reminder printed inside its
  sentence would hide the sentence the same way — look for it before calling a keyword's line unread.
- **THE SOURCE'S MEMORY HAS A MODE.** `controlledVia` without a mode is D453's aura-follow (the source attached to the
  permanent); `whileOnBattlefield` holds while the source stays with the same entry, `whileControlled` while the taker
  still controls the source. A new control duration is a new mode read by the same sweep, never a second memory.
- **A DURATION IS NOT A CONDITION.** The row maker's static reader took every line ending `... as long as X.` for a
  conditional static and refused Sower of Temptation's enters trigger as a condition outside the closed reader. A
  control change's `for as long as` is the vocabulary's duration and skips the static reader.
- **THE ASSERT MESSAGE IS SCANNED.** The generator reads the suite's destructure list off the assert text, so the word
  `no` in a message (`'no end, no memory'`) declared the `no` fixture in a suite that never read it (TS6133 on Sliver
  Overlord). A message names no fixture by accident.
- **A RESIDUE READS THE PARSER'S SELF.** The ledger's residue script first called `for as long as you control this
  creature` a duration the engine does not read; the parser reads `this creature` and the card's name as `~`
  (`selfRef`, `SELF`). A residue regex reads the card's self-reference the parser's way, or its reason is false.

## D532 — CONTROL'S OTHER FORMS: the compound threaten, control given to a named player, owners taking back what they own (2026-09-25)

**12,293 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,283
(+10: six rows — Humble Defector, Bazaar Trader, Jinxed Idol, Jinxed Ring, Overtaker, Bringer of the Red Dawn — and four cards complete on the seam alone — Threaten and Blind with Anger on the compound threaten; Brand and Gruul Charm on the owners' form; the probe diff is the 10, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,048 → **8,051**. The REFUSED ledger 2,789 → **2,780** (+38 / -47: the forty-one entries D531 wrote with a control GIVEN to another player as their reason retired - the engine reads the named-player form now - and six went stale (the compound threaten's cards and the owners' form the seam completed); the cards still blocked came back under what blocks them - a recipient the rule does not name (19), the owners' form the suite cannot stage (5), a give-away over a scope (4), the source given by a bare `it` (3), the row maker's own reason for the rest, and Custody Battle (a quoted give-away under a payment branch the suite cannot assert)). Fixtures 9,121 →
**9,130**. `scriptableToday` 1,923 → **1,927**; the ladder `[1927, 1942, 3229, 4686, 5819]`. Bot reach **5,044** from **393**.
A bounded engine seam and a generator wave on Opus 5.5 — the control forms D531's residue named, over D531's events.
From this decision on the whole loop runs on Opus 5.5, new subsystems included (the user's call, 2026-09-25).

### The measurement chose it — the biggest bounded shapes left, with a precedent in the tree

D531's what-is-left measurement (`d531/remaining-abilities-d532.md`, `next-yield-d532.json`) and the D532 yield probes priced the bounded Opus candidates: the give-away to a named player (21 every-line, 8 reading whole beside it), the compound threaten (7 touched, 5 whose only unread line it is), the owners' form (Homeward Path, Brooding Saurian, Brand, Gruul Charm). Every other Opus candidate measured smaller once its payloads were judged whole: the named kicker's
volvers grant a quoted ability in their second halves (2 to 4 cards, not 8), the threaten riders' blockers are other
riders (the triple itself already reads), the tapped duration rides an untap-choice static the engine lacks.

### The seam (`d532/patch532-engine.cjs`; `controlGiven.test.ts` 6 proofs)

- **THE COMPOUND THREATEN.** `Untap target creature and gain control of it until end of turn.` — D426's conjunction split
  read the untap already; the right half found no referent rule, because `REFERENT_OBJECT` named every object verb but
  `gain control of`. It does now, and D393's until-end-of-turn rule takes a leading `you`, so the referent rewrite of
  `you gain control of that creature until end of turn` reads too. Threaten reads as an untap, a control and the haste,
  all on the one target.
- **CONTROL GIVEN TO A NAMED PLAYER (CR 108.4).** `Target opponent gains control of ~.` and `Target player gains control
  of target artifact, creature, or land you control.` read as `giveControl`: the clause's player target takes the source
  — or the clause's other target, D396's second index after the player's — for good (`ControlGained`). One already that
  player's, or gone, changes nothing, and the step says so.
- **OWNERS TAKE BACK WHAT THEY OWN.** `Each player gains control of all creatures they own.` and `Gain control of all
  permanents you own.` read as `ownersControl` over D505's wide scope: each member under a player other than its owner
  goes to its owner — the caster's own only, for `you own` (`ownersYou`). `ScopeWalked` carries the verb.
- **THE REPAIR — A LATER CONTROL CHANGE OUTLASTS AN EARLIER ONE (CR 613.7).** D393's threaten leaves a cleanup revert on
  the until-end-of-turn list; D531's `ControlGained` and `ControlTakenBySource` left it there, so a threatened creature
  that a newer effect gave or took for good went back to its old controller at cleanup. Both events drop that revert now.
  The proof: p1 threatens p2's creature and gives it on to p3 — it is p3's past the cleanup.
- **THE FUZZ.** No new counter: every new effect emits D531's `ControlGained` (`controlGained`) or `ScopeWalked`.

### D187's rule — three spell defs retired

Donate (`Target player gains control of target permanent you control.`), Harmless Offering (`Target opponent gains
control of target permanent you control.`) and Wrong Turn (`Target opponent gains control of target creature.`) read
whole now that `giveControl` is the vocabulary's; their suppression pins (D187) turned red in the first gate's unit
suite, whose fuzz half was green (916.3 s). The defs are retired (`d532/retire532.cjs`): the cards stay complete, on the
parser - and the parser's `ControlGained` restarts the summoning clock (CR 302.6), which the scripts' older
`ControlChanged` did not. `SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` is six rows up and three defs down. The trap is D531's, paid again: after a
parser change, run every spell script's suppression test (`-t "suppression predicate"` over `scripts/cards`) BEFORE
the gate.

### The tooling (`patch532-tools.cjs`)

The generator asserts `giveControl` — the player fixture holds the source or the clause's other aim, and p1's board count
moves with what p1 gave away. `ownersControl` stays unassertable: its suite would have to stage a permanent under a
non-owner before the fire (`ManualSetController`), and the generator has no pre-fire hook for it yet.

### The wave — six rows

Six suites generated, six landed first time. The whole-leftover row maker offered 11 rows of 18,802 once the compound threaten and the named-player give-away were the engine's - six control rows beside the five perennial non-landers; six taken. Humble Defector and the two Jinxed artifacts give the source away, Bazaar Trader gives a
permanent to a target player, Overtaker and Bringer of the Red Dawn run the compound threaten. The ledger retires the forty-one give-away reasons D531 wrote and the six the seam made stale, and takes the give-away residue back (37) and Custody Battle under the shape that blocks each card.

### A correction to D531's handoff

D531's handoff row for the cards blocked on a script alone said its "25 are OFFERABLE" had been carried unmeasured since
D527, and wrote the whole-leftover row maker's own offer (5) in its place. That was wrong: the 25 is the select pool
`cardgenSelect.node.test.ts` pins on every run. D532's regression caught it by moving it — Custody Battle's quoted grant
(`target opponent gains control of this creature unless you sacrifice a land`) began to read and made the card
offerable (26); the row maker refuses it for a payment branch the suite cannot assert, so it is ledgered, and the pool
is 25 again. The handoff row says 25.

### Traps

- **A QUOTED BODY HIDES FROM A RESIDUE SCRIPT.** The scrub blanks a quoted grant out of the unread line (`Enchanted
  creature has`), so a residue regex over the lines cannot see the mechanic inside it; the select pool's pin is what
  finds such a card. Read the pool after every seam, not only the residue.
- **A REFERENT VERB LIST IS A GATE.** `REFERENT_OBJECT` lists the verbs whose object may be `it` / `that creature`; a
  verb missing from it leaves every compound sentence with that verb unread, however well its own rule reads. Check the
  list before calling a compound form a new seam.
- **A NEWER CONTROL EFFECT OUTLASTS THE OLDER ONE'S END.** Every control event that is not itself temporary must drop the
  until-end-of-turn revert on its permanent, or cleanup hands the permanent back over it.
- **TAKING WHAT IS ALREADY YOURS STILL SKIPS.** A permanent control change on a permanent p1 already holds through a
  threaten changes nothing in D393's executor, so the threaten's revert still fires at cleanup (CR 613.7 would keep it
  with p1 under the newer effect). Not this decision — a reportable.
- **A PLAYER TARGET TAKES THE SUBJECT'S INDEX.** In `Target player gains control of target X you control.` the player
  is the clause's `targetIndex` and the permanent its `otherTargetIndex` (D396's order); the self form has no other target.

## D533 — MONSTROSITY AND ADAPT: the keyword action, the monstrous mark, its head and condition (2026-09-25)

**12,307 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,293
(+14: fourteen rows — Nessian Asp, Fleetfeather Cockatrice, Ravenous Leucrocota, Ill-Tempered Cyclops, Gluttonous Cyclops, Fleecemane Lion, Sinuous Vermin, Chillerpillar, Skittering Crustacean, Keepsake Gorgon, Splitting Slime, Skitter Eel, Sauroform Hybrid, Aeromunculus; the probe diff is the 14, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,051 → **8,065**. The REFUSED ledger 2,780 → **2,828** (+48 / -0: no ledger reason named monstrosity or adapt; the family's residue came in under what blocks it - the counters-put head beside adapt (9), an X amount (7), a cost-reduction sentence on the activation (4), a compound head (2), a shortened-name head (1), and the row maker's own reason for the other 25). Fixtures 9,130 →
**9,144**. `scriptableToday` 1,927 → **1,933**; the ladder `[1933, 1948, 3243, 4705, 5839]`. Bot reach **5,049** from **393**.
The first NEW SUBSYSTEM on Opus 5.5 (the whole loop stays on Opus 5.5 since D532): a keyword action with a designation,
the head that watches the designation, and a static condition on it - renown's pattern (D340), a state field beside it.

### The measurement chose it — the biggest new mechanic, judged the immediate-yield way

D532's probe (`d532/next-yield-d533.json`) took only the mechanism out - the `Monstrosity N.` activation, a `When ~
becomes monstrous,` head (its payload judged), the goad sentence - and judged every other sentence as the vocab probe
judges one: monstrosity 41 touched and 9 read whole, plus the three or four `as long as ~ is monstrous` statics a
condition reader would add; goad 78 touched and 5 whole; coin flip 10 (D531's flip probe). Adapt, measured beside it,
read 4 on the activation alone - the same executor, so it rides this seam.

### The seam (`d533/patch533-engine.cjs`, `patch533-fuzz.cjs`; `monstrosity.test.ts` 4 proofs)

- **MONSTROSITY N (CR 701.37).** `Monstrosity 3.` reads as `monstrosity` (SELF_AIMED - the source): a permanent that is
  not monstrous gets N +1/+1 counters and `BecameMonstrous`; a monstrous one gets nothing, and the step says so.
  `Monstrosity X` (the activation's X) stays unread.
- **THE MONSTROUS MARK (701.37b).** `CardInstance.monstrous`, renown's shape (D340): set by `BecameMonstrous`, cleared
  with the other battlefield fields when the permanent leaves - a Nessian Asp bounced and replayed is a new object and
  can become monstrous again.
- **THE HEAD (701.37c).** `When ~ becomes monstrous, <payload>` is a trigger on `BecameMonstrous` for the permanent
  itself: Keepsake Gorgon's destroys on the first activation and never on the second (no second mark).
- **ADAPT N (CR 701.46).** `Adapt 2.` reads as `adapt` (SELF_AIMED): a source with no +1/+1 counters gets N; one with
  any gets nothing, and the step says so. No mark and no marker - its counters are D130's `CountersChanged`.
- **THE FUZZ.** `monstrosities` (the `BecameMonstrous` markers); Fleecemane Lion and Sinuous Vermin two a seat - the
  cheapest Monstrosity activations rowed; the floor on the counter (4 permanents became monstrous over the gate's 500 seeds - Fleecemane Lion and Sinuous Vermin two a seat; D398's this-turn floor at 2 + 4).

### The tooling (`patch533-tools.cjs`, `-b`)

`monstrosity` and `adapt` are assertable (the row's own permanent carries the counters from none; monstrosity the mark).
The `When ~ becomes monstrous` head joins the library; its FIRE is the row's own Monstrosity activation (paid and
activated; the suite's aim and settle follow it), and a row with the head but no activation is refused by name. The
condition reader takes `~ is monstrous`, staged by the same activation (the row maker hands the row's Monstrosity
activation to the stage) - and the conditional static's met-state P/T counts the counters that stage puts (the four
static suites read the printed base alone and failed at the first trial; `-b` added the delta beside D398's
`selfCounter` one).

### The wave — fourteen rows

Fourteen suites generated; ten landed first time and the four conditional statics after the generator counted the stage's counters. The whole-leftover row maker offered 19 rows of 18,792 once Monstrosity N, the monstrous mark, its head and condition and Adapt N were the engine's - fourteen beside the five perennial non-landers; fourteen taken. Five monstrous creatures on the activation alone (Nessian Asp, Fleetfeather Cockatrice,
Ravenous Leucrocota, Ill-Tempered Cyclops, Gluttonous Cyclops), four with the `as long as ~ is
monstrous` static (Fleecemane Lion, Sinuous Vermin, Chillerpillar, Skittering Crustacean), two with the becomes-monstrous
head (Keepsake Gorgon, Splitting Slime), and three adapters (Skitter Eel, Sauroform Hybrid, Aeromunculus). The ledger takes the family's residue (48) under the shape that blocks each card; the select pool stays 25.

### Traps

- **A STAGE LEAVES WHAT IT PUT.** A condition met by the row's own activation leaves that activation's effects on the
  card - here N +1/+1 counters beside the mark - and every assert after the stage must count them.
- **A HEAD ON A DESIGNATION FIRES ONCE PER OBJECT.** `When ~ becomes monstrous` rides the MARK, not the activation: a
  second activation on a monstrous permanent makes no marker and so no trigger - the proof reads both halves.
- **A NEW STATE FIELD GOES WHERE RENOWN'S DOES.** A per-permanent designation is a required `CardInstance` field set in
  both card constructors and cleared by `clearBattlefieldFields`, or a replayed permanent keeps a mark it no longer has.
- **RUN THE SPELL SUPPRESSION PINS BEFORE THE GATE** (D531, D532): batched over the 471 spell suites (about 90 s) - this
  decision's pass was clean.

## D534 — COIN FLIP: the flip off the game's RNG, its won and lost branches, the suite that finds each by seed (2026-09-25)

**12,317 of 31,692 Commander-legal cards now execute completely, up from 12,307
(+10: six rows — Viashino Sandswimmer, Scoria Wurm, Tavern Swindler, The Gold Saucer, Wild Wurm, Skyclaw Thrash — and four cards complete on the seam alone — Winter Sky, Molten Birth and both printings of Stitch in Time; the probe diff is the 10, nothing regressed).**
`SHIPPED_SCRIPTS` 8,065 → **8,071**. The REFUSED ledger 2,828 → **2,854** (+64 / -38: the thirty-eight entries D524 wrote with a coin flip beside the gate as their reason retired - the engine flips and gates on it now - and the family's residue came in under what blocks it: several flips (18), a flip by another player or by each player (3), and the row maker's own reason for the rest). Fixtures 9,144 →
**9,152**. `scriptableToday` 1,933 → **1,934**; the ladder `[1934, 1949, 3243, 4705, 5838]`. Bot reach **5,050** from **393**.
A new subsystem on Opus 5.5: the first effect whose outcome is the game's randomness, and the generated suites taught to
test a random branch without guessing it.

### The measurement chose it

D533's probe (`d533/next-yield-d534.json`, only the mechanism taken out): coin flip 70 touched and 12 reading whole once
`Flip a coin.` and the `If you win/lose the flip,` prefix were the engine's (3 spells), ahead of goad (6), initiative
(6 - it rides the Undercity dungeon) and the counters-put head (3).

### The seam (`d534/patch534-engine.cjs` + `-b`, `patch534-fuzz.cjs`; `coinFlip.test.ts` 3 proofs)

- **FLIP A COIN (CR 705).** `Flip a coin.` reads as `flipCoin` (the caster's flip): `rng.ts`'s `flipCoin` draws from the
  game's RNG and the draw rides the batch's `rngAfter`, so a replay flips the same coin (D147's rule - the proofs read
  the replay hash on every seed they try).
- **ONE EVENT, NOT TWO (`-b`).** The manual tool already had `CoinFlipped { player, heads }` (M5, with its view cue). The
  rules flip reuses it: the flipper calls heads (705.2 - a fixed call on a fair coin wins half the time), so the flip is
  WON on heads. The first patch had added a second `CoinFlipped` shape and a duplicate reducer case; `-b` took both out.
- **THE BRANCHES.** `If you win the flip, X.` / `If you lose the flip, Y.` are D523's gated clauses on two new
  conditions, `flipWon` / `flipLost` (activatedParse beside D527's `clashWon`), answered - like the clash - off the
  resolution itself: the `CoinFlipped` this resolution made, or the verdict its continuation carried when a clause
  between them asks (`StackObject.flip` / `EffectContinuation.flip`; the proof puts a scry between the flip and its
  lost branch). A board-condition evaluator never answers them (`activationConditions` returns false, and says the
  words `if you win the flip`).
- **THE FUZZ.** `rulesFlips` - the `CoinFlipped` markers not made by the manual tool's own `FlipCoin` intent, which the
  driver also submits; two Winter Skies a seat; the floor on the counter (35 rules coin flips over the gate's 500 seeds - Winter Sky two a seat; D398's this-turn floor at 0 + 4).

### The tooling (`patch534-tools.cjs` + `-b`) — a random branch tested without guessing it

A flip's verdict is the RNG's, so D524's way (stage the gate MET) cannot arm it. An ability whose clauses are gated on a
flip gets TWO tests, D371's branch shape (the payment's `declined` / `paid`): `flipWon` and `flipLost`. Each arms by SEED
- `armedFlip(which, won)` builds the game under `flip-1`, `flip-2`, ... until the fire's flip went its way (forty tries
find either verdict) - and asserts only its own branch's gated clauses (`flipLive`). `flipCoin` is assertable (the
marker with the branch's verdict). The row maker stages no flip gate and refuses a flip beside a payment prompt (four
tests on one ability). `-b`: an activation's separate `Pay N life` assert contradicted the payload's own life assert
when the won branch gained life (Tavern Swindler) - it is skipped when the branch's live clauses change p1's life.

### The wave — six rows

Six suites generated; five landed first time and Tavern Swindler after the cost assert read the branch. The whole-leftover row maker offered 11 rows of 18,778 once a flip and its won and lost branches were the engine's - six flip rows beside the five perennial non-landers; six taken. Viashino Sandswimmer (both branches), Scoria Wurm and Wild Wurm (the lost branch returns them),
Tavern Swindler and The Gold Saucer (the won branch gains or makes), Skyclaw Thrash (the won branch pumps the attacker).
The ledger retires D524's thirty-eight coin-flip reasons and takes the family's residue (64) under the shape that blocks each card; the select pool stays 25.

### Traps

- **LOOK FOR THE EVENT BEFORE ADDING ONE.** The coin flip's marker already existed for the manual tool; a second event
  with the same `t` made a union TypeScript caught only at the first use. Grep `types/events.ts` for the verb first.
- **A RANDOM BRANCH IS FOUND, NOT FORCED.** A suite cannot arm the RNG; it tries seeds until the branch it tests
  happened, and asserts that branch alone. Every future random mechanic (dice) takes the same path.
- **A COST ASSERT MUST READ THE BRANCH.** A payload that changes the same number the cost changes (life) asserts the
  total; a second, cost-only assert beside it is wrong in exactly the branch that pays out.
- **A MANUAL MARKER IS NOT A RULES MARKER.** The fuzz driver flips coins by hand too; a counter over `CoinFlipped` must
  exclude the `FlipCoin` intent's own events, or its floor proves nothing.
- **AN EXAMPLE OF "UNREAD" GOES STALE.** Two pins used `Flip a coin.` as their example of a sentence the vocabulary does
  not read (D344, D191); the die roll is their example now.
